nodes.label: Team flight code
nodes.summary: The team's ROS 2 programs that fly on the drone's Jetson computer: they take a photo every second, find the hiker (mannequin) and the tent in the photos, and tell the autopilot where to drop the payloads. In the simulator the very same code runs unchanged (./launcher.sh sim).

nodes.label: Simulator (Gazebo digital twin)
nodes.summary: Everything that pretends to be the real world: Gazebo draws the field and the drone, ArduCopter SITL is the autopilot, MAVProxy passes the MAVLink messages on, and the SIYI camera emulator answers like the real camera at 192.168.144.25. Started by simulation/scripts/demo.sh.

nodes.label: Ground station
nodes.summary: Mission Planner on the Windows laptop: the pilot's screen. The ASTRA plugin adds the drone camera, the mission phase and the target cards, using only what arrives over MAVLink.

nodes.label: Gazebo Harmonic
nodes.summary: The 3D world simulator (not our code). It draws the field, the hiker, the tent and the drone, and moves the drone the way real physics would.

nodes.label: ArduCopter SITL 4.6.3
nodes.summary: The real Pixhawk autopilot firmware, compiled to run on the laptop ("software in the loop"). It flies the mission exactly like the real drone would.

nodes.label: MAVProxy
nodes.summary: A small MAVLink relay (not our code). It takes the autopilot's messages from TCP 5760 and copies them to MAVROS (UDP 14552), the scripts (UDP 14550) and Mission Planner on Windows.

nodes.label: MAVROS
nodes.summary: The bridge between MAVLink (the autopilot's language) and ROS 2 topics and services (not our code).

nodes.label: Mission Planner
nodes.summary: The ground-station program on Windows (not our code). The pilot uploads the mission, arms and starts AUTO here; the ASTRA plugin runs inside it.

nodes.label: main
nodes.explain: The 'main' ROS 2 package holds the mission brain of the drone: src/main_controller.py (ROS node main_controller) and the three small helper files it imports (target_geolocation.py = drop-aiming math, processing_hold.py = when the 'wait for the detector' hover ends, timed_steps.py = waits that never freeze the node). It also holds THE flight launch file launch/tracker.launch.xml, which starts all six team nodes, and a bench tool (capture_detect_drop.py). It is an ament_cmake package; CMakeLists.txt installs the Python scripts.
nodes.how_it_fits: It is the last link of the chain camera -> detector -> brain -> autopilot. ArduPilot flies the survey on its own; main_controller listens to the detector on /image_detection, follows the mission through MAVROS (/mavros/mission/waypoints, /mavros/mission/reached), reads the mission landmarks from waypoint_manager's parameters, and at the end takes over: GUIDED hover, new target waypoints through /addWaypoint, AUTO, MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO drops on servo outputs 13 (tent) and 11 (person) through /mavros/cmd/command, then RTL. Every step is told to the ground station as STATUSTEXT on /mavros/statustext/send, and the Gazebo simulator reads those same texts to show the mission phase and to score the aim. ./launcher.sh starts it on the Jetson and, unchanged, in the simulator.

nodes.label: mapping
nodes.explain: Despite its name, this package's working part is the survey photo trigger: the program 'trigger' (ROS node 'mission_camera_trigger', file do_digi_cam_trigger.py) starts one photo request per second when the mission reaches its DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL item, and stops at waypoint buffer_wp. The program 'mapping' (mapping.py, a panorama stitcher) is broken and never launched.
nodes.how_it_fits: Started by main/launch/tracker.launch.xml. It listens to ArduPilot through MAVROS (/mavros/statustext/recv for 'Mission: 3 DigiCamCtrl', /mavros/mission/reached) and to waypoint_manager (its buffer_wp parameter, read with the service waypoint_manager/get_parameters and followed on /parameter_events). It talks to video_cam with /camera/trigger (std_msgs/Bool true, every second) and /camera/command ('capture_setup' each time DigiCamCtrl is reported, 'autofocus' every 5 s), and reports 'Camera trigger STARTED' / 'Camera trigger STOPPED' to Mission Planner on /mavros/statustext/send (the simulator's phase monitor reads those texts). mapping_output/ holds example stitched maps (jpg + jgw + report json) made by a GPS-based stitching tool that is not in this repo; README.md explains the parameters.

nodes.label: video_cam
nodes.explain: The team's driver for the SIYI gimbal camera (an ament_python ROS 2 package). Its one program, 'siyi' (ROS node 'siyi'), turns every photo request into one photo saved on the Jetson, named after the drone's GPS position, with a small JSON 'sidecar' file next to it. It talks to the camera directly: SIYI SDK commands over UDP port 37260 (shutter, zoom, focus, gimbal) and the camera's web server on port 82 (download the photo from the camera's SD card).
nodes.how_it_fits: Started by main/launch/tracker.launch.xml (from launcher.sh on the Jetson, or './launcher.sh sim' in the Gazebo twin). It listens to /camera/trigger (one per second from mapping's mission_camera_trigger; also the simulator panel's TAKE PHOTO button), /camera/command (lens and gimbal commands) and MAVROS's /mavros/global_position/global, /rel_alt and /compass_hdg. It writes photos into <ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos as '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' plus '<lat> , <lon>.json'; detection/new_od finds them there and main_controller reads the sidecars to aim the payload drops. It reports to Mission Planner with STATUSTEXT on /mavros/statustext/send (for example 'SUCCESS: Captured 2K image #12'), to scripts/watch_status.py and the simulator's demo panel on /camera/status, and also publishes /camera/disk_free_mb and the full photo on /image_raw (nobody listens to those two). In the simulator the camera address 192.168.144.25 is answered by siyi_emulator, which renders each photo in Gazebo, so this package runs unchanged. Every camera number lives in video_cam/config.py; HOW_OUR_CAMERA_WORKS.md explains the pipeline and siyi_documentations/ holds the vendor manuals.

nodes.label: siyi_emulator
nodes.explain: A pretend SIYI gimbal camera for the simulator. On the real drone a SIYI camera (ZR10 or A8 mini) sits at 192.168.144.25; the team's video_cam driver points it with SIYI SDK commands on UDP port 37260 and downloads each photo from its web server on TCP port 82. This package answers on the same address and ports with the same bytes, but moves a gimbal and takes the photos inside Gazebo, so video_cam runs unchanged with its default settings and gets real rendered pictures.
nodes.how_it_fits: It sits between the team stack and Gazebo. Team side: video_cam (ROS node 'siyi') sends SDK frames to 192.168.144.25:37260 (a loopback alias on this PC, added by simulation/setup/camera_ip_alias.sh or scripts/add_camera_ip.sh) and polls/downloads photos over HTTP port 82; each photo becomes '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' in mapping_photos for the detector. Gazebo side (gz-transport, no ROS bridge): gimbal joint targets on /sim/gimbal/yaw|roll|pitch/cmd_pos, the photo trigger /sim/camera/photo/trigger, and inputs /sim/gimbal/joint_states, /sim/drone/odometry and /sim/camera/photo/image from the iris_a8mini drone model (sim_models). ROS extras: /sim/camera/photo_info (one JSON per photo, read by sim_demo's score_run, demo_markers and truth_detector) and /sim/camera/emulator_state (2 Hz health). sim_bringup's sim.launch.py starts node 'siyi_emulator' with config/siyi_emulator.yaml plus camera_model, camera_ip, sd_card_dir ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<instance> and, from camera_max_zoom, max_zoom (demo.sh uses 1 = '--zoom survey'). The sim_plugins camera slot checks it with siyi_probe.py.

nodes.label: sim_bringup
nodes.explain: sim_bringup is the 'start button' of the simulator: its launch file sim.launch.py starts Gazebo, spawns the drone, starts ArduCopter SITL, MAVProxy, the SIYI camera emulator, the payload release node, the ROS-Gazebo bridge, RViz and the demo panel in the right order. It also holds the small command-line helpers the shell scripts in simulation/scripts use: mission_tool (upload, arm, start over MAVLink), phase_monitor (prints the mission phases), stack_check (waits until the team code is ready), photo_trigger (one photo), wait_then_exec, gz_follow and odom_tf. sim_paths.py is the one place that answers every 'which file / which port' question.
nodes.how_it_fits: It sits between the operator's scripts (demo.sh, start_sim.sh, fly_mission.sh) and every other simulator package: it reads world configs from sim_worlds, builds the drone file from sim_models, starts siyi_emulator and sim_demo, and wires ArduCopter SITL to MAVROS through MAVProxy UDP outputs 14550 (scripts/ground station), 14552 (MAVROS for ./launcher.sh sim) and 14553 (demo panel), plus a copy for Mission Planner on Windows. team_stack.launch.py runs the team's unchanged tracker.launch.xml with only the detector model path pointed at a file that exists on the laptop. The team code itself is never changed by this package.

nodes.label: simulation/scripts
nodes.explain: The simulator's command buttons for the terminal: one small bash script per job. demo.sh runs the whole search demo; start_sim.sh starts only the simulator; fly_mission.sh, upload_mission.sh and take_photo.sh do one ground-crew step each; status.sh looks, stop_sim.sh stops, start_over.sh resets a run; mission_planner.sh and mp_actions.sh connect to Mission Planner on Windows. Every script prints its own header with --help and loads the shared helpers in _common.sh.
nodes.how_it_fits: This is where people (and the Windows .bat files, the Docker containers and the Mission Planner plugin) enter the digital twin. The scripts do not fly anything themselves: they start 'ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py' (Gazebo, ArduCopter SITL, MAVProxy, the SIYI camera emulator), start the team's unchanged ./launcher.sh sim, and drive sim_bringup's tools (mission_tool speaks MAVLink to SITL through MAVProxy's UDP port 14550; stack_check and phase_monitor watch ROS 2; photo_trigger publishes /camera/trigger). Every process they start carries an ASTRA_SIM_SESSION tag so stop_sim.sh can stop exactly those. State goes to ~/.astra_sim/state, results to ~/.astra_sim/runs/<time>_<world>/.

nodes.label: mission_planner_plugin
nodes.explain: The ASTRA Mission Planner plugin: one C# source file, astra_gcs.cs, which Mission Planner compiles by itself when it starts.
nodes.how_it_fits: It replaces the old Qt demo panel: Mission Planner becomes the single ground-station screen for both the simulator and the real drone.

nodes.label: /image_detection
nodes.summary: One message per photo from the detector: what it found (person "0" or tent "1"), how sure it is, where in the photo, and the GPS of the photo.

nodes.label: /mavros/mission/reached
nodes.summary: MAVROS tells everyone which mission item the autopilot just reached.

nodes.label: /mavros/mission/waypoints
nodes.summary: The mission as the autopilot has it, sent by MAVROS.

nodes.label: /mavros/statustext/recv
nodes.summary: Text messages from the autopilot, such as "Mission: 3 DigiCamCtrl".

nodes.label: /mavros/statustext/send
nodes.summary: Text messages from the team code to the ground station (shown in Mission Planner).

nodes.label: /mavros/global_position/global
nodes.summary: The drone's GPS position (about once a second).

nodes.label: /parameter_events
nodes.summary: ROS 2 announces every changed parameter here; the team code watches the mission landmarks.

nodes.label: /camera/trigger
nodes.summary: "Take one photo now" (sent once a second during the survey).

nodes.label: /camera/command
nodes.summary: Lens and gimbal commands for the camera driver, such as capture_setup or autofocus.

nodes.label: main_controller.py
nodes.doc:
Mission controller: hold after the survey, aim at the targets, drop the payloads, go home.

main_controller.py -- PURPOSE: the mission "brain" that runs on the drone's Jetson (ROS node
main_controller). ArduPilot flies the survey mission by itself; this node watches it and takes
over at the end:
  1. SURVEY: it remembers the best "person" and the best "tent" the detector reports (new_od,
     topic /image_detection) and WHERE ON THE GROUND each one is (see "Drop aiming" below).
  2. PROCESSING: at the last survey waypoint it switches to GUIDED (hover) and waits until every
     photo has been checked by the detector (at most PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS).
  3. VISITING: it inserts one waypoint over each target (tent first, then person) right before
     the mission's RTL (service /addWaypoint of waypoint_manager), points the mission at the
     first one and switches back to AUTO.
  4. DROPPING: over each target it hovers (GUIDED) LOITER_SECONDS, opens that target's release
     servo for SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS (MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO), and flies on; after the last one it
     returns home (RTL).

Fixed in October 2026 (found in the Gazebo simulator):
  * Drop aiming: the target position is no longer the drone's GPS position when the photo was
    taken (that missed by 14-25 m), but the ground point under the CENTRE OF THE DETECTION BOX.
    video_cam writes a JSON "sidecar" next to every photo (height above home, heading, field of
    view, zoom, gimbal angles at the shutter) and target_geolocation.py projects the box centre
    onto the ground. A photo without a usable sidecar falls back to the old behaviour (its own
    position); a photo without GPS is ignored instead of sending the drone to lat/lon 0,0.
  * No crash on a slow parameter read: the mission indices from waypoint_manager are read with
    wp_sender.parameter.AsyncParameterReader (never blocks, keeps the old values and retries when
    a read fails). The old blocking read spun the executor inside a callback, timed out,
    returned None and killed this node (2 of 4 simulator runs).
  * Nothing sleeps inside a callback any more: the 4 s + 1 s before resuming AUTO, the 6 s
    loiter, the 3 s servo opening and the 6 s before RTL are one-shot timers
    (timed_steps.StepRunner), so the node keeps handling messages and service answers meanwhile.
    Same timings as before.

Fixed after the Task 2 review for the real drone (October 2026):
  * The processing hold always ends: a missing/unreadable photo folder used to make the check
    raise on every tick so the 90 s limit was never reached (processing_hold.py; timed with the
    monotonic clock).
  * NaN / infinity can no longer become a waypoint: non-finite GPS (photo name or sidecar), box
    centre, score or aiming parameter is rejected (target_geolocation.is_finite_number /
    valid_latlon), and every target is checked once more before /addWaypoint.

Parameters (ros2 run main main_controller.py --ros-args -p name:=value):
  aim_at_detection_box      true   false = old behaviour (fly to the photo's own position)
  default_camera_pitch_deg  -90.0  camera pitch when the camera did not report its attitude
  default_camera_hfov_deg   81.0   field of view when a sidecar has none
  target_ground_height_m    0.0    ground height under the targets above HOME (heights are
                                   measured from home)
  max_aim_offset_m          150.0  an aim point farther than this from the photo is not trusted
The four numbers accept whole numbers too (`-p target_ground_height_m:=3` as well as `:=3.0`; see
_number_parameter). How the photo is turned relative to the drone is video_cam's parameter
image_top_direction_deg; it arrives here inside each photo's sidecar.

Talks to: /image_detection (in), /mavros/mission/waypoints + /mavros/mission/reached (in),
/parameter_events + /waypoint_manager/get_parameters (mission indices), /addWaypoint (out),
/mavros/set_mode, /mavros/mission/set_current, /mavros/cmd/command, /mavros/statustext/send (out).
nodes.explain: The mission brain (ROS node main_controller). During the survey it remembers the best person and the best tent the detector reports and works out where on the ground each one is. At the last waypoint before RTL it hovers in GUIDED until every photo has a detector answer (at most 90 s), then inserts one waypoint over each target (tent first, then person) before RTL, flies there in AUTO, hovers 6 s over each, opens that target's release servo for 3 s, and finally sends the drone home (RTL).
nodes.how_it_fits: Inputs: /image_detection (interfaces/ImageResult from new_od, RELIABLE depth 10), /mavros/mission/waypoints and /mavros/mission/reached from MAVROS, and waypoint_manager's mission indices (read from /waypoint_manager/get_parameters whenever /parameter_events says they changed). Outputs: /addWaypoint (waypoint_manager), /mavros/mission/set_current, /mavros/set_mode (GUIDED / AUTO / RTL), /mavros/cmd/command (MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO 183: channel 13 tent, 11 person, 1400 us open, 500 us closed) and STATUSTEXT on /mavros/statustext/send. To aim it reads each photo's .json sidecar (written by video_cam) in <ws>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos. The simulator's phase monitor and scorer parse its STATUSTEXT texts, so their wording must not change. Target waypoints fly at ALT = 49 m above home (about 160 ft; the code comment '~55ft' is out of date).

nodes.label: Detection_Object
nodes.source:
class Detection_Object:
    def __init__(self, type, confidence, latitude, longitude):
        self.type = type          # person or tent
        self.confidence = confidence     
        # self.waypoint_index = waypoint_index # index > 0
        self.lat = latitude       # where we will fly to drop (the aim point)
        self.long = longitude
        self.image_name = ''      # photo it was seen in
        self.aim_note = ''        # how the aim point was computed (for the log)
nodes.explain: A small record for the best detection of one target class so far: type ('person' or 'tent'), confidence (0 = nothing found yet), lat / long (the AIM point the drone will fly to and drop on), image_name (the photo it was seen in) and aim_note (how the aim point was worked out, for the log).

nodes.label: MainController
nodes.source:
class MainController(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('main_controller')

        # Parameters of the drop aiming (see the module docstring).
        self.declare_parameter('aim_at_detection_box', True)
        self.aim_at_box = bool(self.get_parameter('aim_at_detection_box').value)
        self.default_pitch = self._number_parameter('default_camera_pitch_deg', -90.0)
        self.default_hfov = self._number_parameter('default_camera_hfov_deg', 81.0)
        self.ground_height = self._number_parameter('target_ground_height_m', 0.0)
        self.max_aim_offset = self._number_parameter('max_aim_offset_m', 150.0)

        # Subscribers
        detection_qos = QoSProfile(depth=10, reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.RELIABLE)
        self.create_subscription(ImageResult, "/image_detection", self.image_result_cb, detection_qos)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointList, "/mavros/mission/waypoints", self.waypoints_cb, 10)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointReached, "/mavros/mission/reached", self.update_waypoint_reached, 1)
        self.create_subscription(ParameterEvent, "/parameter_events", self.parameter_event_cb, 10)

        # Publishers
        self.status_publisher = self.create_publisher(StatusText, '/mavros/statustext/send', 10)

        # Clients
        self.set_mode_client = self.create_client(SetMode, "/mavros/set_mode")
        while not self.set_mode_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info(f"Set mode service not available, waiting ...")
        self.add_wp_client = self.create_client(AddWaypoint, "/addWaypoint")
        while not self.add_wp_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info(f"Waiting for add waypoint service ..s.")
        
        self.command_client = self.create_client(CommandLong, '/mavros/cmd/command')
        self.set_current_client = self.create_client(WaypointSetCurrent, "/mavros/mission/set_current")

        # variables
        self.num_waypoints = 0
        self.last_before_rtl = 0
        self.next_after_takeoff = 0
        self.takeoff_index = 0
        self.rtl_index = 0
        self.lap = 0
        self.waypoint_reached = 0
        self.human_wp = -1
        self.tent_wp = -1
        self.wait_to_send_wp = True # wait to send new waypoints until reaching last_before_rtl
        self.last_nav_before_rtl = -1  # last physical nav waypoint before RTL
        self.buffer_wp = -1            # NAV waypoint before trigger, for GUIDED hold
        self.processed_image_names = set()  # image filenames received via /image_detection
        self.waiting_for_processing = False  # True when in GUIDED waiting for processing
        self.auto_resumed = False      # set True after one-time AUTO resume; prevents re-triggering
        self.processing_check_timer = None
        self.processing_started_at = 0.0  # time.monotonic() when the GUIDED processing hold began
        self._photo_folder_error = ''     # last "cannot read the photo folder" reason logged
        self.mission_phase = "survey"   # survey -> processing -> visiting -> done
        self.visit_plan = []            # ordered targets to drop on (tent first, then person)
        self.visit_idx = 0              # how many targets dropped so far
        self.LOITER_SECONDS = 6.0       # loiter over each target + pre-RTL wait
        self.camera_feed_path = self._resolve_camera_feed_path()
        # Timed sequences (resume AUTO, loiter-and-drop) run here, on one-shot timers.
        self.steps = StepRunner(self)

        # Mission indices: read WITHOUT blocking, re-read on every waypoint_manager parameter
        # event; a failed read keeps the previous values and is retried (see the docstring).
        self.index_reader = AsyncParameterReader(
            self, 'waypoint_manager', MISSION_INDEX_PARAMS, self._on_mission_indices)
        self.index_reader.request('start-up')

        self.waypoints = []
        self.detections = {
            "person": Detection_Object(type="person", confidence=0, latitude=0.0, longitude=0.0),
            "tent": Detection_Object(type="tent", confidence=0, latitude=0.0, longitude=0.0)
        }

        while not self.command_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info("Waiting for command service ...")
        # Startup self-test: visibly actuate BOTH targets' servos every launch
        # so we can confirm they are alive before the mission starts.
        # self.get_logger().info("Startup: actuating all servos...")
        # self.actuate_servos(TENT_SERVO_CHANNELS)
        # self.actuate_servos(PERSON_SERVO_CHANNELS)
        # self.get_logger().info("Startup servo test complete.")  # startup servo test disabled

    def _number_parameter(self, name, default):
        """Declare a decimal parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

        ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value: with a plain 0.0 default,
        `-p target_ground_height_m:=3` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
        start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then nobody is left to drop. dynamic_typing
        accepts any type; a value that is not a number is reported and the default is used.
        NaN and infinity (`:=.nan`, `:=.inf`) are not numbers either (Task 2 review fix): a NaN
        ground height would have turned every aim point into NaN.
        """
        self.declare_parameter(name, default, ParameterDescriptor(dynamic_typing=True))
        value = self.get_parameter(name).value
        if (isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
                and math.isfinite(value)):
            return float(value)
        self.get_logger().error(
            f"Parameter {name}={value!r} is not a number: using the default {default:g}")
        return float(default)

    def fetch_mission_indices(self):
        """Ask for a fresh read of the mission indices (never blocks; see _on_mission_indices)."""
        self.index_reader.request('mission indices may have changed')
        
    def _on_mission_indices(self, values):
        """New mission indices from waypoint_manager (runs on this node's executor)."""
        new = {name: int(values[name]) for name in MISSION_INDEX_PARAMS}
        old = {'num_waypoints': self.num_waypoints, 'takeoff_index': self.takeoff_index,
               'rtl_index': self.rtl_index, 'next_after_takeoff': self.next_after_takeoff,
               'last_before_rtl': self.last_before_rtl}
        self.num_waypoints = new['num_waypoints']
        self.takeoff_index = new['takeoff_index']
        self.rtl_index = new['rtl_index']
        self.next_after_takeoff = new['next_after_takeoff']
        self.last_before_rtl = new['last_before_rtl']
        if new != old:
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Mission indices: takeoff={self.takeoff_index}, rtl={self.rtl_index}, "
                f"last_before_rtl={self.last_before_rtl} ({self.num_waypoints} items)")
        # The hold trigger depends on rtl_index: recompute it if the mission list is already here
        # (the list may have arrived before these values).
        self._update_last_nav_before_rtl()

    def parameter_event_cb(self, msg: ParameterEvent):
        if msg.node == "/waypoint_manager":
            for changed_param in msg.changed_parameters:
                name = changed_param.name
                value = changed_param.value

                if name in {"num_waypoints", "takeoff_index", "rtl_index", "next_after_takeoff", "last_before_rtl"}:
                    #self.get_logger().info(f"[Param Update] {name} changed")
                    self.fetch_mission_indices()
                    break
    
    def update_waypoint_reached(self, msg):
        self.waypoint_reached = msg.wp_seq      # latest waypoint index reached

        # Trigger = last physical NAV waypoint before RTL.
        trigger_wp = self.last_nav_before_rtl if self.last_nav_before_rtl >= 0 else self.last_before_rtl

        # PHASE survey -> processing: reached the last waypoint before RTL.
        # Hold in GUIDED (do NOT RTL) until EVERY captured image has been
        # processed by object detection; only then do we pick targets.
        if self.mission_phase == "survey" and self.waypoint_reached == trigger_wp:
            self.mission_phase = "processing"
            self.send_ack("Reached last WP. Holding to finish image processing before RTL")
            self.get_logger().info("Holding (GUIDED) at last WP; waiting for all images to be processed")
            self.change_mode("GUIDED")
            self.waiting_for_processing = True
            # Monotonic: the Jetson's wall clock can be stepped during a flight (network/GPS time).
            self.processing_started_at = time.monotonic()
            if self.processing_check_timer is None:
                self.processing_check_timer = self.create_timer(2.0, self._check_all_images_processed)
            return

        # PHASE visiting: arrive over each planned target in turn; loiter, drop.
        if self.mission_phase == "visiting" and self.visit_idx < len(self.visit_plan):
            if self.steps.busy:
                # A drop (or the resume) is still running: a repeated "reached" must not start
                # a second one (the old code was blocked in time.sleep here instead).
                return
            target = self.visit_plan[self.visit_idx]
            if self.waypoint_reached == target["wp"]:
                self._loiter_and_drop(target)

    def _divert_to_targets(self):
        """Run once, after all images are processed. Build the ordered target
        list (1 highest-confidence TENT first, then 1 highest-confidence PERSON;
        only those actually detected), inject a waypoint for each, fly to the
        first. If nothing was found, RTL straight away."""
        if self.mission_phase != "processing":
            return

        order = [
            ("tent",   TENT_SERVO_CHANNELS),
            ("person", PERSON_SERVO_CHANNELS),
        ]
        self.visit_plan = []
        for obj_type, servos in order:
            if self.valid_detection(obj_type):
                d = self.detections[obj_type]
                if not geo.valid_latlon(d.lat, d.long):
                    # Last check before a waypoint is made (Task 2 review): image_result_cb
                    # never stores such a point, so this only guards against future changes.
                    self.get_logger().error(
                        f"Target {obj_type}: aim point {d.lat}, {d.long} is not a valid "
                        f"position; no waypoint and no drop for it")
                    continue
                self.visit_plan.append({
                    "type": obj_type, "lat": d.lat, "lon": d.long, "alt": ALT,
                    "servos": servos, "wp": -1,
                })
                self.get_logger().info(
                    f"Target {obj_type}: conf {d.confidence:.2f} in '{d.image_name}', aim "
                    f"{d.lat:.7f}, {d.long:.7f} ({d.aim_note})")

        if not self.visit_plan:
            self.send_ack("No valid targets found. Returning to launch.")
            self.get_logger().info("No valid targets; commanding RTL")
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
            return

        # Mission indices in VISIT order: tent=base+1, person=base+2, ...
        base = self.last_before_rtl
        for i, t in enumerate(self.visit_plan):
            t["wp"] = base + 1 + i

        # waypoint_manager INSERTS at the index (pushing later items down), so to
        # land visit_plan[0] at base+1 we must insert the list in REVERSE order.
        inject = [{"lat": t["lat"], "lon": t["lon"], "alt": t["alt"], "index": base + 1}
                  for t in reversed(self.visit_plan)]
        self.send_waypoint_data(inject)

        # Where exactly we aim, for the ground station (fits the 50-character STATUSTEXT limit).
        for t in self.visit_plan:
            self.send_ack(f"Aim {t['type']} {t['lat']:.7f},{t['lon']:.7f}")
        names = " -> ".join(f"{t['type']}@{t['wp']}" for t in self.visit_plan)
        self.send_ack(f"Targets: {names}. Diverting.")
        self.get_logger().info(f"Visit plan: {names}")

        self.mission_phase = "visiting"
        self.visit_idx = 0
        self.last_before_rtl = -1
        # Point the vehicle at the first target and resume AUTO.
        self.divert_and_resume(self.visit_plan[0]["wp"])

    def _loiter_and_drop(self, target):
        """Over a target: loiter (GUIDED) LOITER_SECONDS, actuate its servo, then
        continue to the next target -- or wait LOITER_SECONDS and RTL if last.

        Runs as timed steps (never sleeps): loiter -> open -> SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS
        -> close -> next target (AUTO), or -> LOITER_SECONDS -> RTL after the last.
        """
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Arrived over {target['type']} (WP {target['wp']}). "
            f"Loitering {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s, then dropping.")
        self.send_ack(f"Over {target['type']}: loiter {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s then drop")
        self.change_mode("GUIDED")              # hold position above the target
        is_last = self.visit_idx + 1 >= len(self.visit_plan)

        def after_close():
            self.visit_idx += 1
            if not is_last:
                self.change_mode("AUTO")        # fly to the next target
            else:
                self.send_ack(f"All targets done. Waiting {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s then RTL.")

        def go_home():
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
            self.send_ack("RTL")

        servos = target["servos"]
        steps = [
            (self.LOITER_SECONDS, 'open release servo', lambda: self.open_servos(servos)),
            (SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS, 'close release servo', lambda: self.close_servos(servos)),
            (0.0, 'next target or wait', after_close),
        ]
        if is_last:
            steps.append((self.LOITER_SECONDS, 'RTL', go_home))   # final wait, then home
        self.steps.start(f"drop on the {target['type']}", steps)

    def valid_detection(self, type):
        if type in self.detections:
            if self.detections[type].confidence > 0:
                return True
        return False
        
    def waypoints_cb(self, msg: WaypointList):
        self.waypoints = msg.waypoints
        self._update_last_nav_before_rtl()

    def _update_last_nav_before_rtl(self):
        """Find the last actual NAV waypoint index before RTL, and the buffer
        waypoint (one NAV waypoint before that) used for GUIDED processing hold.
        DigiCamCtrl and other DO_ commands don't trigger WaypointReached,
        so we need the index of the last physical navigation waypoint."""
        NAV_COMMANDS = {16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22}  # NAV_WAYPOINT, NAV_LOITER_*, NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH, NAV_TAKEOFF
        previous = (self.last_nav_before_rtl, self.buffer_wp)
        self.last_nav_before_rtl = -1
        self.buffer_wp = -1
        if self.rtl_index > 0 and len(self.waypoints) > 0:
            found_last = False
            # The parameter can briefly describe an older mission while a new
            # WaypointList is arriving, so never index beyond the received list.
            for i in range(min(self.rtl_index, len(self.waypoints)) - 1, -1, -1):
                if self.waypoints[i].command in NAV_COMMANDS:
                    if not found_last:
                        self.last_nav_before_rtl = i
                        found_last = True
                    else:
                        self.buffer_wp = i
                        break
        if (self.last_nav_before_rtl, self.buffer_wp) == previous:
            return                       # unchanged: do not repeat the log lines
        if self.last_nav_before_rtl >= 0:
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Last nav WP before RTL: index {self.last_nav_before_rtl} "
                f"(last_before_rtl={self.last_before_rtl}, rtl={self.rtl_index})"
            )

        if self.buffer_wp >= 0:
            self.get_logger().info(f"Buffer WP (GUIDED processing hold): index {self.buffer_wp}")
    
    def _resolve_camera_feed_path(self):
        """Resolve camera_feed folder path."""
        current_file = os.path.abspath(__file__)
        search_dir = os.path.dirname(current_file)
        ros2_ws_dir = None
        for _ in range(10):
            if (os.path.exists(os.path.join(search_dir, "install")) and
                    os.path.exists(os.path.join(search_dir, "src"))):
                ros2_ws_dir = search_dir
                break
            parent = os.path.dirname(search_dir)
            if (os.path.exists(os.path.join(parent, "install")) and
                    os.path.exists(os.path.join(parent, "src"))):
                ros2_ws_dir = parent
                break
            search_dir = os.path.dirname(search_dir)
            if search_dir == "/":
                break
        if ros2_ws_dir and os.path.exists(os.path.join(ros2_ws_dir, "src")):
            ros2_ws_dir = os.path.join(ros2_ws_dir, "src")
        if ros2_ws_dir is None:
            ros2_ws_dir = "/astra/ros2_ws/src"
        path = os.path.join(ros2_ws_dir, "video_cam", "mapping_photos")
        return path

    def _check_all_images_processed(self):
        """Timer during the 'processing' hold: once every captured image has been
        processed by object detection, stop waiting and divert to the targets.

        The hold ALWAYS ends by PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (Task 2 review fix): a missing or
        unreadable photo folder used to raise inside the old try/except on every tick, so the
        timeout branch was never reached and the drone hovered until a failsafe. The listing
        and the decision are in processing_hold.py (never raise; unit-tested), and the hold is
        timed with the monotonic clock (a wall-clock jump cannot stretch it).
        """
        if self.mission_phase != "processing":
            if self.processing_check_timer:
                self.processing_check_timer.cancel()
                self.processing_check_timer = None
            return
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self.processing_started_at
        names, folder_error = hold.list_photo_names(self.camera_feed_path)
        decision = hold.decide(names, self.processed_image_names, elapsed,
                               PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)

        # Say once (and again only if the reason changes) that the folder cannot be read,
        # instead of the same error every 2 s.
        if folder_error != getattr(self, '_photo_folder_error', ''):
            self._photo_folder_error = folder_error
            if folder_error:
                self.get_logger().warn(
                    f"Cannot read the photo folder {self.camera_feed_path} ({folder_error}). "
                    f"Waiting for the detector until the {PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:.0f} s "
                    f"limit, then going on with the targets found so far.")
        if decision.folder_readable:
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Processing check: {decision.processed}/{decision.total} images done, "
                f"{decision.remaining} remaining")

        if decision.action == hold.WAIT:
            return
        if decision.action == hold.ALL_DONE:
            self.send_ack(f"All {decision.total} images processed. Selecting targets.")
        elif not decision.folder_readable:
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f"Processing timeout after {elapsed:.0f}s and the photo folder is unreadable "
                f"({folder_error}): diverting with the {len(self.processed_image_names)} "
                f"detector answer(s) received.")
            # <= 50 characters (MAVLink STATUSTEXT) and starts like the other timeout text, which
            # the simulator's phase monitor recognises ("Processing timeout" ... "images").
            self.send_ack("Processing timeout: images unreadable. Diverting.")
        else:
            # Divert with whatever finished rather than loiter indefinitely.
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f"Processing timeout after {elapsed:.0f}s: {decision.processed}/{decision.total} "
                f"done, {decision.remaining} never processed. Diverting anyway.")
            self.send_ack(
                f"Processing timeout ({decision.processed}/{decision.total}). Diverting anyway.")
        self._end_processing_hold()

    def _end_processing_hold(self):
        """Stop the processing hold for good and divert (or RTL when nothing was found)."""
        if self.processing_check_timer:
            self.processing_check_timer.cancel()
            self.processing_check_timer = None
        self.waiting_for_processing = False
        try:
            self._divert_to_targets()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a bug here must not leave the drone hovering
            # The check timer is already gone, so without this the drone would hover in GUIDED
            # until a failsafe. Going home is the safe end of the mission.
            self.get_logger().error(f"Divert failed ({e}); commanding RTL")
            self.send_ack("Divert failed. Returning to launch.")
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")

    def get_waypoint(self, waypoint_index):     # return copy of an old waypoint given index
        if 0 <= waypoint_index < len(self.waypoints):
            wp = self.waypoints[waypoint_index]
            lat = wp.x_lat
            lon = wp.y_long
            alt = wp.z_alt
            return lat, lon, alt
        else:
            self.get_logger().warn(f"Waypoint index {waypoint_index} out of range")
            return None

    def locate_detection(self, msg, detection):
        """Where to drop for one detection box: (AimResult, '') or (None, why it is ignored).

        Uses the photo's sidecar (written by video_cam at the shutter) to project the box centre
        onto the ground (target_geolocation.aim_at_box). Falls back to the photo's own position
        when that is not possible, exactly like the old code did for every detection. Returns
        no aim point when the photo has no usable GPS position (missing, (0, 0), NaN/inf, out of
        range) or the box centre is not a finite number (Task 2 review fix): such a detection
        must never become a waypoint or a drop.
        """
        image_path = os.path.join(self.camera_feed_path, msg.image_name or '')
        meta = geo.read_photo_sidecar(image_path) if msg.image_name else None
        # Prefer the exact numbers: the sidecar's float64 fix, else the 6-decimal file name, and
        # only last the float32 copy in the message (0.4-0.7 m rounding).
        name_lat, name_lon = self._latlon_from_name(msg.image_name)
        if name_lat is None:
            name_lat, name_lon = float(msg.latitude), float(msg.longitude)
        position = geo.photo_position(meta, name_lat, name_lon)
        if position is None:
            return None, 'the photo has no usable GPS position'
        photo_lat, photo_lon = position
        u = float(detection.bbox.center.position.x)
        v = float(detection.bbox.center.position.y)
        if not geo.is_finite_number(u, v):
            # Checked even when aiming is off: a box that is not a number is a broken detection.
            return None, f'the box centre ({u}, {v}) is not a finite number'
        if not self.aim_at_box:
            return geo.AimResult(photo_lat, photo_lon, 'photo',
                                 note='photo position (aim_at_detection_box is false)'), ''
        aim = geo.aim_at_box(meta, photo_lat, photo_lon, u, v, geo.jpeg_size(image_path),
                             default_pitch_deg=self.default_pitch,
                             default_hfov_deg=self.default_hfov,
                             ground_height_m=self.ground_height,
                             max_offset_m=self.max_aim_offset)
        if aim is None:
            return None, 'no usable aim point'
        return aim, ''

    @staticmethod
    def _latlon_from_name(image_name):
        """(lat, lon) from a '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' photo name (same rule as detection/geotag.py)."""
        stem = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(image_name or ''))[0]
        if ' , ' not in stem:
            return None, None
        lat_s, lon_s = stem.split(' , ', 1)
        try:
            return float(lat_s), float(lon_s)
        except ValueError:
            return None, None

    def image_result_cb(self, msg):
         # Track all processed image names for processing completion check
        if msg.image_name:
            self.processed_image_names.add(msg.image_name)

        if msg.detections.detections:
            self.get_logger().info(f"{len(msg.detections.detections)} object(s) detected!")
            
            #self.get_logger().info(f"{msg}")
            for detection in msg.detections.detections:
                for result in detection.results:
                    obj_id = result.hypothesis.class_id
                    obj_class = {"0": "person", "1": "tent"}.get(obj_id)
                    if obj_class is None:
                        # Ignore classes that are not actionable mission targets.
                        continue
                    obj_conf = result.hypothesis.score
                    if not geo.is_finite_number(obj_conf):
                        # An infinite score would win every comparison and lock in this box
                        # for good; NaN never wins but is still a broken result.
                        self.get_logger().warn(
                            f"Ignoring {obj_class} in '{msg.image_name}': its score "
                            f"{obj_conf} is not a finite number")
                        continue

                    if obj_class in self.detections:        # only works if obj_class is saved as 'person' or 'tent'    // TODO: DOUBLE CHECK THIS
                        if obj_conf > self.detections[obj_class].confidence:        # get highest conf
                            aim, why = self.locate_detection(msg, detection)
                            if aim is None:
                                # Nowhere safe to fly to (no/NaN GPS, broken box). The old code
                                # stored 0,0 and would have sent the drone there.
                                self.get_logger().warn(
                                    f"Ignoring {obj_class} ({obj_conf:.2f}) in "
                                    f"'{msg.image_name}': {why}")
                                continue
                            self.get_logger().info(f"Updating {obj_class}: old_conf={self.detections[obj_class].confidence:.2f}, new_conf={obj_conf:.2f}")
                            self.send_ack(f"Detected {obj_class}")
                            # self.move_servo(11,1400)   # debug: fired on every new best detection
                            # self.move_servo(11,500)
                            # update conf
                            self.detections[obj_class].confidence = obj_conf
                            # update wp_index
                            # self.detections[obj_class].waypoint_index = msg.waypoint_index
                            self.detections[obj_class].lat = aim.lat
                            self.detections[obj_class].long = aim.lon
                            self.detections[obj_class].image_name = msg.image_name
                            self.detections[obj_class].aim_note = aim.note
                            self.get_logger().info(f"Obj at long: {self.detections[obj_class].long}, lat: {self.detections[obj_class].lat}")
                            self.get_logger().info(f"  aimed at the {aim.note}")
        else:
            self.get_logger().info("No objects detected.")
            self.send_ack("No objects detected.")

    def change_mode(self, mode):
        # set_mode service should already be ready from self._wait_for_services
        self.get_logger().info(f"Setting mode to {mode}...")
        try:
            req = SetMode.Request()
            req.custom_mode = mode
            # Fire-and-forget: never block (this runs inside a subscription
            # callback under a single-threaded executor — spinning here deadlocks).
            future = self.set_mode_client.call_async(req)
            future.add_done_callback(lambda f, m=mode: self._on_mode_result(f, m))
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(str(e))

    def _on_mode_result(self, future, mode):
        try:
            response = future.result()
            if response is not None and response.mode_sent:
                self.get_logger().info(f"Mode changed to {mode}")
            else:
                self.get_logger().error(f"Failed to change mode to {mode}")
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"set_mode result error: {e}")

    def send_waypoint_data(self, wp_list):
        # AddWaypoint is scalar (one waypoint per call); send one request each.
        self.get_logger().info(f"Sending {len(wp_list)} waypoints")

        for i, wp in enumerate(wp_list):
            try:
                req = AddWaypoint.Request()
                req.command = 16  # NAV_WAYPOINT
                req.latitude = float(wp["lat"])
                req.longitude = float(wp["lon"])
                req.altitude = float(wp["alt"])
                req.index = int(wp["index"])
                req.channel = 0
                req.pwm = 0

                self.get_logger().info(
                    f"Waypoint {i + 1}: lat={wp['lat']}, lon={wp['lon']}, "
                    f"alt={wp['alt']}, index={wp['index']}"
                )

                self.add_wp_client.call_async(req)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().error(f"Error sending waypoint {i + 1}: {str(e)}")
    
    def set_current_wp(self, seq):
        try:
            req = WaypointSetCurrent.Request()
            req.wp_seq = int(seq)
            self.set_current_client.call_async(req)
            self.get_logger().info(f"Set current waypoint -> {seq}")
            self.send_ack(f"Set current WP -> {seq}")
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"set_current failed: {e}")

    def divert_and_resume(self, target_seq):
        # Let the full-mission push land on the FCU, then point the vehicle at
        # the first divert waypoint and resume AUTO so it flies there instead of
        # continuing the RTL. Timed steps, never sleeps: the node keeps handling
        # the /addWaypoint answers and parameter events meanwhile.
        if target_seq is None or target_seq < 0:
            return

        def resume():
            self.change_mode("AUTO")
            self.send_ack(f"Resumed AUTO -> WP {target_seq}")

        self.steps.start('resume AUTO', [
            (PUSH_SETTLE_SECONDS, 'set current waypoint', lambda: self.set_current_wp(target_seq)),
            (SET_CURRENT_TO_AUTO_SECONDS, 'resume AUTO', resume),
        ])

    def open_servos(self, channels):
        """Open the given release servos (all together)."""
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Opening servos {channels} for {SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS:.0f}s")
        for ch in channels:
            self.move_servo(ch, PULLEY_OPEN)

    def close_servos(self, channels):
        """Close the given release servos (all together)."""
        for ch in channels:
            self.move_servo(ch, PULLEY_CLOSE)

    def actuate_servos(self, channels):
        """Open the given release servos, hold OPEN for SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS,
        then close them back. All servos open together and close together.
        Never blocks: the close is a one-shot timer."""
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Opening servos {channels} -> hold {SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS:.0f}s -> close")
        self.open_servos(channels)
        call_later(self, SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS, lambda: self.close_servos(channels))

    def move_servo(self, channel, pwm):
        try:
            # Sending request to move servo
            request = CommandLong.Request()
            request.broadcast = False
            request.command = 183  # MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO
            request.confirmation = 0
            request.param1 = float(channel)
            request.param2 = float(pwm)
            request.param3 = float(0)
            request.param4 = float(0)
            request.param5 = float(0)
            request.param6 = float(0)
            request.param7 = float(0)

            # Fire-and-forget: do NOT spin here. This runs inside a subscription
            # callback under a single-threaded executor, so spin_until_future_complete
            # would deadlock the node. call_async already puts the command on the wire.
            future = self.command_client.call_async(request)
            future.add_done_callback(lambda f, c=channel, p=pwm: self._on_servo_result(f, c, p))

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Service call failed: {e}")

    def _on_servo_result(self, future, channel, pwm):
        try:
            response = future.result()
            if response is not None and response.success:
                self.get_logger().info(f"[SERVO] Channel {channel} moved to {pwm}us")
                self.send_ack(f"Servo {channel} -> {pwm}")
            else:
                self.get_logger().warn(f"[SERVO] Failed to move channel {channel}")
                self.send_ack(f"Servo {channel} move FAILED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Servo result error: {e}")

    def send_ack(self, text):
        msg = StatusText()
        msg.severity = 6  # INFO
        msg.text = text
        self.status_publisher.publish(msg)
        self.get_logger().info(f"Status: {text}")
nodes.explain: The ROS 2 node class 'main_controller', the mission brain. It moves through four phases kept in mission_phase: survey -> processing (GUIDED hover until the photos are checked) -> visiting (fly to and drop on each target) -> done.
