nodes.source:
def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('main_controller')

        # Parameters of the drop aiming (see the module docstring).
        self.declare_parameter('aim_at_detection_box', True)
        self.aim_at_box = bool(self.get_parameter('aim_at_detection_box').value)
        self.default_pitch = self._number_parameter('default_camera_pitch_deg', -90.0)
        self.default_hfov = self._number_parameter('default_camera_hfov_deg', 81.0)
        self.ground_height = self._number_parameter('target_ground_height_m', 0.0)
        self.max_aim_offset = self._number_parameter('max_aim_offset_m', 150.0)

        # Subscribers
        detection_qos = QoSProfile(depth=10, reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.RELIABLE)
        self.create_subscription(ImageResult, "/image_detection", self.image_result_cb, detection_qos)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointList, "/mavros/mission/waypoints", self.waypoints_cb, 10)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointReached, "/mavros/mission/reached", self.update_waypoint_reached, 1)
        self.create_subscription(ParameterEvent, "/parameter_events", self.parameter_event_cb, 10)

        # Publishers
        self.status_publisher = self.create_publisher(StatusText, '/mavros/statustext/send', 10)

        # Clients
        self.set_mode_client = self.create_client(SetMode, "/mavros/set_mode")
        while not self.set_mode_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info(f"Set mode service not available, waiting ...")
        self.add_wp_client = self.create_client(AddWaypoint, "/addWaypoint")
        while not self.add_wp_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info(f"Waiting for add waypoint service ..s.")
        
        self.command_client = self.create_client(CommandLong, '/mavros/cmd/command')
        self.set_current_client = self.create_client(WaypointSetCurrent, "/mavros/mission/set_current")

        # variables
        self.num_waypoints = 0
        self.last_before_rtl = 0
        self.next_after_takeoff = 0
        self.takeoff_index = 0
        self.rtl_index = 0
        self.lap = 0
        self.waypoint_reached = 0
        self.human_wp = -1
        self.tent_wp = -1
        self.wait_to_send_wp = True # wait to send new waypoints until reaching last_before_rtl
        self.last_nav_before_rtl = -1  # last physical nav waypoint before RTL
        self.buffer_wp = -1            # NAV waypoint before trigger, for GUIDED hold
        self.processed_image_names = set()  # image filenames received via /image_detection
        self.waiting_for_processing = False  # True when in GUIDED waiting for processing
        self.auto_resumed = False      # set True after one-time AUTO resume; prevents re-triggering
        self.processing_check_timer = None
        self.processing_started_at = 0.0  # time.monotonic() when the GUIDED processing hold began
        self._photo_folder_error = ''     # last "cannot read the photo folder" reason logged
        self.mission_phase = "survey"   # survey -> processing -> visiting -> done
        self.visit_plan = []            # ordered targets to drop on (tent first, then person)
        self.visit_idx = 0              # how many targets dropped so far
        self.LOITER_SECONDS = 6.0       # loiter over each target + pre-RTL wait
        self.camera_feed_path = self._resolve_camera_feed_path()
        # Timed sequences (resume AUTO, loiter-and-drop) run here, on one-shot timers.
        self.steps = StepRunner(self)

        # Mission indices: read WITHOUT blocking, re-read on every waypoint_manager parameter
        # event; a failed read keeps the previous values and is retried (see the docstring).
        self.index_reader = AsyncParameterReader(
            self, 'waypoint_manager', MISSION_INDEX_PARAMS, self._on_mission_indices)
        self.index_reader.request('start-up')

        self.waypoints = []
        self.detections = {
            "person": Detection_Object(type="person", confidence=0, latitude=0.0, longitude=0.0),
            "tent": Detection_Object(type="tent", confidence=0, latitude=0.0, longitude=0.0)
        }

        while not self.command_client.wait_for_service(timeout_sec=1.0):
            self.get_logger().info("Waiting for command service ...")
nodes.explain: Builds the node: declares the 5 aiming parameters (aim_at_detection_box true, default_camera_pitch_deg -90, default_camera_hfov_deg 81, target_ground_height_m 0, max_aim_offset_m 150), subscribes to /image_detection (RELIABLE depth 10), /mavros/mission/waypoints, /mavros/mission/reached and /parameter_events, creates the /mavros/statustext/send publisher and the service clients, finds the photo folder, and starts the non-blocking read of waypoint_manager's mission indices.
nodes.called_when: Once, when the script starts (bottom of the file: rclpy.init, MainController(), rclpy.spin).
nodes.effects: Waits (1 s per try, a log line each time, no time limit) until /mavros/set_mode, /addWaypoint and /mavros/cmd/command exist, so the node only starts working once MAVROS and waypoint_manager are up. Sends a GetParameters request to /waypoint_manager/get_parameters as soon as that service is ready.

nodes.label: _number_parameter
nodes.doc:
Declare a decimal parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value: with a plain 0.0 default,
`-p target_ground_height_m:=3` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then nobody is left to drop. dynamic_typing
accepts any type; a value that is not a number is reported and the default is used.
NaN and infinity (`:=.nan`, `:=.inf`) are not numbers either (Task 2 review fix): a NaN
ground height would have turned every aim point into NaN.
nodes.source:
def _number_parameter(self, name, default):
        """Declare a decimal parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

        ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value: with a plain 0.0 default,
        `-p target_ground_height_m:=3` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
        start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then nobody is left to drop. dynamic_typing
        accepts any type; a value that is not a number is reported and the default is used.
        NaN and infinity (`:=.nan`, `:=.inf`) are not numbers either (Task 2 review fix): a NaN
        ground height would have turned every aim point into NaN.
        """
        self.declare_parameter(name, default, ParameterDescriptor(dynamic_typing=True))
        value = self.get_parameter(name).value
        if (isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
                and math.isfinite(value)):
            return float(value)
        self.get_logger().error(
            f"Parameter {name}={value!r} is not a number: using the default {default:g}")
        return float(default)
nodes.explain: Declares one decimal ROS parameter that also accepts a whole number (dynamic typing) and returns it as a float. If the value is not a real, finite number (true, a typo, .nan, .inf) it logs 'Parameter <name>=<value> is not a number: using the default <default>' and returns the default.
nodes.called_when: In __init__, for default_camera_pitch_deg, default_camera_hfov_deg, target_ground_height_m and max_aim_offset_m.
nodes.inputs: name and default (for example 'target_ground_height_m', 0.0); the value comes from '--ros-args -p name:=value'.

nodes.label: fetch_mission_indices
nodes.doc: Ask for a fresh read of the mission indices (never blocks; see _on_mission_indices).
nodes.explain: Asks the AsyncParameterReader for a fresh read of the mission indices (reason 'mission indices may have changed'). It returns at once; the answer arrives later in _on_mission_indices.
nodes.called_when: From parameter_event_cb, when waypoint_manager says one of the index parameters changed.

nodes.label: _on_mission_indices
nodes.doc: New mission indices from waypoint_manager (runs on this node's executor).
nodes.source:
def _on_mission_indices(self, values):
        """New mission indices from waypoint_manager (runs on this node's executor)."""
        new = {name: int(values[name]) for name in MISSION_INDEX_PARAMS}
        old = {'num_waypoints': self.num_waypoints, 'takeoff_index': self.takeoff_index,
               'rtl_index': self.rtl_index, 'next_after_takeoff': self.next_after_takeoff,
               'last_before_rtl': self.last_before_rtl}
        self.num_waypoints = new['num_waypoints']
        self.takeoff_index = new['takeoff_index']
        self.rtl_index = new['rtl_index']
        self.next_after_takeoff = new['next_after_takeoff']
        self.last_before_rtl = new['last_before_rtl']
        if new != old:
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Mission indices: takeoff={self.takeoff_index}, rtl={self.rtl_index}, "
                f"last_before_rtl={self.last_before_rtl} ({self.num_waypoints} items)")
        # The hold trigger depends on rtl_index: recompute it if the mission list is already here
        # (the list may have arrived before these values).
        self._update_last_nav_before_rtl()
nodes.explain: Stores the five mission indices waypoint_manager publishes (num_waypoints, takeoff_index, rtl_index, next_after_takeoff, last_before_rtl) as whole numbers, logs 'Mission indices: takeoff=..., rtl=..., last_before_rtl=... (N items)' when they changed, and recomputes the hold waypoint.
nodes.called_when: By AsyncParameterReader, on this node's executor, after every successful read (start-up and after each parameter event).
nodes.inputs: values: a dict {parameter name: value}.

nodes.label: parameter_event_cb
nodes.explain: Watches the ROS-wide /parameter_events topic. When an event comes from /waypoint_manager and one of its changed parameters is num_waypoints, takeoff_index, rtl_index, next_after_takeoff or last_before_rtl, it asks for a fresh read (once per event).
nodes.called_when: On every /parameter_events message (any node's parameter changes).
nodes.inputs: msg: rcl_interfaces/ParameterEvent.

nodes.label: update_waypoint_reached
nodes.source:
def update_waypoint_reached(self, msg):
        self.waypoint_reached = msg.wp_seq      # latest waypoint index reached

        # Trigger = last physical NAV waypoint before RTL.
        trigger_wp = self.last_nav_before_rtl if self.last_nav_before_rtl >= 0 else self.last_before_rtl

        # PHASE survey -> processing: reached the last waypoint before RTL.
        # Hold in GUIDED (do NOT RTL) until EVERY captured image has been
        # processed by object detection; only then do we pick targets.
        if self.mission_phase == "survey" and self.waypoint_reached == trigger_wp:
            self.mission_phase = "processing"
            self.send_ack("Reached last WP. Holding to finish image processing before RTL")
            self.get_logger().info("Holding (GUIDED) at last WP; waiting for all images to be processed")
            self.change_mode("GUIDED")
            self.waiting_for_processing = True
            # Monotonic: the Jetson's wall clock can be stepped during a flight (network/GPS time).
            self.processing_started_at = time.monotonic()
            if self.processing_check_timer is None:
                self.processing_check_timer = self.create_timer(2.0, self._check_all_images_processed)
            return

        # PHASE visiting: arrive over each planned target in turn; loiter, drop.
        if self.mission_phase == "visiting" and self.visit_idx < len(self.visit_plan):
            if self.steps.busy:
                # A drop (or the resume) is still running: a repeated "reached" must not start
                # a second one (the old code was blocked in time.sleep here instead).
                return
            target = self.visit_plan[self.visit_idx]
            if self.waypoint_reached == target["wp"]:
                self._loiter_and_drop(target)
nodes.explain: Reacts to 'reached mission item N' from the autopilot. In the survey phase, reaching the last NAV waypoint before RTL (the hold point; runway example: item 10) starts the processing hold: STATUSTEXT 'Reached last WP. Holding to finish image processing before RTL', GUIDED mode, and a 2 s check timer. In the visiting phase, reaching the current target's waypoint starts the loiter-and-drop sequence, unless a timed sequence is still running.
nodes.called_when: On every /mavros/mission/reached message (wp_seq = mission index; DO_ items never produce one).
nodes.inputs: msg: mavros_msgs/WaypointReached.
nodes.effects: Mode change to GUIDED through /mavros/set_mode; STATUSTEXT (this one is longer than MAVLink's 50 characters, so the ground station sees it cut short).

nodes.label: _divert_to_targets
nodes.doc:
Run once, after all images are processed. Build the ordered target
list (1 highest-confidence TENT first, then 1 highest-confidence PERSON;
only those actually detected), inject a waypoint for each, fly to the
first. If nothing was found, RTL straight away.
nodes.source:
def _divert_to_targets(self):
        """Run once, after all images are processed. Build the ordered target
        list (1 highest-confidence TENT first, then 1 highest-confidence PERSON;
        only those actually detected), inject a waypoint for each, fly to the
        first. If nothing was found, RTL straight away."""
        if self.mission_phase != "processing":
            return

        order = [
            ("tent",   TENT_SERVO_CHANNELS),
            ("person", PERSON_SERVO_CHANNELS),
        ]
        self.visit_plan = []
        for obj_type, servos in order:
            if self.valid_detection(obj_type):
                d = self.detections[obj_type]
                if not geo.valid_latlon(d.lat, d.long):
                    # Last check before a waypoint is made (Task 2 review): image_result_cb
                    # never stores such a point, so this only guards against future changes.
                    self.get_logger().error(
                        f"Target {obj_type}: aim point {d.lat}, {d.long} is not a valid "
                        f"position; no waypoint and no drop for it")
                    continue
                self.visit_plan.append({
                    "type": obj_type, "lat": d.lat, "lon": d.long, "alt": ALT,
                    "servos": servos, "wp": -1,
                })
                self.get_logger().info(
                    f"Target {obj_type}: conf {d.confidence:.2f} in '{d.image_name}', aim "
                    f"{d.lat:.7f}, {d.long:.7f} ({d.aim_note})")

        if not self.visit_plan:
            self.send_ack("No valid targets found. Returning to launch.")
            self.get_logger().info("No valid targets; commanding RTL")
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
            return

        # Mission indices in VISIT order: tent=base+1, person=base+2, ...
        base = self.last_before_rtl
        for i, t in enumerate(self.visit_plan):
            t["wp"] = base + 1 + i

        # waypoint_manager INSERTS at the index (pushing later items down), so to
        # land visit_plan[0] at base+1 we must insert the list in REVERSE order.
        inject = [{"lat": t["lat"], "lon": t["lon"], "alt": t["alt"], "index": base + 1}
                  for t in reversed(self.visit_plan)]
        self.send_waypoint_data(inject)

        # Where exactly we aim, for the ground station (fits the 50-character STATUSTEXT limit).
        for t in self.visit_plan:
            self.send_ack(f"Aim {t['type']} {t['lat']:.7f},{t['lon']:.7f}")
        names = " -> ".join(f"{t['type']}@{t['wp']}" for t in self.visit_plan)
        self.send_ack(f"Targets: {names}. Diverting.")
        self.get_logger().info(f"Visit plan: {names}")

        self.mission_phase = "visiting"
        self.visit_idx = 0
        self.last_before_rtl = -1
        # Point the vehicle at the first target and resume AUTO.
        self.divert_and_resume(self.visit_plan[0]["wp"])
nodes.explain: Runs once when the hold ends and plans the visits: the best tent first, then the best person (only classes found with confidence above 0 and a valid aim point). With nothing found it sends 'No valid targets found. Returning to launch.' and RTL. Otherwise it gives the targets mission indices last_before_rtl + 1, + 2 (runway: tent@11, person@12), asks waypoint_manager to insert them (in reverse order, each at last_before_rtl + 1, so they end up in visit order), sends 'Aim <type> <lat>,<lon>' per target and 'Targets: tent@11 -> person@12. Diverting.', and starts the 'resume AUTO' sequence toward the first target.
nodes.called_when: From _end_processing_hold (all photos answered, or 90 s passed).
nodes.effects: /addWaypoint calls (altitude ALT = 49 m above home), STATUSTEXT, mission_phase becomes 'visiting' (or 'done' plus RTL).

nodes.label: _loiter_and_drop
nodes.doc:
Over a target: loiter (GUIDED) LOITER_SECONDS, actuate its servo, then
continue to the next target -- or wait LOITER_SECONDS and RTL if last.

Runs as timed steps (never sleeps): loiter -> open -> SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS
-> close -> next target (AUTO), or -> LOITER_SECONDS -> RTL after the last.
nodes.source:
def _loiter_and_drop(self, target):
        """Over a target: loiter (GUIDED) LOITER_SECONDS, actuate its servo, then
        continue to the next target -- or wait LOITER_SECONDS and RTL if last.

        Runs as timed steps (never sleeps): loiter -> open -> SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS
        -> close -> next target (AUTO), or -> LOITER_SECONDS -> RTL after the last.
        """
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Arrived over {target['type']} (WP {target['wp']}). "
            f"Loitering {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s, then dropping.")
        self.send_ack(f"Over {target['type']}: loiter {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s then drop")
        self.change_mode("GUIDED")              # hold position above the target
        is_last = self.visit_idx + 1 >= len(self.visit_plan)

        def after_close():
            self.visit_idx += 1
            if not is_last:
                self.change_mode("AUTO")        # fly to the next target
            else:
                self.send_ack(f"All targets done. Waiting {self.LOITER_SECONDS:.0f}s then RTL.")

        def go_home():
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
            self.send_ack("RTL")

        servos = target["servos"]
        steps = [
            (self.LOITER_SECONDS, 'open release servo', lambda: self.open_servos(servos)),
            (SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS, 'close release servo', lambda: self.close_servos(servos)),
            (0.0, 'next target or wait', after_close),
        ]
        if is_last:
            steps.append((self.LOITER_SECONDS, 'RTL', go_home))   # final wait, then home
        self.steps.start(f"drop on the {target['type']}", steps)
nodes.explain: Runs the drop over one target without blocking: STATUSTEXT 'Over <type>: loiter 6s then drop' and GUIDED (hover), then a timed sequence: after 6 s open the target's release servo (1400 us), after 3 s close it (500 us), then fly on in AUTO to the next target. After the last target it says 'All targets done. Waiting 6s then RTL.', waits 6 s more and commands RTL.
nodes.called_when: From update_waypoint_reached when the drone reaches the waypoint of visit_plan[visit_idx].
nodes.inputs: target: one visit_plan entry with type, lat, lon, alt, servos ([13] tent, [11] person) and wp.
nodes.effects: Mode changes (GUIDED, AUTO, RTL) and MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO commands through MAVROS; STATUSTEXT messages.

nodes.label: after_close
nodes.explain: Step that runs right after the servo has closed: it counts this target as done (visit_idx + 1), then switches to AUTO so the drone flies to the next target, or, after the last one, sends 'All targets done. Waiting 6s then RTL.'.
nodes.called_when: By the StepRunner, right after the close step (3 s after the servo opened).

nodes.label: go_home
nodes.source:
def go_home():
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
            self.send_ack("RTL")
nodes.explain: Final step after the last drop: sets mission_phase to 'done', commands RTL and sends the STATUSTEXT 'RTL'.
nodes.called_when: By the StepRunner, 6 s after the last target's servo closed.
nodes.effects: ArduPilot flies home and lands.

nodes.label: valid_detection
nodes.explain: Says whether a target class ('person' or 'tent') has been found at all: True when its best confidence is above 0.

nodes.label: waypoints_cb
nodes.explain: Keeps the newest copy of the mission that MAVROS publishes and recomputes the hold waypoint from it.
nodes.called_when: On every /mavros/mission/waypoints message (after a pull or an upload).

nodes.label: _update_last_nav_before_rtl
nodes.doc:
Find the last actual NAV waypoint index before RTL, and the buffer
waypoint (one NAV waypoint before that) used for GUIDED processing hold.
DigiCamCtrl and other DO_ commands don't trigger WaypointReached,
so we need the index of the last physical navigation waypoint.
nodes.explain: Walks the mission backwards from the RTL item and finds the last real flying waypoint (a NAV command, numbers 16-22) before it, because DO_ items such as DigiCamCtrl never send 'reached'. That index (last_nav_before_rtl; runway: 10) is where the processing hold starts; the NAV item before it is kept as buffer_wp (runway: 9). It never looks past the end of the received list and logs only when the answer changes.
nodes.called_when: After a new mission list (waypoints_cb) and after new indices (_on_mission_indices).

nodes.label: _check_all_images_processed
nodes.doc:
Timer during the 'processing' hold: once every captured image has been
processed by object detection, stop waiting and divert to the targets.

The hold ALWAYS ends by PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (Task 2 review fix): a missing or
unreadable photo folder used to raise inside the old try/except on every tick, so the
timeout branch was never reached and the drone hovered until a failsafe. The listing
and the decision are in processing_hold.py (never raise; unit-tested), and the hold is
timed with the monotonic clock (a wall-clock jump cannot stretch it).
nodes.source:
def _check_all_images_processed(self):
        """Timer during the 'processing' hold: once every captured image has been
        processed by object detection, stop waiting and divert to the targets.

        The hold ALWAYS ends by PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (Task 2 review fix): a missing or
        unreadable photo folder used to raise inside the old try/except on every tick, so the
        timeout branch was never reached and the drone hovered until a failsafe. The listing
        and the decision are in processing_hold.py (never raise; unit-tested), and the hold is
        timed with the monotonic clock (a wall-clock jump cannot stretch it).
        """
        if self.mission_phase != "processing":
            if self.processing_check_timer:
                self.processing_check_timer.cancel()
                self.processing_check_timer = None
            return
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - self.processing_started_at
        names, folder_error = hold.list_photo_names(self.camera_feed_path)
        decision = hold.decide(names, self.processed_image_names, elapsed,
                               PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS)

        # Say once (and again only if the reason changes) that the folder cannot be read,
        # instead of the same error every 2 s.
        if folder_error != getattr(self, '_photo_folder_error', ''):
            self._photo_folder_error = folder_error
            if folder_error:
                self.get_logger().warn(
                    f"Cannot read the photo folder {self.camera_feed_path} ({folder_error}). "
                    f"Waiting for the detector until the {PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:.0f} s "
                    f"limit, then going on with the targets found so far.")
        if decision.folder_readable:
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Processing check: {decision.processed}/{decision.total} images done, "
                f"{decision.remaining} remaining")

        if decision.action == hold.WAIT:
            return
        if decision.action == hold.ALL_DONE:
            self.send_ack(f"All {decision.total} images processed. Selecting targets.")
        elif not decision.folder_readable:
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f"Processing timeout after {elapsed:.0f}s and the photo folder is unreadable "
                f"({folder_error}): diverting with the {len(self.processed_image_names)} "
                f"detector answer(s) received.")
            # <= 50 characters (MAVLink STATUSTEXT) and starts like the other timeout text, which
            # the simulator's phase monitor recognises ("Processing timeout" ... "images").
            self.send_ack("Processing timeout: images unreadable. Diverting.")
        else:
            # Divert with whatever finished rather than loiter indefinitely.
            self.get_logger().warn(
                f"Processing timeout after {elapsed:.0f}s: {decision.processed}/{decision.total} "
                f"done, {decision.remaining} never processed. Diverting anyway.")
            self.send_ack(
                f"Processing timeout ({decision.processed}/{decision.total}). Diverting anyway.")
        self._end_processing_hold()
nodes.explain: The 2 s check during the GUIDED processing hold. It lists the photos in the photo folder (processing_hold.list_photo_names), compares them with the photo names already answered on /image_detection, and lets processing_hold.decide choose (90 s limit, monotonic clock): keep waiting, or go on with 'All N images processed. Selecting targets.' or a 'Processing timeout ...' text and end the hold.
nodes.called_when: Every 2 s by the timer that update_waypoint_reached creates; outside the processing phase it cancels its own timer.
nodes.effects: Logs 'Processing check: x/y images done, z remaining'; warns once (not every 2 s) if the folder cannot be read; STATUSTEXT when the hold ends.

nodes.label: _end_processing_hold
nodes.doc: Stop the processing hold for good and divert (or RTL when nothing was found).
nodes.source:
def _end_processing_hold(self):
        """Stop the processing hold for good and divert (or RTL when nothing was found)."""
        if self.processing_check_timer:
            self.processing_check_timer.cancel()
            self.processing_check_timer = None
        self.waiting_for_processing = False
        try:
            self._divert_to_targets()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a bug here must not leave the drone hovering
            # The check timer is already gone, so without this the drone would hover in GUIDED
            # until a failsafe. Going home is the safe end of the mission.
            self.get_logger().error(f"Divert failed ({e}); commanding RTL")
            self.send_ack("Divert failed. Returning to launch.")
            self.mission_phase = "done"
            self.change_mode("RTL")
nodes.explain: Ends the processing hold for good (cancels the 2 s timer) and runs _divert_to_targets. If the divert itself crashes, it logs the error, sends 'Divert failed. Returning to launch.' and commands RTL, so the drone never keeps hovering.
nodes.called_when: From _check_all_images_processed when the decision is ALL_DONE or TIMED_OUT.

nodes.label: locate_detection
nodes.doc:
Where to drop for one detection box: (AimResult, '') or (None, why it is ignored).

Uses the photo's sidecar (written by video_cam at the shutter) to project the box centre
onto the ground (target_geolocation.aim_at_box). Falls back to the photo's own position
when that is not possible, exactly like the old code did for every detection. Returns
no aim point when the photo has no usable GPS position (missing, (0, 0), NaN/inf, out of
range) or the box centre is not a finite number (Task 2 review fix): such a detection
must never become a waypoint or a drop.
nodes.source:
def locate_detection(self, msg, detection):
        """Where to drop for one detection box: (AimResult, '') or (None, why it is ignored).

        Uses the photo's sidecar (written by video_cam at the shutter) to project the box centre
        onto the ground (target_geolocation.aim_at_box). Falls back to the photo's own position
        when that is not possible, exactly like the old code did for every detection. Returns
        no aim point when the photo has no usable GPS position (missing, (0, 0), NaN/inf, out of
        range) or the box centre is not a finite number (Task 2 review fix): such a detection
        must never become a waypoint or a drop.
        """
        image_path = os.path.join(self.camera_feed_path, msg.image_name or '')
        meta = geo.read_photo_sidecar(image_path) if msg.image_name else None
        # Prefer the exact numbers: the sidecar's float64 fix, else the 6-decimal file name, and
        # only last the float32 copy in the message (0.4-0.7 m rounding).
        name_lat, name_lon = self._latlon_from_name(msg.image_name)
        if name_lat is None:
            name_lat, name_lon = float(msg.latitude), float(msg.longitude)
        position = geo.photo_position(meta, name_lat, name_lon)
        if position is None:
            return None, 'the photo has no usable GPS position'
        photo_lat, photo_lon = position
        u = float(detection.bbox.center.position.x)
        v = float(detection.bbox.center.position.y)
        if not geo.is_finite_number(u, v):
            # Checked even when aiming is off: a box that is not a number is a broken detection.
            return None, f'the box centre ({u}, {v}) is not a finite number'
        if not self.aim_at_box:
            return geo.AimResult(photo_lat, photo_lon, 'photo',
                                 note='photo position (aim_at_detection_box is false)'), ''
        aim = geo.aim_at_box(meta, photo_lat, photo_lon, u, v, geo.jpeg_size(image_path),
                             default_pitch_deg=self.default_pitch,
                             default_hfov_deg=self.default_hfov,
                             ground_height_m=self.ground_height,
                             max_offset_m=self.max_aim_offset)
        if aim is None:
            return None, 'no usable aim point'
        return aim, ''
nodes.explain: Works out where to drop for one detection box. It opens the photo's sidecar, takes the photo's GPS position (the sidecar's fix first, then the 6-decimal file name, last the float32 copy in the message), reads the box centre (bbox.center.position x and y, in pixels) and asks target_geolocation.aim_at_box for the ground point under it. If aim_at_detection_box is false it simply uses the photo's position.
nodes.called_when: From image_result_cb, only for a box that beats the best confidence of its class.
nodes.inputs: msg (the ImageResult) and detection (one box).
nodes.outputs: (AimResult, '') or (None, a reason such as 'the photo has no usable GPS position' or 'the box centre (...) is not a finite number').

nodes.label: _latlon_from_name
nodes.doc: (lat, lon) from a '<lat> , <lon>.jpg' photo name (same rule as detection/geotag.py).
nodes.explain: Reads the GPS position out of a photo name like '36.215153 , -96.006786.jpg' (split at ' , ', the same rule as detection/geotag.py) and returns (lat, lon) as numbers, or (None, None) if the name does not have that form.

nodes.label: image_result_cb
nodes.source:
def image_result_cb(self, msg):
         # Track all processed image names for processing completion check
        if msg.image_name:
            self.processed_image_names.add(msg.image_name)

        if msg.detections.detections:
            self.get_logger().info(f"{len(msg.detections.detections)} object(s) detected!")
            
            #self.get_logger().info(f"{msg}")
            for detection in msg.detections.detections:
                for result in detection.results:
                    obj_id = result.hypothesis.class_id
                    obj_class = {"0": "person", "1": "tent"}.get(obj_id)
                    if obj_class is None:
                        # Ignore classes that are not actionable mission targets.
                        continue
                    obj_conf = result.hypothesis.score
                    if not geo.is_finite_number(obj_conf):
                        # An infinite score would win every comparison and lock in this box
                        # for good; NaN never wins but is still a broken result.
                        self.get_logger().warn(
                            f"Ignoring {obj_class} in '{msg.image_name}': its score "
                            f"{obj_conf} is not a finite number")
                        continue

                    if obj_class in self.detections:        # only works if obj_class is saved as 'person' or 'tent'    // TODO: DOUBLE CHECK THIS
                        if obj_conf > self.detections[obj_class].confidence:        # get highest conf
                            aim, why = self.locate_detection(msg, detection)
                            if aim is None:
                                # Nowhere safe to fly to (no/NaN GPS, broken box). The old code
                                # stored 0,0 and would have sent the drone there.
                                self.get_logger().warn(
                                    f"Ignoring {obj_class} ({obj_conf:.2f}) in "
                                    f"'{msg.image_name}': {why}")
                                continue
                            self.get_logger().info(f"Updating {obj_class}: old_conf={self.detections[obj_class].confidence:.2f}, new_conf={obj_conf:.2f}")
                            self.send_ack(f"Detected {obj_class}")
                            # self.move_servo(11,1400)   # debug: fired on every new best detection
                            # self.move_servo(11,500)
                            # update conf
                            self.detections[obj_class].confidence = obj_conf
                            # update wp_index
                            # self.detections[obj_class].waypoint_index = msg.waypoint_index
                            self.detections[obj_class].lat = aim.lat
                            self.detections[obj_class].long = aim.lon
                            self.detections[obj_class].image_name = msg.image_name
                            self.detections[obj_class].aim_note = aim.note
                            self.get_logger().info(f"Obj at long: {self.detections[obj_class].long}, lat: {self.detections[obj_class].lat}")
                            self.get_logger().info(f"  aimed at the {aim.note}")
        else:
            self.get_logger().info("No objects detected.")
            self.send_ack("No objects detected.")
nodes.explain: Handles the detector's answer for one photo. It records the photo name as processed (for the hold check). For each box with class '0' (person) or '1' (tent) and a finite score higher than the best so far, it works out the aim point with locate_detection and, if it is usable, stores the new best confidence, aim point, photo name and note and sends STATUSTEXT 'Detected <class>'. A photo with no boxes gives the STATUSTEXT 'No objects detected.'.
nodes.called_when: On every /image_detection message (one per photo, about one per second during the survey).
nodes.inputs: msg: interfaces/ImageResult.
nodes.effects: STATUSTEXT messages; a box without a usable position is ignored with a warning (the old code would have sent the drone to 0,0).

nodes.label: change_mode
nodes.source:
def change_mode(self, mode):
        # set_mode service should already be ready from self._wait_for_services
        self.get_logger().info(f"Setting mode to {mode}...")
        try:
            req = SetMode.Request()
            req.custom_mode = mode
            # Fire-and-forget: never block (this runs inside a subscription
            # callback under a single-threaded executor — spinning here deadlocks).
            future = self.set_mode_client.call_async(req)
            future.add_done_callback(lambda f, m=mode: self._on_mode_result(f, m))
        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(str(e))
nodes.explain: Asks the autopilot to switch flight mode ('GUIDED', 'AUTO' or 'RTL') by calling /mavros/set_mode with custom_mode. It does not wait for the answer (call_async); _on_mode_result logs it later.
nodes.effects: MAVROS sends the mode change to ArduPilot over MAVLink.

nodes.label: _on_mode_result
nodes.explain: Logs the answer to a mode change: 'Mode changed to X' when MAVROS reports mode_sent, otherwise 'Failed to change mode to X'.
nodes.called_when: When /mavros/set_mode answers (done-callback set by change_mode).

nodes.label: send_waypoint_data
nodes.source:
def send_waypoint_data(self, wp_list):
        # AddWaypoint is scalar (one waypoint per call); send one request each.
        self.get_logger().info(f"Sending {len(wp_list)} waypoints")

        for i, wp in enumerate(wp_list):
            try:
                req = AddWaypoint.Request()
                req.command = 16  # NAV_WAYPOINT
                req.latitude = float(wp["lat"])
                req.longitude = float(wp["lon"])
                req.altitude = float(wp["alt"])
                req.index = int(wp["index"])
                req.channel = 0
                req.pwm = 0

                self.get_logger().info(
                    f"Waypoint {i + 1}: lat={wp['lat']}, lon={wp['lon']}, "
                    f"alt={wp['alt']}, index={wp['index']}"
                )

                self.add_wp_client.call_async(req)
            except Exception as e:
                self.get_logger().error(f"Error sending waypoint {i + 1}: {str(e)}")
nodes.explain: Sends one /addWaypoint request per target: command 16 (NAV_WAYPOINT), latitude, longitude, altitude and the insert index, channel 0, pwm 0. It does not wait for the answers.
nodes.called_when: From _divert_to_targets.
nodes.effects: waypoint_manager inserts each waypoint and uploads the whole mission to the autopilot.

nodes.label: set_current_wp
nodes.explain: Tells the autopilot which mission item to fly to next (/mavros/mission/set_current with wp_seq), without waiting for the answer, and sends STATUSTEXT 'Set current WP -> N'.
nodes.called_when: By the 'resume AUTO' sequence, 4 s after the targets were sent.

nodes.label: divert_and_resume
nodes.source:
def divert_and_resume(self, target_seq):
        # Let the full-mission push land on the FCU, then point the vehicle at
        # the first divert waypoint and resume AUTO so it flies there instead of
        # continuing the RTL. Timed steps, never sleeps: the node keeps handling
        # the /addWaypoint answers and parameter events meanwhile.
        if target_seq is None or target_seq < 0:
            return

        def resume():
            self.change_mode("AUTO")
            self.send_ack(f"Resumed AUTO -> WP {target_seq}")

        self.steps.start('resume AUTO', [
            (PUSH_SETTLE_SECONDS, 'set current waypoint', lambda: self.set_current_wp(target_seq)),
            (SET_CURRENT_TO_AUTO_SECONDS, 'resume AUTO', resume),
        ])
nodes.explain: Starts the timed 'resume AUTO' sequence: after 4 s (time for the mission upload to reach the autopilot) point the mission at the first target with set_current_wp, and 1 s later switch to AUTO. Does nothing for a missing or negative index.
nodes.called_when: From _divert_to_targets, with the first target's mission index.

nodes.label: resume
nodes.explain: Last step of the 'resume AUTO' sequence: switches to AUTO and sends STATUSTEXT 'Resumed AUTO -> WP N', so the drone flies to the first target.
nodes.called_when: By the StepRunner, 1 s after set_current_wp.

nodes.label: open_servos
nodes.doc: Open the given release servos (all together).
nodes.explain: Opens the given release servo channels together (PWM 1400 us) with move_servo, logging 'Opening servos [..] for 3s'.
nodes.called_when: By the drop sequence, 6 s after arriving over a target.

nodes.label: close_servos
nodes.doc: Close the given release servos (all together).
nodes.explain: Closes the given release servo channels together (PWM 500 us) with move_servo.
nodes.called_when: By the drop sequence, 3 s after opening.

nodes.label: actuate_servos
nodes.doc:
Open the given release servos, hold OPEN for SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS,
then close them back. All servos open together and close together.
Never blocks: the close is a one-shot timer.
nodes.source:
def actuate_servos(self, channels):
        """Open the given release servos, hold OPEN for SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS,
        then close them back. All servos open together and close together.
        Never blocks: the close is a one-shot timer."""
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Opening servos {channels} -> hold {SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS:.0f}s -> close")
        self.open_servos(channels)
        call_later(self, SERVO_OPEN_SECONDS, lambda: self.close_servos(channels))
nodes.explain: Opens the given servos and closes them 3 s later with a one-shot timer (call_later), never blocking. Only the commented-out start-up servo self-test refers to it, so it is not called in flight.

nodes.label: move_servo
nodes.source:
def move_servo(self, channel, pwm):
        try:
            # Sending request to move servo
            request = CommandLong.Request()
            request.broadcast = False
            request.command = 183  # MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO
            request.confirmation = 0
            request.param1 = float(channel)
            request.param2 = float(pwm)
            request.param3 = float(0)
            request.param4 = float(0)
            request.param5 = float(0)
            request.param6 = float(0)
            request.param7 = float(0)

            # Fire-and-forget: do NOT spin here. This runs inside a subscription
            # callback under a single-threaded executor, so spin_until_future_complete
            # would deadlock the node. call_async already puts the command on the wire.
            future = self.command_client.call_async(request)
            future.add_done_callback(lambda f, c=channel, p=pwm: self._on_servo_result(f, c, p))

        except Exception as e:
            self.get_logger().error(f"Service call failed: {e}")
nodes.explain: Sends MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO (command 183) through /mavros/cmd/command: param1 = servo output channel, param2 = PWM in microseconds, the other params 0. Fire-and-forget: the answer is handled by _on_servo_result.
nodes.inputs: channel (11 person, 13 tent) and pwm (1400 open, 500 closed).
nodes.effects: The Pixhawk moves that output (in the simulator, payload_release lets the payload fall when the output reaches 1400 us).

nodes.label: _on_servo_result
nodes.explain: Handles the autopilot's answer to a servo command: on success it logs and sends STATUSTEXT 'Servo C -> PWM' (the simulator counts 'Servo 13 -> 1400' as a drop), otherwise 'Servo C move FAILED'.
nodes.called_when: When /mavros/cmd/command answers (done-callback set by move_servo).

nodes.label: send_ack
nodes.source:
def send_ack(self, text):
        msg = StatusText()
        msg.severity = 6  # INFO
        msg.text = text
        self.status_publisher.publish(msg)
        self.get_logger().info(f"Status: {text}")
nodes.explain: Sends a text to the ground station: publishes a mavros_msgs/StatusText with severity 6 (INFO) on /mavros/statustext/send and writes 'Status: <text>' to the log.
nodes.effects: MAVROS forwards it as a MAVLink STATUSTEXT (cut at 50 characters) to Mission Planner; the simulator's phase monitor and scorer read these texts.

nodes.label: target_geolocation.py
nodes.doc:
Work out where on the ground a detected object is, from its box in the photo.

target_geolocation.py -- PURPOSE: turn the pixel position of a detection box into latitude /
longitude. main_controller.py uses it to aim the payload drops.

Why (October 2026): main_controller used to fly to the drone's own GPS position at the moment the
photo was taken. A target near the edge of a photo is then up to half a picture away: in the
simulator the drops missed by 14-25 m. Now the box centre is projected onto the ground.

The idea, for the normal survey case (camera looking straight down):

        top of the photo = the direction the camera faces (the drone's nose in the simulator)
      +-------------------------------------+
      |                                     |
      |               X  box centre (u, v)  |   (du, dv) = pixels from the photo centre
      |                  +  photo centre    |   on flat ground that is
      |                                     |       du * H / f  metres to the photo's right
      +-------------------------------------+       dv * H / f  metres to the photo's bottom
                                                H = camera height above the ground
                                                f = focal length in pixels
                                                  = (photo width / 2) / tan(horizontal FOV / 2)
    then those metres are turned to east/north with the compass heading of the photo's top
    and added to the drone's GPS position. A tilted camera is handled the same way with a 3D ray.

Inputs come from the photo's "sidecar" (a JSON file video_cam writes next to every photo, format
in video_cam/photo_metadata.py): drone position, height above home and heading at the shutter,
camera field of view, zoom, gimbal angles and how the photo is turned relative to the drone.

Conventions (used everywhere in this file):
  * compass headings in degrees: 0 = north, 90 = east, clockwise;
  * camera pitch in the SIYI sign: 0 = horizon, -90 = straight down;
  * gimbal yaw in the SIYI sign: + = the camera turned LEFT of the nose;
  * pixels in OpenCV order: (0, 0) = top-left corner, u to the right, v down;
  * ground offsets in metres east / north of the point below the camera;
  * latitude/longitude <-> metres with ArduPilot's own flat-earth formula (AP_Common
    Location::offset / get_distance_NE), so the result is exactly what the autopilot flies to.

Numbers that are not numbers (fixed after the Task 2 review, October 2026): NaN ("not a number")
and infinity slip through ordinary comparisons (every comparison with NaN is False, so a check
like `height <= 0` lets NaN pass) and turn the whole answer into NaN, i.e. a waypoint at
latitude NaN. Now every input is checked with math.isfinite: a non-finite or out-of-range GPS
position means "no position" (the detection is ignored), a non-finite box centre means the box is
unusable (ignored, never aimed at), a non-finite sidecar value (height, heading, field of view,
zoom, gimbal angles) counts as "not recorded" (the documented fallback to the photo position), and
every answer is checked once more before it is returned. So no NaN/inf can reach a waypoint.

Pure Python (math, json, os, struct only): no ROS. Unit tests: ../test/test_target_geolocation.py
    python3 -m pytest ros2_ws/src/main/test/test_target_geolocation.py -v
nodes.explain: The drop-aiming math, in pure Python (no ROS). It turns the pixel position of a detection box in a photo into a latitude / longitude on the ground: using the photo's sidecar (height above home, heading, field of view, zoom, gimbal angles, how the photo is turned) it shoots an imaginary ray from the camera through that pixel, finds where the ray hits flat ground, and moves the photo's GPS point by that many metres east / north with ArduPilot's own formula. Anything that is NaN, infinite or out of range is refused, so it can never become a waypoint.
nodes.how_it_fits: main_controller.locate_detection calls read_photo_sidecar, photo_position, jpeg_size and aim_at_box for every new best detection. Before October 2026 the drone dropped where it was when the photo was taken (14-25 m misses in the simulator); with this file the recorded simulator drops land within about 1-2 m of the targets. The sidecar format 'astra.photo_metadata.v1' comes from video_cam/photo_metadata.py. On disk on 2026-10-31 the work-in-progress lattice_bridge package also loads this file to place targets. Tested by test/test_target_geolocation.py.

nodes.label: is_finite_number
nodes.doc: Return True when every value is a real, finite number (not NaN, not +-inf, not junk).
nodes.explain: Returns True only if every value given is a real, finite number. NaN ('not a number'), plus or minus infinity, True / False and anything that cannot be turned into a number make it False.
nodes.called_when: Before the calculations in this file and in main_controller (box centre, score, settings).

nodes.label: valid_latlon
nodes.doc:
Tell whether (lat, lon) is a usable GPS position.

Finite, latitude within +-90, longitude within +-180, and not (0, 0): the flight controller
reports (0, 0) before it has a GPS lock ("Null Island").
nodes.explain: Says whether (lat, lon) is a usable GPS position: both finite, latitude within +-90, longitude within +-180, and not (0, 0) ('Null Island', which the autopilot reports before it has a GPS lock).

nodes.label: wrap_360
nodes.doc: Wrap an angle to [0, 360) degrees.
nodes.source:
def wrap_360(angle_deg: float) -> float:
    """Wrap an angle to [0, 360) degrees."""
    a = math.fmod(float(angle_deg), 360.0)
    return a + 360.0 if a < 0 else a
nodes.explain: Turns any angle into the range 0 up to (not including) 360 degrees; for example -90 becomes 270.

nodes.label: focal_length_px
nodes.signature: def focal_length_px(width_px: float, hfov_deg: float, zoom: float=1.0) -> float
nodes.doc:
Compute the focal length in pixels of a picture `width_px` wide.

Zoom narrows the view: tan(hfov_zoomed / 2) = tan(hfov / 2) / zoom (optical or digital).
nodes.source:
def focal_length_px(width_px: float, hfov_deg: float, zoom: float = 1.0) -> float:
    """
    Compute the focal length in pixels of a picture `width_px` wide.

    Zoom narrows the view: tan(hfov_zoomed / 2) = tan(hfov / 2) / zoom (optical or digital).
    """
    z = max(1e-6, float(zoom))
    return (float(width_px) / 2.0) / (math.tan(math.radians(hfov_deg) / 2.0) / z)
nodes.explain: Computes the camera's focal length in pixels: (picture width / 2) divided by (tan(field of view / 2) / zoom). Example: a 2560-pixel-wide photo with an 81 degree view at zoom 1 gives about 1499 px, so from 30 m up one pixel near the centre covers about 2 cm of ground.
nodes.inputs: width_px, hfov_deg, zoom (1 = widest; zoom narrows the view).

nodes.label: offset_to_latlon
nodes.signature: def offset_to_latlon(lat: float, lon: float, east_m: float, north_m: float) -> Tuple[float, float]
nodes.doc: Move a GPS point by east/north metres (ArduPilot's Location::offset formula).
nodes.source:
def offset_to_latlon(lat: float, lon: float, east_m: float,
                     north_m: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Move a GPS point by east/north metres (ArduPilot's Location::offset formula)."""
    dlat = north_m / METRES_PER_DEGREE
    mid_lat = lat + dlat / 2.0
    scale = max(math.cos(math.radians(mid_lat)), 0.01)
    return lat + dlat, lon + east_m / (METRES_PER_DEGREE * scale)
nodes.explain: Moves a GPS point by some metres east and north and returns the new latitude / longitude, with ArduPilot's own flat-earth formula (about 111,318.8 m per degree of latitude; longitude scaled by the cosine of the latitude), so the result is exactly the point the autopilot will fly to.

nodes.label: latlon_to_offset
nodes.signature: def latlon_to_offset(lat0: float, lon0: float, lat: float, lon: float) -> Tuple[float, float]
nodes.doc: Return the east/north metres from (lat0, lon0) to (lat, lon).
nodes.source:
def latlon_to_offset(lat0: float, lon0: float, lat: float, lon: float) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Return the east/north metres from (lat0, lon0) to (lat, lon)."""
    north = (lat - lat0) * METRES_PER_DEGREE
    dlon = (lon - lon0 + 540.0) % 360.0 - 180.0
    scale = max(math.cos(math.radians((lat0 + lat) / 2.0)), 0.01)
    return dlon * METRES_PER_DEGREE * scale, north
nodes.explain: The opposite of offset_to_latlon: returns how many metres east and north the point (lat, lon) is from (lat0, lon0). main_controller does not use it; the tests do.

nodes.label: compass_name
nodes.signature: def compass_name(east_m: float, north_m: float) -> str
nodes.doc: Name the direction of a ground offset ('north', 'south-east', ...) for log messages.
nodes.source:
def compass_name(east_m: float, north_m: float) -> str:
    """Name the direction of a ground offset ('north', 'south-east', ...) for log messages."""
    names = ['north', 'north-east', 'east', 'south-east', 'south', 'south-west', 'west',
             'north-west']
    bearing = wrap_360(math.degrees(math.atan2(east_m, north_m)))
    return names[int((bearing + 22.5) // 45.0) % 8]
nodes.explain: Names the direction of a ground offset with one of 8 words ('north', 'north-east', 'east', ... 'north-west') for the log messages.

nodes.label: pixel_to_ground_offset
nodes.signature: def pixel_to_ground_offset(u: float, v: float, image_width: int, image_height: int, hfov_deg: float, height_m: float, camera_heading_deg: float, camera_pitch_deg: float=-90.0, image_top_direction_deg: float=0.0, zoom: float=1.0, max_range_m: float=1000.0) -> Optional[Tuple[float, float]]
nodes.doc:
Find where on flat ground pixel (u, v) of a photo is, relative to the point below the camera.

Parameters
----------
u, v
    Pixel position in the saved photo (e.g. a detection box centre).
image_width, image_height
    Size of the saved photo in pixels.
hfov_deg
    Horizontal field of view of the camera's natural picture at zoom 1.
height_m
    Camera height above the ground under the target, metres (> 0).
camera_heading_deg
    Compass direction the camera faces (for a straight-down camera: where the top of its
    natural picture points; = drone heading when the gimbal yaw is centred).
camera_pitch_deg
    -90 = straight down, -60 = tilted 30 deg forward, 0 = horizon.
image_top_direction_deg
    Where the TOP of the SAVED photo points, clockwise from the top of the camera's natural
    picture (same meaning as video_cam's parameter of that name): 0 (simulator), 90 (the
    saved top shows what is on the natural picture's right), 180 (e.g. rotate_180) or 270.
    (The Task 2 review checked the code and tests against this meaning; only the wording
    here was ambiguous.)
zoom
    Zoom factor at the shutter (1 = widest).
max_range_m
    Farther answers are refused (a pixel near the horizon).

Returns
-------
tuple or None
    (east_m, north_m), or None if the pixel looks at the sky/horizon, is farther than
    max_range_m, or an input is impossible (zero size, height <= 0, bad field of view).
nodes.source:
def pixel_to_ground_offset(u: float, v: float, image_width: int, image_height: int,
                           hfov_deg: float, height_m: float, camera_heading_deg: float,
                           camera_pitch_deg: float = -90.0,
                           image_top_direction_deg: float = 0.0, zoom: float = 1.0,
                           max_range_m: float = 1000.0) -> Optional[Tuple[float, float]]:
    """
    Find where on flat ground pixel (u, v) of a photo is, relative to the point below the camera.

    Parameters
    ----------
    u, v
        Pixel position in the saved photo (e.g. a detection box centre).
    image_width, image_height
        Size of the saved photo in pixels.
    hfov_deg
        Horizontal field of view of the camera's natural picture at zoom 1.
    height_m
        Camera height above the ground under the target, metres (> 0).
    camera_heading_deg
        Compass direction the camera faces (for a straight-down camera: where the top of its
        natural picture points; = drone heading when the gimbal yaw is centred).
    camera_pitch_deg
        -90 = straight down, -60 = tilted 30 deg forward, 0 = horizon.
    image_top_direction_deg
        Where the TOP of the SAVED photo points, clockwise from the top of the camera's natural
        picture (same meaning as video_cam's parameter of that name): 0 (simulator), 90 (the
        saved top shows what is on the natural picture's right), 180 (e.g. rotate_180) or 270.
        (The Task 2 review checked the code and tests against this meaning; only the wording
        here was ambiguous.)
    zoom
        Zoom factor at the shutter (1 = widest).
    max_range_m
        Farther answers are refused (a pixel near the horizon).

    Returns
    -------
    tuple or None
        (east_m, north_m), or None if the pixel looks at the sky/horizon, is farther than
        max_range_m, or an input is impossible (zero size, height <= 0, bad field of view).

    """
    # Every input must be a finite number: NaN passes every "<=" test below unnoticed and would
    # come out as a NaN offset (a waypoint at latitude NaN).
    if not is_finite_number(u, v, image_width, image_height, hfov_deg, height_m,
                            camera_heading_deg, camera_pitch_deg, image_top_direction_deg, zoom,
                            max_range_m):
        return None
    if image_width <= 0 or image_height <= 0 or height_m <= 0.0 or zoom <= 0.0:
        return None
    if not 0.0 < hfov_deg < 180.0:
        return None

    # 1. Turn the pixel offset back into the camera's natural picture (top = where it faces).
    alpha = math.radians(image_top_direction_deg)
    ca, sa = math.cos(alpha), math.sin(alpha)
    du_saved = float(u) - image_width / 2.0
    dv_saved = float(v) - image_height / 2.0
    du = ca * du_saved - sa * dv_saved
    dv = sa * du_saved + ca * dv_saved
    # The natural picture's width is the saved width, or the saved height when turned sideways.
    natural_width = image_width if abs(ca) >= abs(sa) else image_height
    f = focal_length_px(natural_width, hfov_deg, zoom)

    # 2. The camera's axes in east/north/up (no roll: the gimbal keeps the picture level).
    psi = math.radians(camera_heading_deg)
    theta = math.radians(camera_pitch_deg)
    forward = (math.cos(theta) * math.sin(psi), math.cos(theta) * math.cos(psi),
               math.sin(theta))
    image_up = (-math.sin(theta) * math.sin(psi), -math.sin(theta) * math.cos(psi),
                math.cos(theta))
    image_down = (-image_up[0], -image_up[1], -image_up[2])
    # right = down x forward
    right = (image_down[1] * forward[2] - image_down[2] * forward[1],
             image_down[2] * forward[0] - image_down[0] * forward[2],
             image_down[0] * forward[1] - image_down[1] * forward[0])

    # 3. The ray through the pixel, and where it meets the ground (height_m below the camera).
    a, b = du / f, dv / f
    ray = tuple(right[i] * a + image_down[i] * b + forward[i] for i in range(3))
    if ray[2] >= -1e-9:
        return None                                  # sky or horizon
    t = height_m / -ray[2]
    east, north = t * ray[0], t * ray[1]
    if not is_finite_number(east, north) or math.hypot(east, north) > max_range_m:
        return None
    return east, north
nodes.explain: The core geometry: finds where pixel (u, v) of a photo lands on flat ground, as metres east and north of the point straight below the camera. It undoes the photo's turn (image_top_direction_deg), builds the camera's forward / right / down directions from its compass heading and pitch, shoots a ray through the pixel and finds where it meets the ground height_m below. It returns None for the sky or the horizon, for anything farther than max_range_m, and for impossible inputs (NaN, zero size, height of 0 or less, field of view outside 0-180 degrees).
nodes.inputs: u, v, image_width, image_height, hfov_deg, height_m, camera_heading_deg, camera_pitch_deg (-90 = straight down), image_top_direction_deg, zoom, max_range_m.

nodes.source:
@dataclass
class AimResult:
    """
    Where main_controller should fly for one detection.

    lat, lon: the aim point (degrees). method: 'box' (projected from the box centre) or 'photo'
    (the photo's own position). east_m, north_m: aim point minus the photo position, metres
    (0, 0 for 'photo'). note: one short line for the log saying how it was computed or why it
    fell back.
    """

    lat: float
    lon: float
    method: str
    east_m: float = 0.0
    north_m: float = 0.0
    note: str = ''

    @property
    def offset_m(self) -> float:
        """Return the distance between the aim point and the photo position, metres."""
        return math.hypot(self.east_m, self.north_m)
nodes.explain: The answer for one detection: lat and lon of the aim point, method ('box' = projected from the box centre, 'photo' = the photo's own position), east_m and north_m (how far the aim point is from the photo position) and a one-line note for the log.

nodes.label: aim_at_box
nodes.signature: def aim_at_box(meta: Optional[dict], photo_lat: float, photo_lon: float, u: float, v: float, image_size: Optional[Tuple[int, int]], default_pitch_deg: float=-90.0, default_hfov_deg: float=81.0, ground_height_m: float=0.0, max_offset_m: float=150.0, min_height_m: float=3.0) -> Optional[AimResult]
nodes.doc:
Compute the aim point for a detection box centred at pixel (u, v) of a photo.

Falls back to the photo's own position (the old behaviour) when the photo cannot be
projected: no sidecar, no height or heading recorded (a NaN/inf value counts as not
recorded), zoom changing at the shutter, unknown image size, a setting that is not a finite
number, or an answer that is implausibly far away. The reason is in AimResult.note.

Returns None -- "do not aim at this detection at all" -- when the photo position is not a
usable GPS position or the box centre (u, v) is not a finite number: there is no safe point
to fly to, and a broken box must never decide a drop.

Parameters
----------
meta
    The photo's sidecar dict (read_photo_sidecar) or None.
photo_lat, photo_lon
    The drone's position for the photo (photo_position()).
u, v
    Box centre in pixels of the saved photo.
image_size
    (width, height) of the saved photo (jpeg_size()) or None.
default_pitch_deg
    Camera pitch when the camera did not report its attitude.
default_hfov_deg
    Field of view when the sidecar has none.
ground_height_m
    Height of the ground under the targets above home (rel_alt is above home).
max_offset_m
    Answers farther than this from the photo position are not trusted.
min_height_m
    Below this height above the ground no projection is attempted.

Returns
-------
AimResult or None
    The aim point and how it was found; None when the detection must be ignored.
nodes.source:
def aim_at_box(meta: Optional[dict], photo_lat: float, photo_lon: float, u: float, v: float,
               image_size: Optional[Tuple[int, int]], default_pitch_deg: float = -90.0,
               default_hfov_deg: float = 81.0, ground_height_m: float = 0.0,
               max_offset_m: float = 150.0,
               min_height_m: float = 3.0) -> Optional[AimResult]:
    """
    Compute the aim point for a detection box centred at pixel (u, v) of a photo.

    Falls back to the photo's own position (the old behaviour) when the photo cannot be
    projected: no sidecar, no height or heading recorded (a NaN/inf value counts as not
    recorded), zoom changing at the shutter, unknown image size, a setting that is not a finite
    number, or an answer that is implausibly far away. The reason is in AimResult.note.

    Returns None -- "do not aim at this detection at all" -- when the photo position is not a
    usable GPS position or the box centre (u, v) is not a finite number: there is no safe point
    to fly to, and a broken box must never decide a drop.

    Parameters
    ----------
    meta
        The photo's sidecar dict (read_photo_sidecar) or None.
    photo_lat, photo_lon
        The drone's position for the photo (photo_position()).
    u, v
        Box centre in pixels of the saved photo.
    image_size
        (width, height) of the saved photo (jpeg_size()) or None.
    default_pitch_deg
        Camera pitch when the camera did not report its attitude.
    default_hfov_deg
        Field of view when the sidecar has none.
    ground_height_m
        Height of the ground under the targets above home (rel_alt is above home).
    max_offset_m
        Answers farther than this from the photo position are not trusted.
    min_height_m
        Below this height above the ground no projection is attempted.

    Returns
    -------
    AimResult or None
        The aim point and how it was found; None when the detection must be ignored.

    """
    if not valid_latlon(photo_lat, photo_lon) or not is_finite_number(u, v):
        return None
    photo_lat, photo_lon = float(photo_lat), float(photo_lon)

    def fallback(why: str) -> AimResult:
        return AimResult(photo_lat, photo_lon, 'photo', note=f'photo position ({why})')

    if not is_finite_number(default_pitch_deg, default_hfov_deg, ground_height_m, max_offset_m,
                            min_height_m):
        return fallback('an aiming setting is not a finite number')
    if meta is None:
        return fallback('no sidecar for this photo')
    if not image_size or not is_finite_number(*image_size):
        return fallback('photo size unknown')
    rel_alt = _num(meta, 'rel_alt_m')
    heading = _num(meta, 'heading_deg')
    if rel_alt is None:
        return fallback('no height recorded at the shutter')
    if heading is None:
        return fallback('no heading recorded at the shutter')
    height = rel_alt - float(ground_height_m)
    if height < min_height_m:
        return fallback(f'only {height:.1f} m above the ground')
    camera = meta.get('camera') if isinstance(meta.get('camera'), dict) else {}
    if camera.get('zoom_changing'):
        return fallback('the zoom was moving at the shutter')
    hfov = _num(camera, 'hfov_deg') or float(default_hfov_deg)
    zoom = _num(camera, 'zoom_x') or 1.0
    top_dir = _num(camera, 'image_top_direction_deg') or 0.0

    pitch, gimbal_yaw, attitude_note = float(default_pitch_deg), 0.0, 'pitch assumed'
    gimbal = meta.get('gimbal') if isinstance(meta.get('gimbal'), dict) else None
    g_pitch, g_yaw = _num(gimbal, 'pitch_deg'), _num(gimbal, 'yaw_deg')
    low, high = TRUSTED_PITCH_RANGE_DEG
    if g_pitch is not None and low <= g_pitch <= high:
        pitch, attitude_note = g_pitch, 'gimbal reported'
        if g_yaw is not None:
            gimbal_yaw = g_yaw
    elif g_pitch is not None:
        attitude_note = f'gimbal said pitch {g_pitch:.0f} deg, not trusted'
    # SIYI yaw + = camera turned LEFT, i.e. counter-clockwise = smaller compass heading.
    camera_heading = wrap_360(heading - gimbal_yaw)

    offset = pixel_to_ground_offset(u, v, image_size[0], image_size[1], hfov, height,
                                    camera_heading, pitch, top_dir, zoom,
                                    max_range_m=max_offset_m)
    if offset is None:
        return fallback('the box does not project onto the ground within '
                        f'{max_offset_m:.0f} m')
    east, north = offset
    lat, lon = offset_to_latlon(photo_lat, photo_lon, east, north)
    if not valid_latlon(lat, lon):          # last line of defence: never hand out NaN/inf
        return fallback('the projected point is not a valid position')
    note = (f'box centre, {math.hypot(east, north):.1f} m {compass_name(east, north)} of the '
            f'photo centre (height {height:.1f} m, heading {camera_heading:.0f}, pitch '
            f'{pitch:.0f} [{attitude_note}], FOV {hfov:.0f} deg, zoom {zoom:.1f}x, '
            f'photo top +{top_dir:.0f} deg)')
    return AimResult(lat, lon, 'box', east, north, note)
nodes.explain: Computes the aim point of one detection box. From the sidecar it takes the height (rel_alt_m minus target_ground_height_m), heading, field of view, zoom, photo turn and gimbal angles (the gimbal pitch is trusted only between -120 and -30 degrees, otherwise -90 is assumed), projects the box centre with pixel_to_ground_offset and turns the offset into lat / lon. If a piece is missing or odd (no sidecar, no height or heading, lower than 3 m, zoom moving at the shutter, size unknown, farther than 150 m) it falls back to the photo position and says why in the note.
nodes.inputs: meta (sidecar dict or None), photo_lat, photo_lon, u, v (box centre in pixels), image_size, default_pitch_deg -90, default_hfov_deg 81, ground_height_m 0, max_offset_m 150, min_height_m 3.
nodes.outputs: AimResult (method 'box' or 'photo'), or None when the photo position or the box centre is unusable: that detection must then be ignored.

The six nodes it starts are the ones the simulator's stack_check waits for (the node names themselves are set in each node's code). Commented-out lines: wp_sender test clients, object_detection_sahi, killnode, the mapping stitcher.

nodes.label: test_target_geolocation.py
nodes.doc:
Unit tests for main/src/target_geolocation.py (the drop-aiming math).

test_target_geolocation.py -- PURPOSE: unit tests for the drop aiming added in October 2026
(project a detection box centre onto the ground instead of dropping at the photo's own position).
Checks the geometry with hand-computable cases (centre pixel, image edges, every heading, a turned
photo, a tilted camera, the sky), the ArduPilot latitude/longitude formula, the JPEG size reader,
the sidecar contract with video_cam's writer, every fallback, and -- as a regression test -- the
best hiker and tent detections of three recorded simulator runs, which the old code missed by
14-25 m and which must now land within 2 m of the ground truth. Since the Task 2 review it also
checks that NaN / infinity in any input (GPS, height, heading, box pixels, settings) can never come
out as an aim point, and documents how much a wrong ground height (sloped terrain) or a camera that
is not exactly straight down moves the aim point.

Needs nothing but Python (no ROS, no build):
    python3 -m pytest ros2_ws/src/main/test/test_target_geolocation.py -v
nodes.explain: Pure test file (plain Python, no ROS) for the drop-aiming math: hand-checkable geometry (centre pixel straight below, image edges, every heading, a turned photo, a tilted camera, the sky), the ArduPilot lat/lon formula, the JPEG size reader, the sidecar contract with video_cam's writer, every fallback, NaN / infinity refusal, and how big the error gets on sloped ground. It also replays the best hiker and tent detections of three recorded simulator runs: the old code missed by 14-25 m, the new aim must land within 2 m.
nodes.how_it_fits: Pins target_geolocation.py so a change cannot quietly move the drops.

    # Top-centre pixel: half the vertical footprint ahead (north). 720 px * 30 m / f.
    e, n = geo.pixel_to_ground_offset(W / 2, 0, W, H, HFOV, 30.0, camera_heading_deg=0.0)
