def test_right_edge_is_half_the_footprint_width():
    # Footprint width = 2 * 30 m * tan(40.5 deg) = 51.2 m: the right edge is 25.6 m to the right.
    e, n = geo.pixel_to_ground_offset(W, H / 2, W, H, HFOV, 30.0, camera_heading_deg=0.0)
    assert close(e, 30.0 * math.tan(math.radians(40.5)), 1e-6) and close(n, 0.0)
    assert close(2 * e, 51.2, 0.05)

nodes.label: do_digi_cam_trigger.py
nodes.doc:
Turn the mission's DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL item into one photo request per second.

do_digi_cam_trigger.py -- PURPOSE: the mission_camera_trigger node. When ArduPilot starts the
survey mission's DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL item it says "Mission: <n> DigiCamCtrl"
(/mavros/statustext/recv); this node then
  * asks the camera node to set the lens up once ("capture_setup" on /camera/command),
  * publishes /camera/trigger (std_msgs/Bool true) every `capture_period_s` seconds (1 s),
  * asks for an autofocus pass every `autofocus_period_s` seconds (5 s; 0 = never),
and stops both when the drone reaches waypoint `buffer_wp` (a waypoint_manager parameter).

October 2026: the two periods became ROS parameters (same defaults as before), e.g.
    ros2 run mapping trigger --ros-args -p autofocus_period_s:=0
(whole numbers and decimals both work: `:=0` and `:=0.0`, see number_parameter()).
The camera node now skips autofocus by itself on cameras that cannot do it (A8 mini) and no
longer drops photos while the lens focuses, so the defaults are safe; the parameters let a team
switch the loop off for a fixed-focus survey or slow the photos down for a slower detector.
Tests: test/test_trigger_node.py (runs the real node with rclpy in a private ROS domain).
nodes.explain: The survey photo trigger node (class MissionCameraTrigger, node 'mission_camera_trigger'). When ArduPilot reports 'Mission: <n> DigiCamCtrl' it asks the camera for 'capture_setup' (zoom + focus; video_cam ignores a repeat when the zoom is already right), publishes /camera/trigger every capture_period_s (1 s) and 'autofocus' every autofocus_period_s (5 s, 0 = off), and stops both when the drone reaches waypoint buffer_wp.
nodes.how_it_fits: The link between the mission plan and the camera: ArduPilot (through MAVROS) decides WHEN photos start, this node turns that into requests, and video_cam takes the photos. buffer_wp comes from waypoint_manager (item R-2 of the mission layout; 9 on the simulator's runway mission).

nodes.label: MissionCameraTrigger
nodes.source:
class MissionCameraTrigger(Node):

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("mission_camera_trigger")
        self.create_subscription(StatusText,'/mavros/statustext/recv', self.statustext_callback, qos_profile_sensor_data)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointReached, "/mavros/mission/reached", self.update_waypoint_reached, 1)

        self.status_publisher = self.create_publisher(StatusText, '/mavros/statustext/send', 10)

        self.camera_trigger_pub = self.create_publisher(Bool, "/camera/trigger", 10)
        # Equivalent of:
        #   ros2 topic pub --once /camera/command std_msgs/msg/String "data: 'autofocus'"
        self.camera_command_pub = self.create_publisher(String, "/camera/command", 10)
        self.create_subscription(ParameterEvent, "/parameter_events", self.parameter_event_cb, 10)

        # Periods as parameters (October 2026); the defaults are the old constants. A photo
        # request faster than every 0.1 s is not useful, so smaller values (and 0) mean 0.1 s.
        self.capture_period_s = max(0.1, self.number_parameter('capture_period_s',
                                                               CAPTURE_PERIOD_SECONDS))
        self.autofocus_period_s = self.number_parameter('autofocus_period_s',
                                                        AUTOFOCUS_PERIOD_SECONDS)

        self.buffer_wp = -1
        self.waypoint_reached = 0
        # Single capture timer. None when not capturing; guards against stacking
        # multiple timers and against cancelling a timer that was never created.
        self.timer = None
        # Repeating autofocus timer, started by the same DigiCamCtrl that starts
        # capture. Same None-guard contract as self.timer above.
        self.autofocus_timer = None

        # buffer_wp is fetched asynchronously on this node's own executor.
        # It must never block __init__: main() would not reach rclpy.spin(),
        # leaving the node alive with its statustext subscription registered
        # but no callback ever running -- DigiCamCtrl silently dropped and no
        # photos taken, while every other node looks healthy.
        # It must also not run on a side thread: building a second node while
        # this one spins corrupts the executor wait set (IndexError: wait set
        # index too big). Client here (before spin), request from a timer.
        self.param_client = self.create_client(
            GetParameters, 'waypoint_manager/get_parameters')
        self.param_timer = self.create_timer(2.0, self.fetch_mission_indices)

    def number_parameter(self, name, default):
        """Declare a decimal ROS parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

        ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value. With a plain 5.0 default,
        `-p autofocus_period_s:=0` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
        start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then not a single survey photo is taken.
        dynamic_typing=True accepts any type; a value that is not a number (true, 'abc', a list)
        is reported in the log and the default is used, so a typo never costs the photos.
        """
        self.declare_parameter(name, default, ParameterDescriptor(dynamic_typing=True))
        value = self.get_parameter(name).value
        # bool is a kind of int in Python, but `:=true` is certainly not a number of seconds.
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
            return float(value)
        self.get_logger().error(
            f'Parameter {name}={value!r} is not a number: using the default {default:g}')
        return float(default)

    def fetch_mission_indices(self):
        # Retried by the timer until waypoint_manager shows up.
        if not self.param_client.service_is_ready():
            return
        if self.param_timer is not None:
            self.param_timer.cancel()
            self.destroy_timer(self.param_timer)
            self.param_timer = None

        req = GetParameters.Request()
        req.names = ['buffer_wp']
        self.param_client.call_async(req).add_done_callback(self._buffer_wp_cb)

    def _buffer_wp_cb(self, future):
        # -1 just means the trigger runs until shutdown instead of stopping at
        # buffer_wp. Capture must never depend on this lookup succeeding.
        try:
            values = future.result().values
            if values and values[0].type == 2:
                self.buffer_wp = values[0].integer_value
            else:
                self.get_logger().warning('buffer_wp unset, using -1')
                self.buffer_wp = -1
        except Exception as exc:
            self.get_logger().error(f'buffer_wp lookup failed ({exc}); using -1')
            self.buffer_wp = -1
        self.get_logger().info(f'buffer_wp = {self.buffer_wp}')

    def parameter_event_cb(self, msg: ParameterEvent):
        if msg.node == "/waypoint_manager":
            for changed_param in msg.changed_parameters:
                name = changed_param.name
                value = changed_param.value

                if name in {"buffer_wp"}:
                    # Non-blocking: call_async + done-callback on this executor.
                    self.fetch_mission_indices()
                    break

    def update_waypoint_reached(self, msg):
        self.waypoint_reached = msg.wp_seq
        if self.waypoint_reached == self.buffer_wp:
            self.stop_camera_trigger()

    def stop_camera_trigger(self):
        # Stopped FIRST, and deliberately outside the self.timer guard below:
        # the autofocus timer is (re)started by EVERY DigiCamCtrl while the
        # capture timer is only created by the first, so returning early on
        # `self.timer is None` would leak an autofocus timer that kept driving
        # the lens after the survey had already stopped.
        self.stop_autofocus_loop()
        # Guard: buffer_wp may be reached before any DigiCamCtrl ever started a
        # timer. Only cancel/destroy when a timer actually exists.
        if self.timer is None:
            return
        self.timer.cancel()
        self.destroy_timer(self.timer)
        self.timer = None
        self.last_before_rtl = -1
        self.get_logger().info("Camera trigger STOPPED")
        self.send_ack("Camera trigger STOPPED")

    def statustext_callback(self, msg):
        if "DigiCamCtrl" in msg.text:
            match = re.search(r"Mission:\s*(\d+)", msg.text)
            wp = match.group(1) if match else "?"
            # self.get_logger().info(f"Camera trigger from DigiCamCtrl at waypoint {wp}")
            # Set the lens up on arrival at the DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL waypoint:
            # rack to CAPTURE_ZOOM_X, then focus. siyi_node queues both onto
            # one lens worker; since October 2026 the photos started below
            # are taken in between its steps (photos have priority over lens
            # housekeeping) and are marked "zoom changing" until the rack ends.
            self.request_capture_setup(wp)
            # Keep re-focusing for the rest of the survey. Started BEFORE the
            # capture-timer guard below, so a repeat DigiCamCtrl that returns
            # early there still re-arms this loop if buffer_wp had stopped it.
            self.start_autofocus_loop()
            # Idempotent start: if a timer is already running, a second
            # DigiCamCtrl must NOT spawn another timer (that would stack the
            # capture rate and leak timers that cancel() can no longer reach).
            if self.timer is not None:
                return
            self.timer = self.create_timer(self.capture_period_s, self.trigger_camera)
            self.get_logger().info(
                f"Camera trigger STARTED (a photo every {self.capture_period_s:g} s)")
            self.send_ack(f"Camera trigger STARTED")

    def request_capture_setup(self, wp="?"):
        # siyi_node parses a bare (non-JSON) string as "<command> [parameter]".
        # "capture_setup" racks the lens to video_cam/config.py CAPTURE_ZOOM_X
        # and THEN focuses per FOCUS_MODE -- infinity by default for mapping,
        # since every subject at survey altitude is past the hyperfocal
        # distance. (Not "autofocus", which would hard-force AF and override
        # that setting.)
        #
        # Deliberately ONE command rather than a "zoom" followed by a "focus":
        # published separately the two would race on siyi_node's worker, and a
        # focus that won would be undone anyway by the autofocus CMD 0x0F
        # carries. It is also idempotent -- DigiCamCtrl repeats on every pass
        # through the waypoint, and a lens already at CAPTURE_ZOOM_X is left
        # alone rather than re-racked.
        self.camera_command_pub.publish(String(data="capture_setup"))
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Zoom + focus requested (DigiCamCtrl at waypoint {wp})")

    def start_autofocus_loop(self):
        """Autofocus every autofocus_period_s seconds until the survey stops (0 = never).

        Publishes the plain "autofocus" command, the one siyi_node handles
        AHEAD of its pipeline-busy guard and queues onto the single lens worker
        thread. Four properties of that path are what make a 5 s loop safe to
        run underneath 1 Hz captures:

          - it is not rejected while the pipeline is busy, which during a survey
            is almost continuously -- the trap that stopped the original
            one-shot autofocus here from ever taking effect;
          - a pass that lands while the DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL zoom rack is still
            travelling is SKIPPED by the worker's busy check rather than queued
            behind it, so passes can never stack up on a slow lens;
          - "autofocus" pins mode='auto' (CMD 0x04 at the frame centre) instead
            of following FOCUS_MODE, so this is a real AF cycle and not the
            drive-to-infinity that FOCUS_MODE='infinity' would otherwise do;
          - (October 2026) the pass no longer holds the camera while the lens
            settles, so photos keep coming, and siyi_node ignores it on cameras
            without autofocus (A8 mini).

        Idempotent, like the capture timer: DigiCamCtrl repeats on every pass
        through the waypoint and a second one must not spawn a second timer.
        """
        if self.autofocus_timer is not None:
            return
        if self.autofocus_period_s <= 0.0:
            return                     # switched off with -p autofocus_period_s:=0.0
        self.autofocus_timer = self.create_timer(
            self.autofocus_period_s, self.request_autofocus)
        self.get_logger().info(
            f"Autofocus loop STARTED (every {self.autofocus_period_s:g}s)")
        self.send_ack(f"Autofocus every {self.autofocus_period_s:.0f}s")

    def request_autofocus(self):
        self.camera_command_pub.publish(String(data="autofocus"))
        self.get_logger().info("Autofocus requested")

    def stop_autofocus_loop(self):
        # Same guard as stop_camera_trigger: buffer_wp can be reached before any
        # DigiCamCtrl ever started the loop.
        if self.autofocus_timer is None:
            return
        self.autofocus_timer.cancel()
        self.destroy_timer(self.autofocus_timer)
        self.autofocus_timer = None
        self.get_logger().info("Autofocus loop STOPPED")
        self.send_ack("Autofocus loop STOPPED")

    def trigger_camera(self):
        self.get_logger().info("Triggering camera...")
        self.camera_trigger_pub.publish(Bool(data=True))

    def send_ack(self, text):
        msg = StatusText()
        msg.severity = 6  # INFO
        msg.text = text
        self.status_publisher.publish(msg)
        self.get_logger().info(f"Status: {text}")
nodes.explain: The survey trigger node 'mission_camera_trigger': the photo timer, the autofocus timer, the buffer_wp waypoint it stops at, and publishers to the camera and to the ground station.

nodes.label: __init__
nodes.source:
def __init__(self):
        super().__init__("mission_camera_trigger")
        self.create_subscription(StatusText,'/mavros/statustext/recv', self.statustext_callback, qos_profile_sensor_data)
        self.create_subscription(WaypointReached, "/mavros/mission/reached", self.update_waypoint_reached, 1)

        self.status_publisher = self.create_publisher(StatusText, '/mavros/statustext/send', 10)

        self.camera_trigger_pub = self.create_publisher(Bool, "/camera/trigger", 10)
        # Equivalent of:
        #   ros2 topic pub --once /camera/command std_msgs/msg/String "data: 'autofocus'"
        self.camera_command_pub = self.create_publisher(String, "/camera/command", 10)
        self.create_subscription(ParameterEvent, "/parameter_events", self.parameter_event_cb, 10)

        # Periods as parameters (October 2026); the defaults are the old constants. A photo
        # request faster than every 0.1 s is not useful, so smaller values (and 0) mean 0.1 s.
        self.capture_period_s = max(0.1, self.number_parameter('capture_period_s',
                                                               CAPTURE_PERIOD_SECONDS))
        self.autofocus_period_s = self.number_parameter('autofocus_period_s',
                                                        AUTOFOCUS_PERIOD_SECONDS)

        self.buffer_wp = -1
        self.waypoint_reached = 0
        # Single capture timer. None when not capturing; guards against stacking
        # multiple timers and against cancelling a timer that was never created.
        self.timer = None
        # Repeating autofocus timer, started by the same DigiCamCtrl that starts
        # capture. Same None-guard contract as self.timer above.
        self.autofocus_timer = None

        # buffer_wp is fetched asynchronously on this node's own executor.
        # It must never block __init__: main() would not reach rclpy.spin(),
        # leaving the node alive with its statustext subscription registered
        # but no callback ever running -- DigiCamCtrl silently dropped and no
        # photos taken, while every other node looks healthy.
        # It must also not run on a side thread: building a second node while
        # this one spins corrupts the executor wait set (IndexError: wait set
        # index too big). Client here (before spin), request from a timer.
        self.param_client = self.create_client(
            GetParameters, 'waypoint_manager/get_parameters')
        self.param_timer = self.create_timer(2.0, self.fetch_mission_indices)
nodes.explain: Subscribes to /mavros/statustext/recv (sensor QoS), /mavros/mission/reached and /parameter_events, creates the publishers /mavros/statustext/send, /camera/trigger and /camera/command, and reads the two period parameters (capture_period_s 1.0, never below 0.1; autofocus_period_s 5.0). It also creates a client for waypoint_manager/get_parameters and a 2 s timer that asks for buffer_wp without ever blocking.
nodes.called_when: Once at start-up, from main().
nodes.effects: Nothing is sent until DigiCamCtrl arrives; buffer_wp starts at -1 (= never stop).

nodes.label: number_parameter
nodes.doc:
Declare a decimal ROS parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value. With a plain 5.0 default,
`-p autofocus_period_s:=0` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then not a single survey photo is taken.
dynamic_typing=True accepts any type; a value that is not a number (true, 'abc', a list)
is reported in the log and the default is used, so a typo never costs the photos.
nodes.source:
def number_parameter(self, name, default):
        """Declare a decimal ROS parameter that also accepts a whole number; return it as a float.

        ROS 2 gives a parameter the type of its default value. With a plain 5.0 default,
        `-p autofocus_period_s:=0` (a whole number, so an INTEGER) makes this node refuse to
        start (InvalidParameterTypeException), and then not a single survey photo is taken.
        dynamic_typing=True accepts any type; a value that is not a number (true, 'abc', a list)
        is reported in the log and the default is used, so a typo never costs the photos.
        """
        self.declare_parameter(name, default, ParameterDescriptor(dynamic_typing=True))
        value = self.get_parameter(name).value
        # bool is a kind of int in Python, but `:=true` is certainly not a number of seconds.
        if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
            return float(value)
        self.get_logger().error(
            f'Parameter {name}={value!r} is not a number: using the default {default:g}')
        return float(default)
nodes.explain: Declares a number parameter that accepts both whole numbers and decimals (dynamic typing) and returns it as a float. If the value is not a number (for example true or 'abc') it logs an error and uses the default instead of stopping the node, which would cost every survey photo.

nodes.label: fetch_mission_indices
nodes.source:
def fetch_mission_indices(self):
        # Retried by the timer until waypoint_manager shows up.
        if not self.param_client.service_is_ready():
            return
        if self.param_timer is not None:
            self.param_timer.cancel()
            self.destroy_timer(self.param_timer)
            self.param_timer = None

        req = GetParameters.Request()
        req.names = ['buffer_wp']
        self.param_client.call_async(req).add_done_callback(self._buffer_wp_cb)
nodes.explain: Asks waypoint_manager for its buffer_wp parameter without waiting (call_async). Until that service exists it just returns and the 2 s timer tries again; the first time the service is ready the timer is removed.
nodes.called_when: Every 2 s at start-up until waypoint_manager answers, and whenever waypoint_manager announces a new buffer_wp.

nodes.label: _buffer_wp_cb
nodes.explain: Receives waypoint_manager's answer: an integer value (type 2) becomes buffer_wp; a missing value or a failed call gives -1 (photos then run until shutdown). Logs 'buffer_wp = <n>' (9 on the simulator's runway mission).

nodes.label: parameter_event_cb
nodes.explain: Watches /parameter_events; when the node /waypoint_manager reports a changed buffer_wp (for example after a new mission was read) it fetches the new value.

nodes.label: update_waypoint_reached
nodes.explain: Remembers the waypoint the drone just reached (wp_seq of /mavros/mission/reached) and stops the photos when it equals buffer_wp.

nodes.label: stop_camera_trigger
nodes.source:
def stop_camera_trigger(self):
        # Stopped FIRST, and deliberately outside the self.timer guard below:
        # the autofocus timer is (re)started by EVERY DigiCamCtrl while the
        # capture timer is only created by the first, so returning early on
        # `self.timer is None` would leak an autofocus timer that kept driving
        # the lens after the survey had already stopped.
        self.stop_autofocus_loop()
        # Guard: buffer_wp may be reached before any DigiCamCtrl ever started a
        # timer. Only cancel/destroy when a timer actually exists.
        if self.timer is None:
            return
        self.timer.cancel()
        self.destroy_timer(self.timer)
        self.timer = None
        self.last_before_rtl = -1
        self.get_logger().info("Camera trigger STOPPED")
        self.send_ack("Camera trigger STOPPED")
nodes.explain: Stops the survey photos: first the autofocus loop, then (if it is running) the photo timer, and sends STATUSTEXT 'Camera trigger STOPPED'. Safe to call when nothing was started.
nodes.effects: STATUSTEXT 'Camera trigger STOPPED' (and 'Autofocus loop STOPPED').
