    0x01  firmware version     uint32 x2 (A8 mini) or x3 (ZR10)                  answered
    0x02  hardware id          12 ASCII chars, '6B..' ZR10 / '73..' A8 mini      answered
    0x04  auto focus           01                                                SILENT
    0x05  manual zoom          uint16 zoom*10 (zoom right now)                   answered
    0x06  manual focus         01                                                SILENT
    0x07  gimbal speed         01                                                answered
    0x08  centre               01                                                answered
    0x0A  system info          7/8 bytes, [3] record_sta, [4] gimbal mode        answered
    0x0C  photo / mode         never answered; photo -> 0x0B push (hook)         -
    0x0D  attitude             int16 x6: yaw,pitch,roll [deg*10], rates [deg/s*10] answered
    0x0E  set angles           int16 x3: CURRENT yaw,pitch,roll [deg*10]         answered
    0x0F  absolute zoom        01                                                answered
    0x16  max zoom             int part, tenths                                  SILENT
    0x18  current zoom         int part, tenths                                  SILENT
    0x19  gimbal mode          0 lock / 1 follow / 2 fpv                         SILENT
    0x41  single axis          as 0x0E (sent with cmd 0x0E by the A8 mini, 0x41 by the ZR10)
    0x48  format SD            never answered; deletes every photo (hook)        -

Unknown or malformed commands are ignored with a one-time warning; nothing here can crash the
emulator. Replies echo the request SEQ and use CTRL = 0x02 (ack_pack); video_cam checks neither.
nodes.explain: Decides what the pretend camera does and answers for every SIYI SDK command. It takes one decoded frame, changes the camera state or the gimbal, and returns the reply frame, or nothing when a real camera would stay silent. Taking photos, pushing the 0x0B 'photo done' message and formatting the SD card are handed to 'hooks', so this file has no sockets, threads or Gazebo and can be tested on its own.
nodes.how_it_fits: SiyiEmulator._udp_loop (emulator.py) passes every frame that arrives on UDP 37260 from the team's video_cam driver to CommandHandler.handle and sends the reply back. Rules it copies from the real camera: replies echo the request's sequence number and use CTRL 0x02; 0x0C (photo) and 0x48 (format) are never answered; in strict mode 0x04/0x06/0x16/0x18/0x19 are not answered (like an A8 mini); unknown or broken commands are ignored with a one-time warning.

nodes.label: HandlerHooks
nodes.doc:
What the command handler needs from the rest of the emulator. Override in the emulator/tests.

Default implementations do nothing (photos are not taken, attitude comes from the commanded
joints), which is enough for pure unit tests of the reply formats.
nodes.explain: The list of things the command handler needs from the rest of the emulator: the measured attitude, 'take a photo', 'push a 0x0B message' and 'format the SD card'. The default versions do nothing (no photo, attitude from the commanded joints, 0 files deleted), which is enough for unit tests; the emulator replaces them with _EmulatorHooks.

nodes.label: take_photo
nodes.doc: 0x0C func 0 arrived from ``addr``: take a photo and push 0x0B to ``addr``.
nodes.source:
def take_photo(self, addr: Addr) -> None:
        """0x0C func 0 arrived from ``addr``: take a photo and push 0x0B to ``addr``."""
nodes.explain: Placeholder for 'command 0x0C function 0 arrived: take a photo and later push 0x0B to this address'. The default does nothing.

nodes.label: CommandHandler
nodes.doc:
Turns SDK frames into state changes and replies.

Args:
    camera:  the :class:`CameraState` (model profile, zoom, strict flag, SD presence ...).
    gimbal:  the :class:`GimbalModel`.
    hooks:   :class:`HandlerHooks` (photo, 0x0B push, SD format, measured attitude).
    lock:    lock shared with the emulator's control loop (an RLock; created if None).
    clock:   monotonic time source in seconds (injectable for tests).
    logger:  ``logging.Logger``; ``log_commands=True`` logs every command at INFO.
nodes.explain: Turns SDK frames into state changes and replies. It holds the CameraState, the GimbalModel, the hooks, a lock shared with the emulator's control loop, a clock (replaceable in tests), a logger and a per-command counter, plus a table that maps each command number to the private method handling it.

nodes.label: __init__
nodes.signature: def __init__(self, camera: CameraState, gimbal: GimbalModel, hooks: Optional[HandlerHooks]=None, lock: Optional[threading.RLock]=None, clock: Callable[[], float]=time.monotonic, logger: Optional[logging.Logger]=None, log_commands: bool=False) -> None
nodes.source:
def __init__(self, camera: CameraState, gimbal: GimbalModel, hooks: Optional[HandlerHooks] = None,
                 lock: Optional[threading.RLock] = None, clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
                 logger: Optional[logging.Logger] = None, log_commands: bool = False) -> None:
        self.camera = camera
        self.gimbal = gimbal
        self.hooks = hooks or HandlerHooks(gimbal)
        self.lock = lock or threading.RLock()
        self.clock = clock
        self.log = logger or logging.getLogger("siyi_emulator.commands")
        self.log_commands = bool(log_commands)
        self.stats: Counter = Counter()          # cmd_id -> how many received
        self._warned: set = set()
        self._dispatch = {
            sp.CMD_HEARTBEAT: self._heartbeat,
            sp.CMD_FIRMWARE_VERSION: self._firmware,
            sp.CMD_HARDWARE_ID: self._hardware_id,
            sp.CMD_AUTO_FOCUS: self._ack_only,
            sp.CMD_MANUAL_ZOOM: self._manual_zoom,
            sp.CMD_MANUAL_FOCUS: self._ack_only,
            sp.CMD_GIMBAL_ROTATION: self._rotation,
            sp.CMD_CENTER: self._center,
            sp.CMD_SYSTEM_INFO: self._system_info,
            sp.CMD_FUNCTION_FEEDBACK: self._ignore_feedback,
            sp.CMD_CAPTURE: self._capture,
            sp.CMD_GIMBAL_ATTITUDE: self._attitude,
            sp.CMD_SET_ANGLES: self._set_angles,
            sp.CMD_ABSOLUTE_ZOOM: self._absolute_zoom,
            sp.CMD_ZOOM_RANGE: self._zoom_range,
            sp.CMD_CURRENT_ZOOM: self._current_zoom,
            sp.CMD_GIMBAL_MODE: self._gimbal_mode,
            sp.CMD_SINGLE_AXIS: self._single_axis,
            sp.CMD_FORMAT_SD: self._format_sd,
        }
nodes.explain: Stores the camera, gimbal, hooks (default HandlerHooks), lock (a new RLock if none), clock (time.monotonic) and logger, and builds the dispatch table for the 19 known commands 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04-0x08, 0x0A-0x0F, 0x16, 0x18, 0x19, 0x41 and 0x48.

nodes.label: handle
nodes.signature: def handle(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr=None) -> Optional[sp.Frame]
nodes.doc: Process one frame. Returns the reply frame, or None when the camera stays silent.
nodes.source:
def handle(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr = None) -> Optional[sp.Frame]:
        """Process one frame. Returns the reply frame, or None when the camera stays silent."""
        cmd = frame.cmd_id
        with self.lock:
            self.stats[cmd] += 1
        level = logging.INFO if self.log_commands else logging.DEBUG
        self.log.log(level, "SDK <- 0x%02X %s seq=%d data=[%s] from %s", cmd, frame.name, frame.seq,
                     sp.hexdump(frame.data), _fmt_addr(addr))
        func = self._dispatch.get(cmd)
        if func is None:
            self._warn_once(("unknown", cmd), f"SDK command 0x{cmd:02X} is not emulated - ignored (no reply)")
            return None
        if self.camera.is_silent(cmd):
            self._info_once(("strict", cmd), f"strict mode: not answering 0x{cmd:02X} ({frame.name}), "
                                             "like a real A8 mini")
            return None
        try:
            with self.lock:
                result = func(frame, addr)
        except (sp.FrameError, ValueError) as exc:
            self._warn_once(("bad", cmd), f"malformed 0x{cmd:02X} ({frame.name}) ignored: {exc}")
            return None
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive: never let a command crash the server
            self.log.error("error while handling 0x%02X (%s): %s", cmd, frame.name, exc)
            return None
        if result is None:
            return None
        reply_cmd, payload = result if isinstance(result, tuple) else (cmd, result)
        reply = sp.Frame(reply_cmd, bytes(payload), seq=frame.seq, ctrl=sp.CTRL_ACK_PACK)
        self.log.log(level, "SDK -> 0x%02X data=[%s]", reply_cmd, sp.hexdump(reply.data))
        return reply
nodes.explain: Handles one frame: counts it, logs it (at INFO when log_commands is true), looks up its handler, and stays silent for unknown commands (one-time warning) or strict-mode silent ones. It runs the handler under the lock; a malformed payload is ignored with a one-time warning and any other error is logged, so nothing can crash the server. A result becomes a reply frame with the same sequence number and CTRL 0x02; for 0x41 the handler may pick a different reply command.
nodes.called_when: for every frame that arrives on the SDK port (from video_cam, siyi_client or the tests)
nodes.inputs: a parsed Frame and the sender's (ip, port)
nodes.outputs: the reply Frame, or None for no answer

nodes.label: _heartbeat
nodes.signature: def _heartbeat(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.explain: Command 0x00 (heartbeat, a TCP-only message): logs once that it was ignored and sends no reply, like the real camera does over UDP.

nodes.label: _hardware_id
nodes.signature: def _hardware_id(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.source:
def _hardware_id(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult:
        return self.camera.hardware_id_payload()
nodes.explain: Command 0x02: answers with the 12-character hardware ID ('6B...' ZR10, '73...' A8 mini) that video_cam uses to detect the model.

nodes.label: _capture
nodes.signature: def _capture(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.doc: 0x0C: never acknowledged. func 0 = photo (repeated SEQ 0 is fine: no de-duplication).
nodes.explain: Command 0x0C, never answered directly. Function 0 = take a photo (hands it to hooks.take_photo; repeated sequence number 0 is fine). 1 toggles HDR, 2 toggles 'recording' (pushes 0x0B 'record failed' if there is no card), 3/4/5 switch the gimbal to lock/follow/FPV, 6/7/8 store a video-output setting, 9 points the camera straight down, 10 (zoom linkage) and unknown values are ignored with a one-time message.
nodes.called_when: every photo the team's video_cam takes (it sends the fixed packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce)
nodes.effects: starts a photo capture (Gazebo trigger, SD card file, 0x0B push) through the hooks

nodes.label: _attitude
nodes.signature: def _attitude(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.source:
def _attitude(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult:
        return sp.encode_attitude(*self.hooks.attitude())
nodes.explain: Command 0x0D: answers with the 12-byte attitude (yaw, pitch, roll and their rates) from hooks.attitude(), which in the emulator uses the joint angles measured in Gazebo.

nodes.label: _set_angles
nodes.signature: def _set_angles(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.source:
def _set_angles(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult:
        yaw, pitch = sp.decode_set_angles_request(frame.data)
        reply = self._current_angles()            # the ACK carries the attitude BEFORE moving
        self.gimbal.set_attitude(yaw, pitch)
        return reply
nodes.explain: Command 0x0E: reads the requested yaw and pitch, packs the attitude BEFORE moving as the reply (like the real camera), then sets the new gimbal target (clamped to -135..135 yaw, -90..25 pitch).

nodes.label: _absolute_zoom
nodes.signature: def _absolute_zoom(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.source:
def _absolute_zoom(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult:
        zoom = sp.decode_zoom(frame.data)
        target = self.camera.zoom.set_absolute(zoom, self.clock())
        if abs(target - zoom) > 0.05:
            self._info_once(("zoom_clamp", round(zoom, 1)),
                            f"zoom {zoom:.1f}x requested, {self.camera.profile.display_name} limit -> {target:.1f}x")
        return b"\x01"
nodes.explain: Command 0x0F: reads the requested zoom (whole part, tenths), starts the zoom travelling there (clamped to the model's maximum, which is 1x on the A8 mini or with --zoom survey), logs once if it had to clamp, and answers 01. video_cam's capture_setup asks for 5.0x here.

nodes.label: _current_zoom
nodes.signature: def _current_zoom(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult
nodes.source:
def _current_zoom(self, frame: sp.Frame, addr: Addr) -> HandlerResult:
        return sp.encode_zoom(self.camera.zoom.reported(self.clock()))
nodes.explain: Command 0x18: answers with the current zoom rounded to one decimal, as (whole part, tenths). video_cam polls this to confirm its zoom rack.

nodes.label: node.py
nodes.doc:
siyi_emulator/node.py -- PURPOSE: the ROS 2 entry point of the emulator (executable ``siyi_emulator``).
It declares one ROS parameter per EmulatorConfig setting (same names, see the README table), starts
the emulator core (emulator.py), forwards its log lines to the ROS logger, and publishes two
simulator-only topics that help the demo panel and debugging:

    /sim/camera/photo_info      std_msgs/String (JSON), one message per saved photo: SD name, URL, camera
                                pose, gimbal angles, zoom, field of view (reliable, transient local, depth 10)
    /sim/camera/emulator_state  std_msgs/String (JSON) at publish_state_hz: model, gimbal, zoom, Gazebo health

The emulator itself talks to video_cam over UDP/HTTP and to Gazebo over gz-transport, not over ROS.
Without ROS (rclpy missing, or with --standalone) the same executable runs the plain command line of
emulator.py, so unit tests and quick experiments need no ROS at all:

    ros2 run siyi_emulator siyi_emulator --ros-args -p camera_model:=a8mini -p strict:=true
    python3 -m siyi_emulator.node --standalone --bind-ip 127.0.0.3 --no-gazebo
nodes.explain: The ROS 2 front door of the camera emulator (the executable 'siyi_emulator'). It declares one ROS parameter per emulator setting (same names as EmulatorConfig, each with a short description for 'ros2 param describe'), starts the emulator core, forwards its log lines to the ROS logger, and publishes two simulator-only JSON topics. If ROS is missing, or with --standalone / --no-ros, the same program runs emulator.py's plain command line instead.
nodes.effects: publishes topic:/sim/camera/photo_info and topic:/sim/camera/emulator_state
nodes.how_it_fits: Started by the simulator's launch (sim.launch.py, or launch/siyi_emulator.launch.py) as node 'siyi_emulator'. The emulator talks to video_cam over UDP/HTTP and to Gazebo over gz-transport, not ROS; ROS is only used for the extras /sim/camera/photo_info (one JSON per saved photo, RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL, depth 10; read by sim_demo's score_run, demo_markers and truth_detector) and /sim/camera/emulator_state (JSON status at publish_state_hz, default 2 Hz).

nodes.label: main
nodes.doc: Entry point: ROS node when rclpy is available, plain command line otherwise (or --standalone).
nodes.explain: Entry point of 'ros2 run siyi_emulator siyi_emulator'. With --standalone or --no-ros it runs the plain emulator command line (emulator.main); if rclpy cannot be imported it says so and does the same; otherwise it runs the ROS node through _run_ros.
nodes.outputs: the process exit code (0 ok, 2 could not start)

nodes.label: media_server.py
nodes.doc:
siyi_emulator/media_server.py -- PURPOSE: the camera's media web server (TCP port 82), the one
video_cam uses to find and download each photo after the shutter fires. It serves the emulated SD
card (sd_card.py) with exactly the requests and JSON shapes video_cam depends on
(video_cam.md section 4.4 and 19.B; video_cam camera_interface.py:512-601):

    GET /cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getdirectories?media_type=0
        -> {"code":200,"success":true,"message":"","data":{"directories":[{"name":D,"path":D}]}}
    GET /cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getmedialist?media_type=0&path=D&start=0&count=N
        -> {"code":200,"success":true,"message":"","data":{"list":[{"name":"IMG_0001.jpg",
            "url":"http://<host>/D/IMG_0001.jpg","size":<bytes>}, ...],"total":<all files>}}
           oldest first; start/count slice the list, "total" always counts every file
    GET /cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getmediacount?media_type=0&path=D
        -> {"code":200,"success":true,"message":"","data":{"count":N}}
    GET /D/IMG_0001.jpg   -> 200 image/jpeg bytes (404 if missing)
    GET /                 -> a small HTML page listing the card (handy in a web browser)

media_type=1 (videos) answers with empty lists. Errors use the SIYI shape with "success": false
and code 400 ("Invalid media type", "path not exist"), like SIYI's media API chapter.
The double slash of SIYI's documented base URL (http://host:82//cgi-bin/...) is accepted.

The "url" of each photo uses the Host header of the request (what the client used to reach us),
so the link always works for that client; video_cam also rewrites 192.168.144.25 -> camera_ip.
Standard library only (http.server), one thread per connection, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive.
nodes.explain: The pretend camera's little web server on TCP port 82, the same one the real SIYI camera has. After the shutter fires, the team's video_cam driver uses it to find the newest photo and download it. It answers exactly the requests and JSON shapes video_cam depends on: getdirectories, getmedialist (oldest first), getmediacount, the photo files themselves, plus a small HTML page at / for people with a browser. Standard library only (http.server).
nodes.effects: opens a TCP listening socket on bind_ip:82 (needs net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=80)
nodes.how_it_fits: Serves the emulated SD card (sd_card.py) started by emulator.py. video_cam polls http://192.168.144.25:82/cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getmedialist?media_type=0&path=101SIYI_IMG&start=0&count=9999 every 0.5 s (up to 15 s), then GETs the photo URL. Each photo URL uses the Host header the client used, so the link always works for that client.

nodes.label: sim.launch.py
nodes.doc:
sim_bringup/launch/sim.launch.py -- PURPOSE: start the whole ASTRA simulator with one command.

    ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py [world:=runway|suas_field|/path/world.sdf] [camera_model:=zr10|a8mini]
        [gui:=true] [rviz:=true] [panel:=true] [headless_rendering:=false] [detector:=real|truth]
        [sitl:=true] [sitl_instance:=0] [mavproxy:=true] [windows_gcs:=true] [emulator:=true] [payload:=true]
        [bridge:=true] [markers:=true] [follow:=true]   (and more, see `ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py --show-args`)

What it starts, in this order (every part can be switched off with its argument):
  1. Gazebo server (gz sim -s -r) with the world, and the Gazebo window (gz sim -g) with the world's own
     layout (its <gui> section) or ours (config/gazebo_gui.config): big 3D view + a live camera POV panel.
     The window is a separate program: closing it does NOT stop the simulation. gui_camera:=window moves the
     camera picture into its own small Gazebo window (config/gazebo_camera_window.config) and opens the main
     window without the panel (config/gazebo_gui_no_camera.config); gui_camera:=off leaves the camera out.
  2. The drone: sim_models' model.sdf.xacro is run through xacro (photo size from camera_model, SITL
     port from sitl_instance) and spawned as entity "iris" at the world's spawn pose.
  3. ArduCopter SITL (the Pixhawk's firmware on the PC), started only when the drone's ArduPilotPlugin
     has opened UDP 9002+10*I, in ~/.astra_sim/sitl_I<I> (eeprom.bin = saved parameters persists there).
  4. MAVProxy, started when SITL listens on TCP 5760+10*I, with three outputs:
     udp 127.0.0.1:14550 ground station / our scripts, :14552 MAVROS (./launcher.sh sim), :14553 demo panel,
     plus (inside WSL, windows_gcs:=true) a fourth copy for Mission Planner / QGroundControl on WINDOWS:
     udp <Windows host>:14550, the address found at every start (sim_paths.windows_gcs_output).
  5. The SIYI camera emulator (pretends to be the camera at 192.168.144.25; its SD card is
     ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<I>) and the payload release node.
  6. ros_gz_bridge: /sim/camera/image, /sim/camera/camera_info, /sim/camera/photo, /sim/drone/odometry,
     /sim/gimbal/joint_states into ROS 2; odom_tf (drone TF for RViz).
  7. The demo nodes, through sim_demo's own launch file (demo_nodes.launch.py): demo_markers (RViz
     markers), demo_panel (the demo window), truth_detector (only with detector:=truth) and score_run
     (only with score:=true: records the run, writes the score report when the drone lands).
  8. RViz with rviz/sim.rviz (big camera POV + 3D view with markers), and gz_follow, which makes the
     Gazebo 3D view follow the drone once the window and the drone are there.
When a simulation package is not built yet, the launch says so and uses a stand-in (ardupilot_gazebo's
iris_runway world / iris_with_gimbal drone) or skips that part, instead of crashing.
The team's flight stack is NOT started here: run ./launcher.sh sim (or simulation/scripts/demo.sh).

Plug-and-play (package sim_plugins; docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md and docs/simulation/ARDUPILOT.md): the
arguments at the end of ARGUMENTS swap one piece for another, and every one of them defaults to today's
behaviour (with all of them at their defaults the commands are exactly the ones before they existed):
  profile:=NAME|FILE     a plug-in profile: its values for every argument left at its default, plus its
                         custom camera and its extras that start with the simulator
  autopilot:=external, sitl_version:=4.7.1, sitl_source:=/opt/ardupilot, sitl_param_files:=my.param, ...
                         which ArduCopter flies the drone (see sim_plugins/autopilot.py)
  mavlink_master, gcs_out, mavros_out, extra_outs, camera_bind, fdm_addr
                         where MAVLink goes and where the camera / the physics link listen (Docker, 2 PCs)
sim_plugins is imported only when one of these arguments is used, so the default start never needs it.
nodes.explain: The launch file that starts the whole simulator with one command (ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py). It declares 56 launch arguments (world, camera_model, gui, gui_env, rviz, panel, detector, sitl_instance, ports, windows_gcs, emulator, payload, bridge, follow, plug-in profile ...) and then, in order, starts the Gazebo server and window, spawns the drone 'iris', starts ArduCopter SITL and MAVProxy behind wait_then_exec, the SIYI camera emulator, payload_release, the ROS bridge + odom_tf, the sim_demo nodes, the Mission Planner camera stream (pov_server), RViz and gz_follow. A missing simulator package never crashes it: it prints a note and uses a stand-in or skips that part.
nodes.effects: starts processes gz sim, arducopter, mavproxy.py, siyi_emulator, payload_release, parameter_bridge, odom_tf, demo nodes, rviz2, gz_follow; writes ~/.astra_sim/generated/* and ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml; sets GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH, GZ_PARTITION=astra_sim, ASTRA_SIM_SESSION
nodes.how_it_fits: It is the simulator half of a run (the team code half is ./launcher.sh sim with team_stack.launch.py). demo.sh and start_sim.sh call it; it writes ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml so status.sh, demo.sh and START OVER know what is running.

nodes.label: share_or_none
nodes.doc: Installed share folder of a package, or None (no exception) when it is not built/sourced.
nodes.explain: Asks ROS where a package's installed 'share' folder is (for example sim_models or sim_worlds) and returns that path. If the package is not built or not sourced it returns None instead of crashing, so the launch can print a friendly note and carry on.
nodes.inputs: package name

nodes.label: _running_in_wsl
nodes.doc: True inside Windows' WSL2 (its kernel version string mentions Microsoft).
nodes.explain: Reads /proc/version and returns True when the Linux kernel's version text mentions 'microsoft', which means the simulator runs inside Windows' WSL2. Returns False if the file cannot be read.

nodes.label: _launch_setup
nodes.doc: Build every action from the resolved launch arguments (runs once when the launch starts).
nodes.source:
def _launch_setup(context):
    """Build every action from the resolved launch arguments (runs once when the launch starts)."""
    cfg = {name: LaunchConfiguration(name).perform(context) for name, _, _ in ARGUMENTS}
    actions = []

    def say(msg):
        actions.append(LogInfo(msg=f'[sim] {msg}'))

    def fatal(msg):
        actions.append(LogInfo(msg=f'[sim] ERROR: {msg}'))
        actions.append(EmitEvent(event=Shutdown(reason=msg)))
        return actions

    # ---- 0. arguments --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A plug-in profile (sim_plugins) first: it fills in every argument the user left at its default.
    profile_rp = None
    if cfg['profile'].strip():
        try:
            from sim_plugins import launch_support, plan as plug_plan
        except ImportError:
            return fatal('profile:= needs the sim_plugins package: build it with simulation/setup/03_build.sh')
        try:
            profile_rp = launch_support.load_profile(cfg['profile'])
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - sim_plugins.profiles.ProfileError: every problem in words
            return fatal(f'the profile "{cfg["profile"]}" cannot be used:\n{exc}')
        say(f'plug-in profile "{profile_rp.name}" ({profile_rp.source})')
        arg_defaults = {name: default for name, default, _ in ARGUMENTS}
        for name, _, new in launch_support.apply_profile_args(cfg, arg_defaults,
                                                              plug_plan.sim_args_full(profile_rp)):
            say(f'  from the profile: {name}:={new}')
        for warning in profile_rp.warnings:
            say(f'  profile warning: {warning.text()}')
    try:
        instance = int(cfg['sitl_instance'])
        ports = sp.sitl_ports(instance)
        gcs_port, mavros_port, panel_port = (int(cfg[k]) for k in ('gcs_port', 'mavros_port', 'panel_port'))
    except ValueError as exc:
        return fatal(f'bad number in the launch arguments: {exc}')
    camera = cfg['camera_model'].strip().lower().replace('-', '').replace('_', '')
    if camera not in sp.CAMERA_PROFILES:
        say(f'camera_model "{cfg["camera_model"]}" is unknown (use zr10 or a8mini); using zr10')
        camera = 'zr10'
    detector = cfg['detector'].strip().lower()
    if detector not in ('real', 'truth', 'custom'):
        say(f'detector "{cfg["detector"]}" is unknown (use real, truth or custom); using real')
        detector = 'real'
    # custom = a teammate's detector, started with the team stack (team_stack.launch.py). For the demo nodes it
    # counts as a real detector: no truth_detector, no answer-key banner.
    demo_detector = 'truth' if detector == 'truth' else 'real'
    # The autopilot slot (sim_plugins.autopilot), only when one of its arguments is not at its default.
    arg_defaults = {name: default for name, default, _ in ARGUMENTS}
    external = cfg['autopilot'].strip().lower() in ('external', 'remote')
    plug_ap = ap_settings = None
    if any(cfg[n].strip() != arg_defaults[n] for n in PLUGIN_AUTOPILOT_ARGS):
        try:
            from sim_plugins import autopilot as plug_ap
        except ImportError:
            return fatal('the autopilot arguments (autopilot, sitl_version, sitl_source, sitl_param_files, '
                         'mavlink_master, fdm_addr ...) need the sim_plugins package: build it with '
                         'simulation/setup/03_build.sh')
        ap_settings = plug_ap.settings_from_launch(cfg)
    fdm_addr = cfg['fdm_addr'].strip() or ('0.0.0.0' if external else '')
    gui = sp.truthy(cfg['gui'])
    # Windows started below must not inherit Qt plugin paths from a Python wheel (OpenCV sets them when
    # something imports cv2), or Gazebo / RViz / the panel abort with "Could not load the Qt platform plugin".
    for name in sp.scrub_foreign_qt_env():
        say(f'removed {name} from the environment (it pointed into a Python package, e.g. OpenCV\'s Qt)')
    state_home = Path(sp.expand(cfg['run_dir'])) if cfg['run_dir'] else sp.sim_home()
    gen_dir = sp.generated_dir(state_home)
    gen_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # ---- 1. which packages / tools are there ---------------------------------------------------
    shares = {pkg: share_or_none(pkg) for pkg in ('sim_models', 'sim_worlds', 'siyi_emulator', 'sim_demo',
                                                   'sim_bringup')}
    for pkg in ('sim_models', 'sim_worlds', 'siyi_emulator', 'sim_demo'):
        if not shares[pkg]:
            say(f'package {pkg} is not built: its part is replaced by a stand-in or skipped '
                '(build everything with simulation/setup/03_build.sh)')
    ag_dir = sp.find_ardupilot_gazebo()
    if not ag_dir:
        say('ArduPilot Gazebo plugin not found (~/ardupilot_gazebo/build or /opt/ardupilot_gazebo/build): '
            'the drone cannot talk to SITL. Run simulation/setup/02_setup_ardupilot.sh')

    # ---- 2. world ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    world_cfg = sp.load_world_config(cfg['world'], shares['sim_worlds'])
    if not world_cfg.world_file and (shares['sim_worlds'] is None or cfg['world'] in ('standin', 'iris_runway')):
        for n in world_cfg.notes:
            say(n)
        world_cfg = sp.standin_world_config(ag_dir, gen_dir)
    for n in world_cfg.notes:
        say(n)

    # Gazebo looks for model:// folders in GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH and for system plugins (the
    # ArduPilotPlugin) in GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH.
    resource = []
    if shares['sim_models']:
        resource.append(os.path.join(shares['sim_models'], 'models'))
    for wdir in dict.fromkeys(d for d in (world_cfg.worlds_dir, shares['sim_worlds']) if d):
        resource += [os.path.join(wdir, 'models'), os.path.join(wdir, 'worlds')]
    if ag_dir:
        resource += [os.path.join(ag_dir, 'models'), os.path.join(ag_dir, 'worlds')]
    actions.append(_prepend_env('GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH', [p for p in resource if os.path.isdir(p)]))
    if ag_dir:
        actions.append(_prepend_env('GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH', [os.path.join(ag_dir, 'build')]))
    actions.append(SetEnvironmentVariable('GZ_VERSION', 'harmonic'))
    if not world_cfg.world_file:
        return fatal(f'no world file for world:={cfg["world"]}. Known worlds: runway, suas_field '
                     '(sim_worlds/config/<name>.yaml), or give a path to an .sdf file.')
    if ' ' in world_cfg.world_file:
        say('WARNING: the world path contains a space; Gazebo may not open it. Use the Linux-side copy '
            '(simulation/setup/03_build.sh) instead of /mnt/... paths.')
    world_name = sp.world_name_from_sdf(Path(world_cfg.world_file).read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'))
    spawn = dict(world_cfg.spawn)
    for key in ('x', 'y', 'z', 'yaw'):
        if cfg[key] != '':
            spawn[key] = float(cfg[key])
    say(f'world "{world_cfg.name}" ({world_name}): {world_cfg.world_file}')
    say(f'SITL home {world_cfg.home}; spawn x={spawn["x"]:.2f} y={spawn["y"]:.2f} z={spawn["z"]:.2f} '
        f'yaw={spawn["yaw"]:.3f} rad; mission {world_cfg.mission or "-"}; truth {world_cfg.truth or "-"}')

    # A second simulator with the same SITL instance would steal the ports: refuse early and clearly.
    if sp.truthy(cfg['sitl']):
        busy = []
        if ports['fdm'] in bound_ports('udp'):
            busy.append(f'UDP {ports["fdm"]}')
        if ports['serial0'] in bound_ports('tcp'):
            busy.append(f'TCP {ports["serial0"]}')
        if busy:
            return fatal(f'SITL instance {instance} ports are already in use ({", ".join(busy)}): another '
                         'simulator is still running. Stop it with simulation/scripts/stop_sim.sh, or start '
                         f'this one with sitl_instance:={instance + 1}.')

    # ---- 3. drone model ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    model_file, notes = ('', [])
    if shares['sim_models'] or cfg['model']:
        model_file, notes = sp.generate_drone_sdf(shares['sim_models'], camera, instance, gen_dir, cfg['model'])
    standin_model = False
    if not model_file:
        more = []
        model_file, more = sp.standin_drone_sdf(ag_dir, instance, gen_dir)
        notes += more
        standin_model = bool(model_file)
    for n in notes:
        say(n)
    if fdm_addr and model_file and plug_ap is not None:
        # The plugin binds its JSON physics port on <fdm_addr> (127.0.0.1 in the model): 0.0.0.0 lets a SITL on
        # another computer / container reach it. The plugin answers whoever sends, so nothing else changes.
        text, found = plug_ap.patch_plugin_fdm_addr(Path(model_file).read_text(encoding='utf-8'), fdm_addr)
        if found:
            Path(model_file).write_text(text, encoding='utf-8')
            say(f'drone ArduPilot plugin: physics port UDP {ports["fdm"]} bound on {fdm_addr}')
        else:
            say(f'WARNING: fdm_addr:={fdm_addr} but the drone model has no ArduPilotPlugin to change')
    say(f'camera profile: {sp.CAMERA_PROFILES[camera]["label"]}')

    # ---- 4. Gazebo server + window ---------------------------------------------------------------
    gz_server = ['gz', 'sim', '-s', '-r', '-v', cfg['gz_verbosity']]
    if sp.truthy(cfg['headless_rendering']):
        gz_server.append('--headless-rendering')
    gz_server.append(world_cfg.world_file)
    server = ExecuteProcess(cmd=gz_server, name='gz_server', output='screen',
                            sigterm_timeout='10', sigkill_timeout='5')
    actions.append(server)
    actions.append(RegisterEventHandler(OnProcessExit(target_action=server, on_exit=[
        LogInfo(msg='[sim] the Gazebo server stopped -> stopping the whole simulator'),
        EmitEvent(event=Shutdown(reason='Gazebo server exited'))])))

    if gui:
        gui_cmd = ['gz', 'sim', '-g', '-v', cfg['gz_verbosity']]
        layout = cfg['gui_config'].strip()
        world_has_gui = re.search(r'<gui[\s>]', Path(world_cfg.world_file).read_text(encoding='utf-8',
                                                                                    errors='replace')) is not None
        # gui_camera: panel (as before) | window (own small window) | off. See ARGUMENTS and TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
        gui_camera = cfg['gui_camera'].strip().lower() or 'panel'
        if gui_camera not in ('panel', 'window', 'off'):
            say(f'gui_camera "{cfg["gui_camera"]}" is unknown (use panel, window or off); using panel')
            gui_camera = 'panel'

        def bringup_config(name):
            """Path of one of our layout files, patched for the stand-in drone's camera topic when needed."""
            path = os.path.join(shares['sim_bringup'] or '', 'config', name)
            if os.path.isfile(path) and standin_model:
                # The stand-in drone's camera publishes on a different topic: use a patched copy.
                text = Path(path).read_text(encoding='utf-8').replace(
                    '/sim/camera/video/image', sp.bridge_entries(True, world_name)[0]['gz_topic_name'])
                path = str(gen_dir / name.replace('.config', '_standin.config'))
                Path(path).write_text(text, encoding='utf-8')
            return path if os.path.isfile(path) else ''

        if gui_camera != 'panel' and layout in ('', 'world', 'astra'):
            main_layout = bringup_config('gazebo_gui_no_camera.config')
            if main_layout:
                gui_cmd += ['--gui-config', main_layout]
                say(f'Gazebo window: our layout without the camera panel (gui_camera:={gui_camera})')
        elif layout in ('', 'world') and world_has_gui:
            say('Gazebo window: the world\'s own layout (its <gui> section)')
        elif layout in ('', 'world', 'astra'):
            ours = bringup_config('gazebo_gui.config')
            if ours:
                gui_cmd += ['--gui-config', ours]
        elif layout == 'default':
            stock = '/usr/share/gz/gz-sim8/gui/gui.config'      # Gazebo's own layout (ignores the world's)
            if os.path.isfile(stock):
                gui_cmd += ['--gui-config', stock]
        else:
            gui_cmd += ['--gui-config', sp.expand(layout)]
        # gui_env: extra environment for this window only (e.g. QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic); "" changes nothing.
        window_env = _gui_env()
        extra_env, bad_env = sp.parse_env_assignments(cfg['gui_env'])
        window_env.update(extra_env)
        if extra_env:
            say('Gazebo window extra environment (gui_env): ' + ', '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k, v in extra_env.items()))
        if bad_env:
            say(f'gui_env: ignored {", ".join(bad_env)} (write NAME=value, items separated by commas)')
        window = ExecuteProcess(cmd=gui_cmd, name='gz_gui', output='screen', additional_env=window_env)
        actions.append(window)
        actions.append(RegisterEventHandler(OnProcessExit(target_action=window, on_exit=[
            LogInfo(msg='[sim] the Gazebo window was closed; the simulation keeps running '
                        '(stop everything with Ctrl+C or simulation/scripts/stop_sim.sh)')])))
        if gui_camera == 'window':
            # The live camera in its OWN Gazebo program: no 3D view draws in that program, so its panel cannot
            # pick up 3D-view pictures (the fault this option avoids). Closing it changes nothing else.
            camera_layout = bringup_config('gazebo_camera_window.config')
            if camera_layout:
                actions.append(ExecuteProcess(cmd=['gz', 'sim', '-g', '-v', cfg['gz_verbosity'], '--gui-config',
                                                   camera_layout], name='gz_camera_window', output='screen',
                                              additional_env=window_env))
                say('Gazebo camera window: the live gimbal camera in its own small window (gui_camera:=window)')
            else:
                say('gui_camera:=window but config/gazebo_camera_window.config is missing (rebuild sim_bringup)')

    # ---- 5. spawn the drone ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    if model_file:
        actions.append(Node(
            package='ros_gz_sim', executable='create', name='spawn_drone', output='screen',
            arguments=['-file', model_file, '-name', sp.DRONE_ENTITY,
                       '-x', str(spawn['x']), '-y', str(spawn['y']), '-z', str(spawn['z']),
                       '-Y', str(spawn['yaw'])]))
    else:
        say('NO DRONE MODEL (neither sim_models nor ardupilot_gazebo found): nothing is spawned')

    waiter = executable_or_none('sim_bringup', 'wait_then_exec')

    # ---- 6. ArduCopter SITL ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    run_dir = sp.sitl_run_dir(instance, state_home)
    win_out = ''            # MAVProxy's extra output for a ground station on Windows ('' = none), set in step 7
    sitl_used = ''          # the arducopter program that was started (written into the state file)
    ap_plan = None          # sim_plugins AutopilotPlan: another version / source tree / parameter files / external
    if ap_settings is not None and ap_settings.needs_plan():
        if not ap_settings.run_dir:
            # Another version / tree / parameter set keeps its own saved parameters (eeprom.bin) in its own
            # folder, so switching back and forth never mixes them.
            tag = plug_ap.flavour_tag(ap_settings)
            ap_settings.run_dir = str(state_home / f'sitl_I{instance}_{tag}') if tag else str(run_dir)
        ap_plan = plug_ap.plan_autopilot(ap_settings, params_out_dir=gen_dir / 'params',
                                         binary_finder=lambda: sp.find_sitl_binary(''))
        run_dir = Path(ap_plan.run_dir)
        say(f'autopilot: {ap_plan.how}')
        if ap_plan.errors:
            return fatal('the autopilot cannot start: ' + ' | '.join(ap_plan.errors))

    def add_mavproxy(waiter_prefix):
        """Step 7: MAVProxy and its outputs. waiter_prefix = the wait_then_exec words ([] = start at once)."""
        nonlocal win_out
        mavproxy = sp.find_mavproxy(cfg['mavproxy_bin'])
        if not mavproxy:
            say('MAVProxy not found (~/sitl/venv/bin/mavproxy.py or mavproxy.py on PATH): '
                f'connect a ground station to TCP 127.0.0.1:{ports["serial0"]} yourself')
            return
        # Mission Planner / QGroundControl on WINDOWS cannot hear the 127.0.0.1 outputs (in WSL2's
        # NAT networking Ubuntu is a separate computer behind Windows): give them their own copy,
        # sent to the Windows host. The 127.0.0.1:gcs_port output our scripts use is unchanged.
        win_out, win_notes = sp.windows_gcs_output(cfg['windows_gcs'], cfg['windows_gcs_addr'],
                                                   local_ports=(gcs_port, mavros_port, panel_port))
        for n in win_notes:
            say(n)
        # Plug-and-play outputs (Docker / two computers); all default to today's 127.0.0.1 ports.
        master = cfg['mavlink_master'].strip() or f'tcp:127.0.0.1:{ports["serial0"]}'
        gcs_out = cfg['gcs_out'].strip() or f'udp:127.0.0.1:{gcs_port}'
        mavros_out = cfg['mavros_out'].strip() or f'udp:127.0.0.1:{mavros_port}'
        extra_outs = [o.strip() for o in cfg['extra_outs'].split(',') if o.strip()]
        master_args = plug_ap.mavproxy_master_args(master, external) if plug_ap else ['--master', master]
        mp_cmd = [mavproxy, *master_args,
                  '--out', gcs_out, '--out', mavros_out,
                  '--out', f'udp:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}', *[w for o in extra_outs for w in ('--out', o)],
                  *(['--out', win_out] if win_out else []),
                  '--daemon', '--state-basedir', str(run_dir), '--logfile', 'mav.tlog']
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        actions.append(ExecuteProcess(
            cmd=[*waiter_prefix, *mp_cmd],
            cwd=str(run_dir), name='mavproxy', output='screen', sigterm_timeout='5', sigkill_timeout='3'))
        say(f'MAVProxy outputs: ground station {gcs_out}, MAVROS {mavros_out} '
            f'(fcu_url udp://:{mavros_port}@localhost:{mavros_port}), demo panel udp:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}'
            + ''.join(f', extra {o}' for o in extra_outs)
            + (f', Windows ground station {win_out}' if win_out else '')
            + (f'; MAVLink from {master}' if cfg['mavlink_master'].strip() else ''))

    if external:
        # autopilot:=external: ArduCopter runs in another container / on another PC. Nothing to start here
        # except MAVProxy, which picks up its MAVLink and shares it out exactly like for the local SITL.
        say(f'autopilot:=external: no SITL here. Start ArduCopter on the other computer, e.g.: '
            f'{plug_ap.remote_command(ap_settings, world_cfg.home)}')
        if sp.truthy(cfg['mavproxy']):
            add_mavproxy([])
        else:
            say(f'mavproxy:=false: connect your ground station / MAVROS to {ap_plan.mavlink_master} yourself')
    elif sp.truthy(cfg['sitl']):
        astra_parm = os.path.join(shares['sim_models'], 'config', 'astra_sitl.parm') if shares['sim_models'] else None
        if ap_plan is None:         # today's code path (also sitl_bin:= / sitl_wipe:= on their own)
            sitl_bin = sp.find_sitl_binary(cfg['sitl_bin'])
            defaults, notes = sp.sitl_defaults(astra_parm)
        else:                       # another version / source tree / extra parameter files (sim_plugins)
            sitl_bin = ap_plan.binary
            defaults = ap_plan.defaults_list(astra_parm, finder=sp.find_param_file)
            notes = list(ap_plan.notes)
            say(f'autopilot: {plug_ap.describe(ap_plan, ap_settings)}')
        for n in notes:
            say(n)
        if not sitl_bin:
            say('ArduCopter SITL not found ($ARDUPILOT_SITL_BIN, ~/sitl/arducopter, '
                '/opt/ardupilot/build/sitl/bin/arducopter): run simulation/setup/02_setup_ardupilot.sh')
        elif not waiter:
            say('sim_bringup wait_then_exec is not installed (rebuild sim_bringup): SITL not started')
        else:
            run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            sitl_used = sitl_bin
            sitl_cmd = [sitl_bin, '--model', 'JSON', '-I', str(instance), '--home', world_cfg.home]
            if defaults:
                sitl_cmd += ['--defaults', ','.join(defaults)]
            if sp.truthy(cfg['sitl_wipe']):
                sitl_cmd.append('-w')
            # SITL may only start once the drone's ArduPilotPlugin listens (Gazebo up + drone spawned).
            actions.append(ExecuteProcess(
                cmd=[waiter, '--udp-port', str(ports['fdm']), '--timeout', '420', '--label', 'sitl', '--', *sitl_cmd],
                cwd=str(run_dir), name='sitl', output='screen', sigterm_timeout='5', sigkill_timeout='5'))
            say(f'SITL instance {instance}: MAVLink TCP {ports["serial0"]}, Gazebo link UDP {ports["fdm"]}, '
                f'run folder {run_dir} (wait ~30 s after boot before arming: "Arm: Gyros inconsistent" is normal)')

            # ---- 7. MAVProxy ----------------------------------------------------------------------
            if sp.truthy(cfg['mavproxy']):
                add_mavproxy([waiter, '--tcp-port', str(ports['serial0']), '--timeout', '480', '--delay', '1',
                              '--label', 'mavproxy', '--'])
            else:
                say(f'mavproxy:=false: SITL waits for a ground station on TCP 127.0.0.1:{ports["serial0"]}')
    elif sp.truthy(cfg['mavproxy']):
        say('sitl:=false: MAVProxy is not started either (it has nothing to talk to)')

    # ---- 8. SIYI camera emulator + payload release ---------------------------------------------
    camera_ip = cfg['camera_ip'].strip() or sp.DEFAULT_CAMERA_IP
    if sp.truthy(cfg['emulator']):
        if executable_or_none('siyi_emulator', 'siyi_emulator'):
            # The emulator's own parameter file first, then our overrides (later entries win).
            emu_params = []
            emu_yaml = os.path.join(shares['siyi_emulator'] or '', 'config', 'siyi_emulator.yaml')
            if os.path.isfile(emu_yaml):
                emu_params.append(emu_yaml)
            overrides = {'camera_model': camera, 'camera_ip': camera_ip,
                         'sd_card_dir': str(state_home / f'sd_card_I{instance}')}
            if cfg['camera_max_zoom'].strip():
                try:
                    overrides['max_zoom'] = float(cfg['camera_max_zoom'])
                    say(f'camera max zoom := {overrides["max_zoom"]:g}x (photos keep '
                        f'{"the full view" if overrides["max_zoom"] <= 1 else "the zoomed view"})')
                except ValueError:
                    say(f'camera_max_zoom "{cfg["camera_max_zoom"]}" is not a number; using the camera default')
            # Plug-and-play (camera slot): where it listens (0.0.0.0 in containers) and the strict A8 mini mode.
            if cfg['camera_bind'].strip():
                overrides['bind_ip'] = cfg['camera_bind'].strip()
                say(f'camera emulator listens on {overrides["bind_ip"]} (camera_bind)')
            if cfg['camera_strict'].strip():
                overrides['strict'] = sp.truthy(cfg['camera_strict'])
                say(f'camera emulator strict mode := {str(overrides["strict"]).lower()}')
            emu_params.append(overrides)
            actions.append(Node(package='siyi_emulator', executable='siyi_emulator', name='siyi_emulator',
                                output='screen', parameters=emu_params))
            if not cfg['camera_bind'].strip() and not _address_exists(camera_ip):
                say(f'the camera address {camera_ip} does not exist on this PC: the emulator will use its '
                    'fallback address and the team\'s video_cam will NOT reach it. Add it with '
                    'simulation/setup/camera_ip_alias.sh (start_sim.sh and demo.sh do this for you).')
        else:
            say('siyi_emulator is not built: no SIYI camera on the network (video_cam captures will fail)')
    if sp.truthy(cfg['payload']):
        if executable_or_none('sim_models', 'payload_release'):
            actions.append(Node(package='sim_models', executable='payload_release', name='payload_release',
                                output='screen'))
        else:
            say('sim_models payload_release is not built: payloads will not fall')

    # ---- 9. ROS <-> Gazebo bridge + drone TF ----------------------------------------------------
    if sp.truthy(cfg['bridge']):
        entries = sp.bridge_entries(standin=standin_model, world_name=world_name)
        bridge_yaml = sp.write_bridge_yaml(entries, gen_dir / f'bridge_I{instance}.yaml')
        actions.append(Node(package='ros_gz_bridge', executable='parameter_bridge', name='sim_bridge',
                            output='screen', parameters=[{'config_file': bridge_yaml}]))
        say('bridge: ' + ', '.join(f'{e["gz_topic_name"]} -> {e["ros_topic_name"]}' for e in entries))
        if not standin_model:
            actions.append(Node(package='sim_bringup', executable='odom_tf', name='odom_tf', output='screen'))

    # ---- 10. demo nodes (sim_demo) --------------------------------------------------------------
    # sim_demo's own launch file knows its nodes' parameters: include it (panel, markers, truth_detector,
    # score_run). Only when that file is missing are the nodes started one by one with the basics.
    photo_dir = sp.team_photo_dir(cfg['photo_dir'])
    gui_env = _gui_env()
    demo_launch = os.path.join(shares['sim_demo'] or '', 'launch', 'demo_nodes.launch.py')
    if shares['sim_demo'] and os.path.isfile(demo_launch):
        demo_args = {
            'world': world_cfg.name, 'detector': demo_detector, 'panel': str(sp.truthy(cfg['panel'])).lower(),
            'markers': str(sp.truthy(cfg['markers'])).lower(), 'score': str(sp.truthy(cfg['score'])).lower(),
            'photo_dir': cfg['photo_dir'], 'run_dir': sp.expand(cfg['demo_run_dir']),
            'mavlink_url': f'udpin:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}', 'auto_start': str(sp.truthy(cfg['auto_start'])).lower(),
            'frame_id': 'world', 'worlds_dir': world_cfg.worlds_dir,
        }
        actions.append(IncludeLaunchDescription(PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(demo_launch),
                                                launch_arguments=demo_args.items()))
        parts = [n for n, on in (('panel', sp.truthy(cfg['panel'])), ('markers', sp.truthy(cfg['markers'])),
                                 ('truth_detector', detector == 'truth'), ('score_run', sp.truthy(cfg['score'])))
                 if on]
        say(f'sim_demo: {", ".join(parts) or "nothing"} (sim_demo/launch/demo_nodes.launch.py)')
    elif shares['sim_demo']:
        basic = {'world': world_cfg.name, 'photo_dir': cfg['photo_dir'], 'detector': demo_detector}
        for exe, on in (('demo_markers', sp.truthy(cfg['markers'])), ('truth_detector', detector == 'truth'),
                        ('demo_panel', sp.truthy(cfg['panel'])), ('score_run', sp.truthy(cfg['score']))):
            if on and executable_or_none('sim_demo', exe):
                extra = dict(basic, run_dir=sp.expand(cfg['demo_run_dir'])) if exe == 'score_run' else dict(basic)
                if exe == 'demo_panel':
                    extra['mavlink_url'] = f'udpin:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}'
                actions.append(Node(package='sim_demo', executable=exe, name=exe, output='screen',
                                    parameters=[extra], additional_env=gui_env))
    if detector == 'truth':
        say('detector:=truth -> sim_demo truth_detector publishes /image_detection (the panel says so)')
    elif detector == 'custom':
        say('detector:=custom -> a teammate\'s detector publishes /image_detection (started with the team stack: '
            'team_stack.launch.py detector:=custom profile:=...)')
    say(f'team photo folder (the panel shows the newest photo): {photo_dir}')

    # ---- 10a. the camera picture for Mission Planner (MJPEG over HTTP, this computer only) ---------------
    if sp.truthy(cfg['pov_server']) and shares['sim_demo'] and executable_or_none('sim_demo', 'pov_server'):
        actions.append(Node(package='sim_demo', executable='pov_server', name='pov_server', output='screen',
                            parameters=[{'port': int(cfg['pov_port']), 'topic': '/sim/camera/image'}]))
        say(f'camera feed for Mission Planner: http://127.0.0.1:{cfg["pov_port"]}/pov.mjpg '
            f'(HUD right-click > Video > Set MJPEG Source)')

    # ---- 10b. plug-in profile: custom camera + extras that start with the simulator ----------------
    if profile_rp is not None:
        for role, entry in plug_plan.sim_side_entries(profile_rp):
            actions.extend(launch_support.entry_actions(entry, role, tag='sim'))

    # ---- 11. RViz + Gazebo follow camera ---------------------------------------------------------
    if sp.truthy(cfg['rviz']):
        rviz_cfg = os.path.join(shares['sim_bringup'] or '', 'rviz', 'sim.rviz')
        actions.append(Node(package='rviz2', executable='rviz2', name='rviz2', output='log',
                            arguments=['-d', rviz_cfg] if os.path.isfile(rviz_cfg) else [],
                            additional_env=gui_env))
    if gui and sp.truthy(cfg['follow']):
        follower = executable_or_none('sim_bringup', 'gz_follow')
        try:
            offset = [str(float(v)) for v in cfg['follow_offset'].split(',')]
            assert len(offset) == 3
        except (ValueError, AssertionError):
            say(f'follow_offset "{cfg["follow_offset"]}" is not "x,y,z"; using -12,0,6')
            offset = ['-12', '0', '6']
        if follower:
            actions.append(ExecuteProcess(cmd=[follower, '--entity', sp.DRONE_ENTITY, '--offset', *offset],
                                          name='gz_follow', output='screen'))

    # ---- 12. remember what was started (for status.sh, demo.sh and the scripts) -----------------
    _write_state(state_home, {
        'session': os.environ.get('ASTRA_SIM_SESSION', ''), 'started': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'),
        'world': world_cfg.name, 'world_name': world_name, 'world_file': world_cfg.world_file,
        'home': world_cfg.home, 'spawn': spawn, 'mission': world_cfg.mission, 'truth': world_cfg.truth,
        'worlds_dir': world_cfg.worlds_dir,
        'standin_world': world_cfg.standin, 'standin_model': standin_model, 'model_file': model_file,
        'camera_model': camera, 'detector': detector, 'sitl_instance': instance, 'ports': ports,
        'gcs_port': gcs_port, 'mavros_port': mavros_port, 'panel_port': panel_port, 'windows_gcs': win_out,
        'camera_ip': camera_ip,
        'sitl_run_dir': str(run_dir), 'photo_dir': photo_dir,
        'autopilot': 'external' if external else 'sitl', 'sitl_bin': sitl_used,
        'profile': profile_rp.source if profile_rp is not None else '',
        'gz_partition': os.environ.get('GZ_PARTITION', ''), 'ros_domain_id': os.environ.get('ROS_DOMAIN_ID', '0'),
    }, actions)
    return actions
nodes.explain: The heart of the launch file, run once when the launch starts. It reads every argument (and an optional plug-in profile), checks the numbers, picks the world (sim_paths.load_world_config, or the ardupilot_gazebo stand-in), refuses to start when SITL's ports 9002+10I / 5760+10I are already taken, and makes the drone SDF with xacro. Then it builds, in order, the list of programs and nodes to start (see effects), and last it writes state/current_launch.yaml.
nodes.called_when: by the OpaqueFunction that generate_launch_description adds, after the launch arguments are known
nodes.inputs: the launch context (resolved arguments)
nodes.outputs: the list of launch actions (processes, nodes, log lines, environment settings)
nodes.effects: starts the gz sim server (its exit stops everything) and window (plus any gui_env NAME=value extras for that window only), the spawn of entity 'iris', SITL (waits for UDP 9002+10I), MAVProxy (waits for TCP 5760+10I), siyi_emulator (camera_model, camera_ip, SD card ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<I>), payload_release, parameter_bridge + odom_tf, sim_demo's demo_nodes.launch.py, pov_server (port 8081), RViz and gz_follow; writes ~/.astra_sim/generated/ (drone SDF, bridge_I<I>.yaml) and ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml; may emit Shutdown on a fatal error

nodes.label: add_mavproxy
nodes.doc: Step 7: MAVProxy and its outputs. waiter_prefix = the wait_then_exec words ([] = start at once).
nodes.source:
def add_mavproxy(waiter_prefix):
        """Step 7: MAVProxy and its outputs. waiter_prefix = the wait_then_exec words ([] = start at once)."""
        nonlocal win_out
        mavproxy = sp.find_mavproxy(cfg['mavproxy_bin'])
        if not mavproxy:
            say('MAVProxy not found (~/sitl/venv/bin/mavproxy.py or mavproxy.py on PATH): '
                f'connect a ground station to TCP 127.0.0.1:{ports["serial0"]} yourself')
            return
        # Mission Planner / QGroundControl on WINDOWS cannot hear the 127.0.0.1 outputs (in WSL2's
        # NAT networking Ubuntu is a separate computer behind Windows): give them their own copy,
        # sent to the Windows host. The 127.0.0.1:gcs_port output our scripts use is unchanged.
        win_out, win_notes = sp.windows_gcs_output(cfg['windows_gcs'], cfg['windows_gcs_addr'],
                                                   local_ports=(gcs_port, mavros_port, panel_port))
        for n in win_notes:
            say(n)
        # Plug-and-play outputs (Docker / two computers); all default to today's 127.0.0.1 ports.
        master = cfg['mavlink_master'].strip() or f'tcp:127.0.0.1:{ports["serial0"]}'
        gcs_out = cfg['gcs_out'].strip() or f'udp:127.0.0.1:{gcs_port}'
        mavros_out = cfg['mavros_out'].strip() or f'udp:127.0.0.1:{mavros_port}'
        extra_outs = [o.strip() for o in cfg['extra_outs'].split(',') if o.strip()]
        master_args = plug_ap.mavproxy_master_args(master, external) if plug_ap else ['--master', master]
        mp_cmd = [mavproxy, *master_args,
                  '--out', gcs_out, '--out', mavros_out,
                  '--out', f'udp:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}', *[w for o in extra_outs for w in ('--out', o)],
                  *(['--out', win_out] if win_out else []),
                  '--daemon', '--state-basedir', str(run_dir), '--logfile', 'mav.tlog']
        run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        actions.append(ExecuteProcess(
            cmd=[*waiter_prefix, *mp_cmd],
            cwd=str(run_dir), name='mavproxy', output='screen', sigterm_timeout='5', sigkill_timeout='3'))
        say(f'MAVProxy outputs: ground station {gcs_out}, MAVROS {mavros_out} '
            f'(fcu_url udp://:{mavros_port}@localhost:{mavros_port}), demo panel udp:127.0.0.1:{panel_port}'
            + ''.join(f', extra {o}' for o in extra_outs)
            + (f', Windows ground station {win_out}' if win_out else '')
            + (f'; MAVLink from {master}' if cfg['mavlink_master'].strip() else ''))
nodes.explain: Step 7: adds MAVProxy, the program that copies the autopilot's MAVLink to several listeners. It finds mavproxy.py, asks sim_paths.windows_gcs_output for the extra Windows copy, and builds the command: --master tcp:127.0.0.1:5760+10I, --out udp:127.0.0.1:14550 (scripts / ground station), --out udp:127.0.0.1:14552 (MAVROS), --out udp:127.0.0.1:14553 (demo panel), any extra outputs, the Windows output, --daemon, state folder ~/.astra_sim/sitl_I<I> and log mav.tlog. The command is started behind the given wait_then_exec words.
nodes.inputs: waiter_prefix: the wait_then_exec words (empty = start at once)
nodes.effects: adds the 'mavproxy' process; logs the chosen outputs; if MAVProxy is missing it only prints how to connect to TCP 5760 directly

nodes.label: generate_launch_description
nodes.doc: Entry point used by `ros2 launch`.
nodes.source:
def generate_launch_description():
    """Entry point used by `ros2 launch`."""
    decls = [DeclareLaunchArgument(name, default_value=default, description=desc)
             for name, default, desc in ARGUMENTS]
    # Every process started below inherits this tag; stop_sim.sh uses it to stop exactly this simulator.
    session = [] if os.environ.get('ASTRA_SIM_SESSION') else [
        SetEnvironmentVariable('ASTRA_SIM_SESSION', f'launch-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}')]
    # Keep Gazebo's messages in their own "partition" so other Gazebo programs on this PC do not mix in.
    partition = [] if os.environ.get('GZ_PARTITION') else [SetEnvironmentVariable('GZ_PARTITION', 'astra_sim')]
    # Qt windows (Gazebo, RViz, demo panel) work best on X11 inside WSL2 (see _gui_env).
    qt = [SetEnvironmentVariable('QT_QPA_PLATFORM', 'xcb')] if (_running_in_wsl() and
                                                                 not os.environ.get('QT_QPA_PLATFORM')) else []
    return LaunchDescription(decls + session + partition + qt + [OpaqueFunction(function=_launch_setup)])
nodes.explain: The function 'ros2 launch' calls. It declares every launch argument from the ARGUMENTS table with its default and help text. When they are not already set, it gives all started programs a session tag ASTRA_SIM_SESSION=launch-<12 hex> (stop_sim.sh uses it), sets GZ_PARTITION=astra_sim so other Gazebo programs do not mix in, and sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb inside WSL. Finally it adds _launch_setup to build everything else.
nodes.called_when: ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py (from start_sim.sh / demo.sh)

nodes.label: demo.sh
nodes.doc:
=============================================================================
demo.sh  --  THE FULL SEARCH DEMO, one command

PURPOSE: shows the whole search-and-deliver mission in the simulator, flown by the team's REAL code:
1. starts the simulator WITH its windows: Gazebo (3D view following the drone + a live camera POV
panel), RViz (camera POV + markers) and the demo panel (live POV, newest photo with detection boxes,
detection list with class / confidence / lat-lon, mission phase); sim_demo's score_run records the run;
2. waits until ArduCopter SITL has GPS and a settled EKF (the first ~30 s "Arm: Gyros inconsistent" is
normal), then uploads the world's survey mission (like Mission Planner);
3. starts the team's real flight stack exactly as on the drone: ./launcher.sh sim (MAVROS + video_cam +
new_od detection + DigiCamCtrl trigger + waypoint_manager + main_controller), from the Linux-side repo
copy, and waits until it is ready (MAVROS connected, mission read, detector model loaded);
4. arms and starts the mission (AUTO): take-off, search lanes over the hiker (mannequin) and the tent with
a photo every second, detections, main_controller inserts the target waypoints, the drone flies to each
target and the payloads fall in Gazebo, then it returns home (RTL) and lands;
5. prints every phase in this terminal as it happens (phase_monitor), and
6. at the end (landed, or Ctrl+C) makes sure the score report is written (detections vs the ground truth,
drop errors), copies the photos into the run folder and stops everything cleanly.
Everything of one run is in ~/.astra_sim/runs/<date>_<world>/ (logs, phases, photos, score_report.md).

HOW TO RUN:   bash demo.sh                          -> runway world (small and quick, about 6-8 minutes)
bash demo.sh suas_field                -> the SUAS 2026 field (longer)
bash demo.sh runway --detector truth   -> answer-key detector stand-in instead of the team model
bash demo.sh runway --camera a8mini    -> A8 mini profile, 4K photos
Options:      --detector real|truth   who finds the targets (default real = the team's new_od + yolo26m)
--camera zr10|a8mini    photo profile (default zr10 = 2K photos, last year's camera default)
--zoom survey|team      survey (default): photos keep the full 81 deg view the mission was
planned for; team: let video_cam's 5x zoom rack shrink the photos
--headless              no windows (for tests and servers)
--panel                 also open the old ASTRA demo panel (the Qt window). It is OFF by default:
Mission Planner is the ground station (the camera picture is at
http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg, see docs/simulation/MISSION_PLANNER.md)
--no-panel              (the default) do not open the ASTRA demo panel
--no-windows-gcs        no MAVLink copy for Mission Planner / QGroundControl on Windows (by default,
inside WSL, it goes to the Windows host: Mission Planner -> UDP -> port 14550)
--windows-gcs HOST[:PORT]  send that copy somewhere else (another laptop, mirrored networking)
--timeout MINUTES       give up after this long (default 30)
--keep                  leave everything running after the landing
--manual                MISSION PLANNER MODE (fly it like at the competition): start everything
(simulator, windows, team stack, the MAVLink copy for Mission Planner) and
then WAIT: nothing is uploaded, armed or started automatically. You do it
in Mission Planner (the steps are printed). Stays open like --keep.
--dry-run               check everything and print the plan, start nothing
Run it again: START OVER in the demo panel (click twice), or bash start_over.sh [--fly] (see start_over.sh).
Advanced:     --mission FILE (fly another .waypoints mission), --sitl-instance N, --gcs-port P,
--mavros-port P, --panel-port P (run beside another simulator), --launch-arg name:=value
(repeatable, passed to sim.launch.py). World "standin" = ardupilot_gazebo's runway, no targets
(needs --mission; for testing the chain when sim_worlds is not built).
Plug and play (swap one piece for your own; docs/simulation/PLUGINS.md and ARDUPILOT.md):
--profile NAME|FILE     a plug-in profile (simulation/profiles/NAME.yaml or your own file): which
detector, mission brain, autopilot, camera, world and extras to use
--set KEY=VALUE         change one profile setting (repeatable), e.g. --set camera.strict=true
--detector custom       your detector (needs a profile with detector.custom)
--sitl-version V        ArduCopter V from setup/fetch_sitl.sh (e.g. 4.7.1, latest)
--sitl-source DIR       ArduCopter built in an ArduPilot source tree (e.g. /opt/ardupilot)
--sitl-bin FILE         any arducopter program
--param-file FILE       extra parameters after the simulator's own (e.g. the real drone's .param;
hardware lines are filtered out), repeatable
--autopilot external --mavlink ADDR   an autopilot running elsewhere (another container / PC)
--mavros-out ADDR, --extra-out ADDR, --camera-bind IP, --fcu-url URL, --team-stack external
network endpoints for Docker / two computers
Options typed here win over the profile; --dry-run prints the profile's full plan.
Without any of these, demo.sh runs exactly as it always did (no profile is read).
Stop early:   Ctrl+C here (the score report is still written).
=============================================================================
nodes.explain: THE full search demo in one command. It checks that everything is built, starts the simulator with its windows, waits until ArduCopter SITL is ready, uploads the world's survey mission, starts the team's real flight stack (./launcher.sh sim), arms and starts the mission (AUTO), prints every mission phase as it happens, and at the end makes sure the score report is written, copies the photos into the run folder and stops everything.
nodes.how_it_fits: The conductor of the whole twin. Step 1 starts sim.launch.py (Gazebo, SITL, MAVProxy, camera emulator, score_run); steps 2 and 5 use mission_tool over MAVLink on udpin:127.0.0.1:14550; step 3 starts launcher.sh with TRACKER_CMD='ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py detector:=...' and, on disk on 2026-10-31, FCU_URL tcp://127.0.0.1:5763 (+10 per SITL instance), i.e. MAVROS on SITL's spare port SERIAL2 like the real Jetson on the Pixhawk's TELEM2 (before that it went through MAVProxy's UDP 14552); stack_check and phase_monitor watch over ROS 2. Each run gets ~/.astra_sim/runs/<time>_<world>/ (demo.env, sim.log, team_stack.log, phases.jsonl, photos/, score_report.md). --profile/--set ask sim_plugins.profile_tool for the plan; --manual leaves upload, arm and start to Mission Planner. START OVER (start_over.sh / run_reset.py) can take over a running demo. Start Search Demo.bat and Start for Mission Planner.bat call it.

nodes.label: problem
nodes.source: problem() { warn "$*"; PROBLEMS=$((PROBLEMS + 1)); }
nodes.explain: Prints a warning and adds 1 to the PROBLEMS counter. demo.sh runs ALL its checks first and stops only afterwards (when the counter is above 0), so you see every problem at once instead of one per try.

nodes.label: port_busy
nodes.source: port_busy() { printf '%s\n' "$UDP_NOW" | grep -qE "[:.]$1\b"; }
nodes.explain: Answers whether a UDP port is already taken, by searching the list of listening UDP sockets that 'ss -lunH' printed once before the checks. demo.sh uses it to refuse to start when the ground-station port (14550) or the MAVROS port (14552) is busy, for example because a ground station or an old MAVROS still runs.
nodes.inputs: a port number

nodes.label: stop_group
nodes.source:
stop_group() {   # stop_group PGID NAME : Ctrl+C to a whole process group, then wait (up to 20 s)
  local pg="$1" name="$2"
  [ -n "$pg" ] || return 0
  kill -0 -- "-$pg" 2>/dev/null || return 0
  info "stopping the $name ..."
  kill -INT -- "-$pg" 2>/dev/null
  for _ in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 -- "-$pg" 2>/dev/null || return 0; sleep 1; done
  kill -TERM -- "-$pg" 2>/dev/null; sleep 3
  kill -KILL -- "-$pg" 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
nodes.explain: Stops a whole process group (the simulator launch, or the team stack) politely: first Ctrl+C (SIGINT) to the group, then it waits up to 20 seconds, then SIGTERM, 3 more seconds, then SIGKILL.
nodes.called_when: finish (normal end), and before the second try of the team stack
nodes.inputs: the process group id and a name for the message

nodes.label: finish
nodes.source:
finish() {   # write the score, collect the photos, stop everything (called once)
  [ "$FINISHED" = 1 ] && return
  FINISHED=1
  trap - INT TERM
  # START OVER owns the old run's collection and the new recorder now. A late finish here could ask
  # the NEW score_run to write an unfinished report, or copy NEW photos into the old run folder.
  if taken_over; then
    info "START OVER owns this simulator now; its run recorder collects the results."
    return
  fi
  [ -n "$MON_PID" ] && kill -INT "$MON_PID" 2>/dev/null
  say "Finishing the demo"
  if [ ! -s "$RUN_DIR/score_report.md" ] && [ -n "$SIM_PG" ] && kill -0 -- "-$SIM_PG" 2>/dev/null; then
    info "asking score_run to write the score report ..."
    timeout 25 ros2 service call /sim/demo/write_score std_srvs/srv/Trigger "{}" > "$RUN_DIR/write_score.log" 2>&1 || true
  fi
  if compgen -G "$PHOTO_DIR/*" > /dev/null; then
    mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/photos"
    cp -p "$PHOTO_DIR"/* "$RUN_DIR/photos/" 2>/dev/null
    DET_DIR="$(dirname "$PHOTO_DIR")/detection_results_sahi"
    if compgen -G "$DET_DIR/*" > /dev/null; then mkdir -p "$RUN_DIR/detections"; cp -p "$DET_DIR"/* "$RUN_DIR/detections/" 2>/dev/null; fi
    info "photos copied to $RUN_DIR/photos ($(find "$RUN_DIR/photos" -type f | wc -l) files)"
  fi
  echo
  if [ -s "$RUN_DIR/score_report.md" ]; then
    say "SCORE REPORT ($RUN_DIR/score_report.md)"
    head -40 "$RUN_DIR/score_report.md" | sed 's/^/    /'
  else
    warn "no score report was written yet (it is written when the simulator stops; see $RUN_DIR/sim.log)"
  fi
  # START OVER (start_over.sh / the panel's button) has taken this simulator over: never close it from here.
  if [ "$(cat "$ASTRA_STATE_DIR/keep_open" 2>/dev/null)" = "$ASTRA_SIM_SESSION" ] && [ "$INTERRUPTED" = 0 ]; then
    KEEP=1
  fi
  if [ "$KEEP" = 1 ] && [ "$INTERRUPTED" = 0 ]; then
    ok "--keep: everything keeps running. Stop it later with:  bash $ASTRA_SCRIPTS_DIR/stop_sim.sh"
    if [ "$MANUAL" = 1 ]; then
      info "another run: START OVER in the demo panel (click twice) or  bash $ASTRA_SCRIPTS_DIR/start_over.sh ;" \
           "then do the Mission Planner steps 2-5 again (Load File, Write, Arm, Auto)"
    else
      info "fly it again: START OVER in the demo panel (click twice), or  bash $ASTRA_SCRIPTS_DIR/start_over.sh --fly"
    fi
  else
    if [ "$INTERRUPTED" = 0 ] && [ "$HEADLESS" = 0 ] && [ -t 0 ]; then
      # Give the audience a moment to look at the panel, the markers and the payloads on the ground.
      read -r -t 120 -p "    The windows stay open so you can look around. Press Enter to close everything (auto-close in 2 min) " _ || true
      echo
    fi
    if [ "$(cat "$ASTRA_STATE_DIR/keep_open" 2>/dev/null)" = "$ASTRA_SIM_SESSION" ] && [ "$INTERRUPTED" = 0 ]; then
      ok "START OVER took this simulator over meanwhile: it stays open (stop it with: bash $ASTRA_SCRIPTS_DIR/stop_sim.sh)"
      say "Everything from this run is in $RUN_DIR"
      return
    fi
    stop_group "$TEAM_PG" "team flight stack (launcher.sh)"
    stop_group "$SIM_PG" "simulator"
    bash "$ASTRA_SCRIPTS_DIR/stop_sim.sh" --quiet --session "$ASTRA_SIM_SESSION" || true
    [ -s "$RUN_DIR/score_report.md" ] && info "score report: $RUN_DIR/score_report.md"
  fi
  say "Everything from this run is in $RUN_DIR"
}
nodes.explain: Ends the demo, only once. If START OVER has taken this simulator over it only says so and leaves everything running. Otherwise it stops the phase monitor, asks score_run to write the report now when it is still missing (ROS service /sim/demo/write_score, std_srvs/srv/Trigger), copies the photos and detection images into the run folder, prints the first 40 lines of score_report.md, and then either keeps everything running (--keep, --manual, or when START OVER took over meanwhile) or stops the team stack, the simulator and any leftovers (stop_sim.sh --session); with windows and a terminal it first waits up to 2 minutes for Enter so people can look around.
nodes.called_when: after the landing, after a failed step, or on Ctrl+C (through on_interrupt)
nodes.effects: one ROS service call; files copied to <run>/photos and <run>/detections; may stop the simulator's processes

nodes.label: on_interrupt
nodes.source: on_interrupt() { INTERRUPTED=1; echo; warn "Ctrl+C: stopping the demo (the score report is still written)"; finish; exit 130; }
nodes.explain: What Ctrl+C (or SIGTERM) does in demo.sh: it marks the run as interrupted, says that the score report is still written, runs finish and exits with code 130.

nodes.label: astra_gcs.cs
nodes.doc:
simulation/windows/mission_planner_plugin/astra_gcs.cs -- PURPOSE: make Mission Planner the ONE ground-station
screen of the ASTRA search mission. It replaces the old "ASTRA Simulation" demo panel. Mission Planner compiles this
file by itself when it starts (it is a Mission Planner plugin: a C# file in Mission Planner's "plugins" folder; the
installer simulation/windows/install_mp_plugin.ps1, or mission_planner.sh start, puts it there).

What it adds to Mission Planner:
  1. THE DRONE CAMERA IN THE HUD, with no clicks. When the camera stream answers (the simulator serves it at
     http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg, see sim_demo/pov_server.py), the HUD background becomes the live camera picture;
     when the stream goes away the normal artificial horizon comes back. HUD right-click > "ASTRA camera" turns it
     on or off and changes the address.
  2. AN "ASTRA" TAB on the DATA screen (it opens by default), the job the old panel did:
       - the mission phase strip: Waiting > Take-off > Search > Process > Targets > Drop > Return > Landed,
       - one plain sentence about what the drone is doing right now,
       - big readouts: flight mode, height, speed, battery, GPS, distance home, time in the air, waypoint,
       - one card each for the HIKER and the TENT: detections, the target position chosen, the payload drop,
       - an event log (the autopilot's and the team code's messages), warnings in amber,
       - buttons: ARM + START MISSION and RETURN HOME (RTL), each with a confirmation box; in the simulator also
         TAKE PHOTO, CAMERA DOWN, CAMERA FORWARD and START OVER (run through WSL by simulation/scripts/mp_actions.sh).
  3. MAP MARKERS for the chosen targets (from the team's "Aim ..." messages) and for the drop points.

Where the information comes from: ONLY what Mission Planner already receives over MAVLink, so it works the same with
the real drone over the telemetry radio. The team's flight code (main_controller.py) sends status texts such as
"Detected tent", "All 97 images processed. Selecting targets.", "Aim tent 36.2149350,-96.0069430",
"Targets: tent@11 -> person@12. Diverting.", "Over tent: loiter 6s then drop" and "Servo 13 -> 1400"; the optional
Jetson reporter (lattice_bridge) adds "TGT p 36.214935 -96.006203 95 12"; the autopilot supplies the flight mode,
arming, height, speed, battery and GPS. Only the camera picture and the simulator buttons use something else (the
camera stream, and WSL).

Safety: it never changes the flight by itself. The two flight buttons ask "are you sure" first and then do exactly
what Mission Planner's own buttons do (set GUIDED, arm, set AUTO / set RTL). Every part catches its own errors: a
problem here shows up as a line in the event log and in the status file, never as a crash of Mission Planner.

Observability: every 2 s it writes Documents\Mission Planner\astra_plugin_status.json (phase, camera pictures, what
it has seen), so scripts and teammates can check it works without looking at the screen.

Settings (Mission Planner's config.xml, changed through the HUD menu or by hand while Mission Planner is closed):
  astra_camera_on       "true"/"false"   show the camera in the HUD (default true)
  astra_camera_url      MJPEG address    default http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg
  astra_sim_buttons     auto|on|off      simulator buttons: auto = only when connected to the simulator (SITL)
  astra_wsl_distro      WSL distribution for the simulator buttons (default Ubuntu-22.04)
  astra_wsl_repo        the repository copy inside WSL (default ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026)
  astra_drop_channels   servo channel -> payload, default "11:person,13:tent";  astra_drop_open_pwm default 1400

Two technical notes for whoever changes this file:
  - Mission Planner ships its OWN copy of most System.Drawing types (MissionPlanner.Drawing, built on SkiaSharp),
    next to .NET's. Naming Font, Pen, Brush, Bitmap or Image in this file would therefore be ambiguous. So it never
    names them: fonts are made by reflection (Ui.SetFont), the phase strip is plain labels, and camera pictures are
    decoded with .NET's Image.FromStream found through Form.BackgroundImage (the type the HUD's bgimage expects).
    Color is safe (it exists only once).
  - Plain C# 5, so both Mission Planner's compiler and the old .NET Framework compiler accept it. Check it with
    simulation/windows/check_mp_plugin.ps1 before installing.
Written for Mission Planner 1.3.83 (FlightData.myhud, CurrentState, MAVLinkInterface, PluginHost).
nodes.explain: Makes Mission Planner the ONE ground-station screen of the ASTRA search mission.
