It adds (1) the drone camera as the HUD background (an MJPEG stream, default http://127.0.0.1:8081/pov.mjpg from sim_demo's pov_server); (2) an 'ASTRA' tab on the DATA screen with the mission phase strip, one plain sentence about what the drone is doing, 8 readouts, a card each for the hiker and the tent, an event log and buttons (ARM + START MISSION, RETURN HOME, and in the simulator TAKE PHOTO, CAMERA DOWN, CAMERA FORWARD, START OVER); and (3) map markers for the chosen targets and the drop points. Every 2 s it writes Documents\Mission Planner\astra_plugin_status.json.
nodes.how_it_fits: It learns everything from what Mission Planner already receives over MAVLink: the autopilot's state, and the STATUSTEXT messages the team's main_controller sends through MAVROS ('Detected tent', 'All N images processed', 'Aim tent <lat>,<lon>', 'Targets: ...', 'Over tent:', 'Servo 13 -> 1400', 'RTL'), plus the optional lattice_reporter's 'TGT p <lat> <lon> <conf> <n>' texts, so it works the same with the real drone over the telemetry radio. Only the camera picture (HTTP) and the simulator buttons (wsl.exe running simulation/scripts/mp_actions.sh) use something else. The flight buttons ask first and then do what Mission Planner's own buttons do (GUIDED, arm, AUTO; or RTL). Settings live in Mission Planner's config.xml (astra_camera_on, astra_camera_url, astra_sim_buttons, astra_wsl_distro, astra_wsl_repo, astra_drop_channels '11:person,13:tent', astra_drop_open_pwm 1400). Written for Mission Planner 1.3.83 in plain C# 5; check it with check_mp_plugin.ps1, install it with install_mp_plugin.ps1.

nodes.label: AstraPlugin
nodes.explain: The plugin itself, a Mission Planner 'Plugin'. It keeps the mission state (phase, targets, events) on Mission Planner's plugin thread, reads the camera stream on its own thread, and changes the ASTRA tab only on the window thread.

nodes.label: Init
nodes.explain: Called once when Mission Planner loads the plugin: asks Mission Planner to call Loop 2 times per second (loopratehz = 2) and creates the two empty target records 'person' and 'tent'.

nodes.label: Loaded
nodes.explain: Called when Mission Planner's screens exist: builds the ASTRA tab, adds the 'ASTRA camera' HUD menu and the map layer, subscribes to every STATUSTEXT packet from any system and component, logs 'plugin loaded', starts the camera thread and writes the first status file. Every part catches its own errors (kept in lastError), so one failure never stops the others or Mission Planner.

nodes.label: Loop
nodes.explain: Called by Mission Planner 2 times per second: runs Tick and catches any error.

nodes.label: Exit
nodes.explain: Called when Mission Planner closes: tells the camera thread to stop, removes the STATUSTEXT subscription and clears the camera picture from the HUD.

nodes.label: OnStatusText
nodes.explain: Runs on Mission Planner's MAVLink reader thread for every STATUSTEXT packet. It skips the autopilot's own texts (component 1; ReadMessages gets those), decodes the text and queues it with its 'sysid:compid' source, keeping at most 500 waiting. It stays fast: the parsing happens later in Tick.
nodes.inputs: one MAVLink message

nodes.label: Tick
nodes.explain: The update that runs 2 times per second. It reads new autopilot and companion status texts, decides whether this is the simulator, notices arming (a new flight starts; after Landed the facts are reset) and disarming, and works out the phase: not armed = Waiting or Landed; RTL, LAND, SMART_RTL or a return message = Return; a drop under way or done = Drop; targets chosen = Targets; search done or photos processed = Process; AUTO above 10 m at waypoint 2 or later = Search; otherwise Takeoff. During a flight the phase never steps back. Then it writes the status file every 2 s and asks the window thread to redraw.

nodes.label: HandleText
nodes.signature: private void HandleText(DateTime time, byte compid, string text, MAVLinkInterface com)
nodes.explain: Turns one status text from the autopilot or the team's code into mission facts, by matching it against a few fixed patterns (listed under 'effects'). Texts with words like FAILED, timeout or PreArm are logged as warnings, and every text goes into the event log.
nodes.inputs: time, component id, text
nodes.effects: 'Detected person|tent' counts a detection; 'TGT p|t <lat> <lon> <conf> <n>' keeps the best radio report; 'All N images processed' or 'Reached last WP' = search done; 'Aim person|tent <lat>,<lon>' = target position and map marker; 'Targets:' = targets chosen; 'Over person|tent:' = dropping; 'Servo <channel> -> <pwm>' = payload released when the channel is in astra_drop_channels and pwm equals the open value (1400), with the drone's position as the drop point; 'RTL', 'All targets done', 'No valid targets' or 'Divert failed' = returning
